title: Securing Enterprise DevOps: Zero Trust Architecture in Cloud-Native and Microservices Environments
abstract: Abstract—Modern enterprise software engineering has undergone an architectural paradigm shift toward cloud-native architectures, containerized microservices, and high-velocity continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. Concurrently, legacy perimeter-based security models ('castle-and-moat') have proven entirely inadequate in distributed, multi-tenant cloud ecosystems where internal network boundaries are non-existent and lateral movement vectors abound. The integration of Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)—grounded in the foundational tenet of 'never trust, always verify'—into enterprise DevOps pipelines establishes an end-to-end security framework spanning code authoring, artifact signing, workload attestation, and runtime execution. However, embedding continuous, multi-dimensional verification into automated deployment pipelines introduces acute tensions between developer velocity, cryptographic verification latency, operational overhead, and distributed policy consistency. This paper provides an exshaustive, mathematically grounded technical investigation and architectural synthesis of Zero Trust DevOps (DevSecOps) across cloud-native environments. We formalize workload identity mechanics utilizing the SPIFFE/SPIRE cryptographic framework, model service-mesh-based mutual Transport Layer Security (mTLS) enforcement with sidecar and ambient proxies, and formalize Policy-as-Code (PaC) invariants under Open Policy Agent (OPA) gatekeepers. Furthermore, we implement an empirical enterprise testbed comprising 120 containerized microservices deployed across a production-grade Kubernetes cluster, subjected to automated adversarial red-team injection vectors (including supply-chain dependency poisoning, stolen credential replay, and kernel escape exploits). Our empirical findings demonstrate that an optimized Zero Trust posture reduces lateral attack propagation by 96.4% and halts software supply-chain compromises at the CI boundary with an operational latency penalty of only 4.8% on end-to-end pipeline execution. Finally, we formulate open challenges in post-quantum cryptographic workload attestation, continuous behavioral policy synthesis, and automated zero-knowledge secretless pipelines. Index Terms—Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), Cloud-Native Systems, Microservices, DevSecOps, SPIFFE/SPIRE, Service Mesh, Policy-as-Code, Open Policy Agent (OPA), Supply Chain Security, eBPF Runtime Security.

title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
abstract: Abstract: We derive an improved upper bound on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability $\gamma$, given by $\log_2[1+(1-\gamma)\gamma^{\gamma/(1-\gamma)}]$. It applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement, and strictly improves the PLOB relative-entropy bound, the analytic max-relative-entropy bound, and the optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bound. At high damping, a known triple-rail protocol attains more than $99.54\%$ of its leading coefficient. Our method extends sector teleportation simulation to qubits: phase rotations and permutations give exact simulations within fixed-excitation subspaces while preserving the two-level input structure. We determine the exact, additive relative entropy of entanglement of the amplitude-damping resources and the exact regularized entanglement gain at fixed input population. We then derive explicit bounds for generalized amplitude damping, which includes thermal excitation. Combining the amplitude-damping gain with unital and entanglement-breaking channels gives a closed expression that recovers the zero-temperature result and vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region. It improves established benchmarks over broad parameter ranges, while the exact entanglement of the generalized resources remains open. Both results admit refinements under an average-excitation constraint. The bounds provide quantitative limits for adaptive communication through relaxing qubits and show how a sector simulation can remain useful beyond channels whose resource entanglement is known exactly.

title: Adaptive Knowledge Consolidation for Sequential Learning in Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Catastrophic forgetting is a major challenge in sequential deep learning, where learning new tasks can degrade previously acquired knowledge, particularly in evolving healthcare applications. Existing approaches mainly rely on replay, regularization, or architectural strategies, while the integration of adaptive, biologically inspired sleep mechanisms in conventional deep networks remains limited. To address this gap, this paper proposes a conceptual Adaptive Knowledge Consolidation (AKC) framework integrating wake-phase learning, NREM-inspired replay, REM-inspired knowledge integration, synaptic homeostasis, and adaptive sleep scheduling. The framework is designed for sequential image classification, with planned validation using Alzheimer?s disease-related brain MRI data. Evaluation will consider accuracy, forgetting measure, backward and forward transfer, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and AUROC. As implementation is ongoing, no numerical results are claimed. The study establishes the framework, mathematical formulation, and experimental protocol for future empirical validation.

title: Another look at universal one-to-one codes
abstract: For universal prefix codes, redundancy separates into a Θ(logn) predictor component and an O(1) coding component. Kosut and Sankar showed that dropping the prefix constraint cuts universal redundancy by logn—far more than the prefix code costs. We locate the origin of this gain by deterministic counting in Shtarkov’s single-transmission setting. The optimal universal one-to-one code ranks sequences by increasing empirical entropy, with redundancy exactly R1:1n = maxh[⌊log2 Bn(h)⌋−nh], with Bn(h) the number of sequences whose empirical entropy does not exceed h. Both code classes face the same object: the mass the maximized likelihood places on unit shells of empirical entropy. Prefix codes, bound by one Kraft budget, pay the logarithm of the total mass; one-to-one codes pay only that of the heaviest shell. For memoryless sources the mass spans Θ(n) shells, and the removed logn is the cost of aggregating the predictor’s regret across them—equivalently, of the level pointer that a self-delimiting codeword must carry and a transport-delimited ranking gets for free. The same formula yields finite-n bounds for all alphabet sizes and R1:1n = 1 bit for binary sources at all n.

title: Opening the Black Box of Classifier-Free Guidance via Information Bottleneck
abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is a standard technique for improving conditional generation in diffusion models, yet its activation schedule is usually selected heuristically. In practice, most existing CFG-based methods rely on a pre-defined activation policy throughout inference, while recent dynamic variants often depend on hand-designed schedules without a principled theoretical explanation of when conditional information is most useful. In order to understand how the informational relevance between conditioning inputs and the score function evolves over the course of generation, we explore when guidance should be activated from an information-theoretic perspective. In this work, we formulate the diffusion trajectory as a time-dependent information bottleneck and show that the effectiveness of conditional information is not uniform throughout sampling, but becomes significantly stronger after a critical stage characterized by a Fisher-information balance condition. Motivated by this insight, we propose a training-free dynamic CFG strategy for inference. Rather than prescribing a fixed schedule in advance, our method constructs a stochastic process from conditional and unconditional score statistics and activates guidance when the estimated guidance gain crosses a prescribed threshold. This yields an adaptive activation rule that aligns condition injection with the underlying generation dynamics, while also recovering interval-based guidance as a limiting special case. Extensive experiments across diverse architectures and tasks, demonstrate that our method is effective, robust, and broadly applicable. Beyond empirical improvements, our framework provides an interpretation of dynamic guidance methods and a principled foundation for inference-time control in conditional diffusion models.

title: Measurable Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting with Joint Region and Depth Supervision for Interactive Building Inspection
abstract: Image-based 3D reconstruction provides a scalable representation for building inspection and maintenance. However, photorealistic reconstruction alone does not fully provide the geometric measurability, semantic structure, and interactive information access required for engineering applications. This study proposes a measurable semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework with region and depth supervision for interactive building inspection from multi-view imagery. Mask-based region supervision suppresses irrelevant backgrounds and focuses optimization on target regions. Point-wise depth supervision guides Gaussian centers toward physical surfaces using reference geometry derived from multi-view stereo (MVS) point clouds, providing geometric anchors for measuring physical dimensions and areas. A semantic Gaussian field associates learnable class features with individual Gaussian primitives, enabling semantic rendering and component-level inspection. These capabilities are operationalized through AEC-SplatTwin, an interactive building inspection platform supporting real-time visualization, semantic analysis, quantitative measurement, and multimodal large language model (MLLM)-assisted interaction. On the synthetic UAV-inspection QuakeCity and smartphone-captured HKUPB datasets, the framework reduces Gaussian-center depth MAE by 58.1% and 86.8%, while its semantic field achieves mIoU values of 0.8529 and 0.8642. On HKUPB, the mean relative errors for height, width, and area measurements are 0.33%, 1.07%, and 0.60%. These results show that the proposed framework extends 3DGS beyond visual reconstruction into a measurable, semantically structured, and interactive engineering representation for building inspection.

title: linked-rolls
abstract: A TypeScript library for digital editions of piano rolls. It reads roll copies from scans and analysis files, collates them into versions, records editorial assumptions together with the beliefs behind them, exports the edition as JSON-LD in the Roll Edition Format, and plays a version through an emulated reproducing piano.

title: Podporna orodja za raziskovanje govorjene slovenščine
abstract: Članek predstavlja pet odprtokodnih orodij za obdelavo govornih posnetkov, raz­vitih za podporo raziskovanju govorjenega slovenskega jezika. Orodja pokrivajo različne vidike dela z govornimi jezikovnimi podatki in se med seboj dopolnjujejo. Prvo orodje omogoča vsiljeno poravnavo govora z besedilom s pomočjo orodij pro­gramske knjižnice Montreal Forced Aligner. Drugo orodje je namenjeno anonimi­zaciji zvočnih posnetkov, kjer sistem samodejno prepoznane ali ročno označene dele posnetkov z osebnimi podatki nadomesti z zvočnimi maskami. Tretje orodje služi validaciji govornih posnetkov in z grafičnim vmesnikom omogoča prever­janje ujemanja posnetka s transkripcijo. Četrto orodje je akustični normalizator, ki združuje različne metode za odstranjevanje šuma in izboljšanje kakovosti pos­netkov. Peto orodje pa je grafemsko-fonemski pretvornik, ki samodejno pretvarja besedila iz običajnega grafemskega zapisa v fonetično transkripcijo.

title: Integrity Diagnostics for Cross-Silo Federated Deepfake Speech Detection Under Heterogeneity and Poisoning
abstract: Cross-silo deepfake speech detection must accommodate organizations that observe different attack profiles and channel conditions while avoiding routine centralization of raw speech. We study federated learning (FL) for a compact detector combining linear-frequency cepstral coefficients (LFCCs) with frozen WavLM representations over heterogeneous partitions derived from ASVspoof 2019 and 2021. An official-metadata audit of the historical seed-42 Client-C split reproduces the reported 2,572/3,655 (70.37%) bona-fide source overlap; a stricter unified-source audit against the complete A+B+C fit pool finds still greater dependence. We therefore repeat the principal audio evaluation with five source-disjoint splits whose holdouts are independently verified against the complete fit pool. Mean equal error rate (EER) is 3.836% for pooled centralized training, 4.622% for Federated Averaging (FedAvg), 4.095% for local C, 21.883% for local A, and 33.398% for local B. On the common Client-C holdout, A-only and B-only models transfer poorly, while FedAvg is on average 0.787 percentage points worse than pooled training and 0.527 points worse than local C; these comparisons do not establish native-domain benefit for A or B. Separately, a 20-seed controlled stress test examines integrity mechanisms under malicious participation. Increasing untargeted label-flip compromise produces progressively more negative benign--malicious update alignment and stronger aggregate-step attenuation; the signature persists across four classifier topologies and FedProx settings. Additional tests cover targeted label poisoning, a controlled trigger backdoor, zero-update free riding, and coordinated sign-flip model poisoning. We frame the contribution as an auditable experimental protocol and a bounded set of observations, not as a new detector, optimizer, attack, aggregator, or universal defense.

title: Textless Speech-to-Speech Translation from Nepali to English Using Discrete Units: A Deep Learning Approach
abstract: This study implements direct speech to speech translation eliminating the conventional need for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Machine Translation (MT) by leveraging HuBERT for discrete unit extraction, a Transformer-based encoder-decoder for translation, and HiFi-GAN for speech reconstruction. Inspired by recent advances in unit-based S2ST, the model is trained on the multilingual FLEURS dataset for Nepali to English language translation. It achieved a BLEU score of 42.80, demonstrating both translation accuracy and natural-sounding speech synthesis. This work offers a scalable and effective solution for low-resource languages like Nepali.

title: A Study on the Impact of AI-Assisted Teaching Integration in College English on Students’ Writing Performance: A Case Study of Hubei Polytechnic University
abstract: At present, there are some problems in college English writing teaching, such as students ' low interest in writing, lack of personalized guidance, and low feedback efficiency. Artificial intelligence technology provides new ideas for teaching reform. In order to explore the actual impact of artificial intelligence-assisted teaching on college students’ English writing ability, this study selected two non-English major classes in Hubei Polytechnic University to carry out a one-semester quasi-experiment: 55 students in the experimental group adopted artificial intelligence-assisted teaching, and 53 students in the control group adopted traditional teaching. After the experiment, data were collected through questionnaires and in-depth interviews (10 students in each group), and the teaching effectiveness was evaluated by combining quantitative and qualitative results. The results showed that the average scores of each dimension of writing ability in the experimental class were higher than those in the control group, but did not reach a statistically significant level (P > 0.05). In the interview, the students in the experimental class had a significantly higher positive evaluation of writing interest (80%), learning effect (70%) and classroom interaction (90%). At the same time, they also put forward the problems of imperfect AI tools and easy to produce technical dependence. The control group feedback that the traditional teaching has the shortcomings of feedback lag and single form. In summary, although there is no significant statistical difference in the quantitative data, the mean value shows a positive trend of AI-assisted teaching, and the interview results also confirm that it can stimulate writing interest and improve learning experience. The teaching mode has application potential, and the teaching effect can be improved by prolonging the intervention cycle, optimizing the tools and strengthening the guidance of teachers.

title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion
abstract: Accurate detection of drivable area is essential for autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance systems. While state-of-the-art methods focus on general traversability estimation, they prove inadequate for snow-covered roads where following existing wheel tracks offers crucial advantages: improved traction, predictable vehicle dynamics, and verified path stability. To address this, we propose a low-cost, self-supervised approach detecting safety-critical wheel tracks using synchronized RGB-I (RGB + Long-Wave Infrared) imagery. Our method automatically generates training labels by projecting future wheel trajectories from recorded GNSS data. A neural network is designed to identify wheel tracks with the 4-channel RGB-I images from challenging, white-out road surfaces. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in visually monotonous and featureless adverse environment, offering a robust and cost-effective alternative for winter autonomy. The newly introduced ThermalTrack dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/thermaltrack/.

title: THE QUANTITY-TO-QUALITY PARADOX: How Language Models Turn Prediction into Intelligence
abstract: The large-language-model revolution demonstrates that quantitative scale alters the computational nature of a learning system:Scaled Data + Scaled Parameters + Scaled Optimization⇓Dense, Hierarchical Internal Representations⇓Invariant-Preserving Compositional Operators⇓Qualitatively Distinct Computational Regimes Prediction is an engine of algorithmic compression. A learning machine cannot predict a complex symbolic world without encoding the invariants that structure it. When that symbolic world contains physics, mathematics, algorithms, and logic, the internal representations mirror human reason.The central research question of artificial intelligence has moved beyond empirical benchmark fitting to the underlying science of representation:At what point does an internal representation cease to be a model of language and become an invariant model of reality?

title: Lost in the comments: Social context as a single‐pass jailbreak and defense on agentic platforms
abstract: Abstract As LLM‐based agents move onto multiagent platforms, they process direct prompts and surrounding social context—posts, comments, and upvotes—an attack surface that single‐turn alignment never addressed. We built a simulation of Moltbook, a social network for AI agents, and a pipeline turning 100 JailBreakBench goals into platform‐native posts with bystander comments of three valences: aggressive, ethical, and measured. Platform‐context reformatting alone raises the attack success rate (ASR) of GPT‐4o‐mini from 7% to 71%, beating a twenty‐query optimization baseline in one pass. Valence then acts as a bidirectional safety modulator: Ethical comments sharply suppress ASR, aggressive endorsements paradoxically reduce it by exposing intent, and measured, intellectually toned comments prove most dangerous, sustaining or elevating ASR. An ablation identifies valence rather than volume as key—a 35‐fold rise in upvotes leaves ASR unchanged—and every finding reproduces under an independent safety classifier with human adjudication. Ambiguous social context thus poses a greater threat than explicit pressure, while safety‐valenced signals offer a deployable defense for agentic platforms.

title: Analytical Hierarchy Process Approach in Expert Systems to Improve the Accuracy of Network Fault Detection
abstract: Computer networks play an important role in supporting information systems across sectors such as education, government, industry, and private organizations. The growing reliance on stable, reliable networks makes network disruptions a serious concern. Common issues such as internet disconnections, IP address conflicts, device failures to connect, and DNS errors often require a fast, accurate diagnosis. In practice, however, the handling of these problems is often limited by the number of available technicians and by users lack of technical understanding. This study aims to develop an expert system to automatically monitor and detect network faults. The system applies the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to assign weights to each symptom through pairwise comparisons, thereby prioritizing and yielding more relevant diagnostic results. The knowledge base was developed using secondary data from previous studies that utilized forward chaining. The system is implemented as a web-based application with a user-friendly interface. System evaluation was conducted using 50 network fault test cases, and the results showed that the proposed system achieved 92% accuracy, 91% precision, 90% recall, and an F1-score of 90.5% based on expert validation. In addition, the AHP consistency test produced a Consistency Ratio (CR) value of 0.08, indicating that the pairwise comparison matrix was logically consistent. These results demonstrate that the proposed system improves the efficiency and effectiveness of network fault diagnosis for both technical and non-technical users.

title: Design and performance analysis of a six-state QKD over FSO and optical fiber utilizing switch-controlled polarization generation for secure optical communications
abstract: Abstract Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a process that utilizes the principles of quantum mechanics to securely share a secret key between two parties, ensuring unconditional security. Diverse QKD protocols are established to guarantee the security and integrity of information against any attempts by an eavesdropper monitoring the transferred photons. One of these protocols is the six-state protocol. This work employs OptiSystem 21.1 simulation software to design and emulate the six-state protocol, wherein polarization states are produced through random switching control rather than optical modulators. The protocol’s performance, indicated by quantum bit error rate and secure key rate, is analytically examined for both free space optical (FSO) channel and optical fiber channel, incorporating parameters from two types of commercial single-photon detectors to enhance realism. The maximum secure key rate attains 5.439 Mbps at 10 km of optical fiber, in contrast to 1.674 Mbps at 0.2 km under clear weather conditions in the FSO quantum channel utilizing ID 281 single-photon detector modules across both channels. The maximum distance that guarantees secure key rate with ID 281 for FSO channel is 2 km with 1760 bps with heavy haze compared to 100 km optical fiber with secure key rate of 15,000 bps.

title: Factoring some integers using Shor’s algorithm on real quantum hardware
abstract: Abstract Experimental realizations of Shor’s algorithm on NISQ devices often rely on heavy circuit compilation, inadvertently encodingprior knowledge of the solution and bypassing the core challenge of quantum arithmetic. In this work, we present a transparent,hardware execution baseline for the quantum order-finding routine that maintains explicit modular exponentiation, but focusingon structured composite integers that simplify modular arithmetic. We mitigate the circuit depth by targeting moduli composedof Fermat primes, where the multiplication constants ck = A2kmod N simplify to either identities or powers of two, requiringonly simple bit-shift operations. We executed this explicit arithmetic approach on IBM superconducting hardware for N ∈{51, 85, 255, 771}. For moduli up to N = 255, we observed Hellinger fidelities up to 0.946. For N = 771, we quantitativelydemonstrate the signal degradation caused by increased circuit depth and accumulated hardware noise. By reporting raw anddevice-compiled gate counts alongside intermediate arithmetic validation, this methodology provides an experimental proxyfor studying circuit depth and noise in structured instances of order-finding, establishing a reproducible reference point forevaluating future hardware-aware optimizations.

title: Many Scores Force Many Reads: An Optimality Proof for Score of Parentheses
abstract: LeetCode Problem 856, Score of Parentheses, admits a one-pass algorithm using $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ auxiliary registers. Its correctness follows from a local interpretation: every occurrence of () contributes a power of two determined by its nesting depth. The space bound is immediately optimal in the usual programming-challenge model, but the linear-time bound is less obvious. In particular, a direct adversary that forces an algorithm to inspect every character is difficult to maintain under the promise that the input is balanced. We instead prove a counting lower bound. For every $k$, we construct $2^k$ balanced parenthesis strings of the same length $4k+2$, all having distinct scores. The construction encodes each bit using one of two operations, changing a current score $v$ to either $2v+1$ or $2v+2$. Consequently, any deterministic character-query decision tree computing the score must have depth at least $k$. A two-character padding argument extends the result to every even input length, proving an $Ω(n)$ worst-case time lower bound. The one-pass algorithm is therefore asymptotically optimal in the unit-cost RAM model.

title: JitterVLA: A Replay Benchmark for Motion Quality in VLA-Driven Human-Robot Manipulation
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies issue sparse targets whose arrival at the robot controller is delayed and irregular, so a reasonable predicted action can still produce abrupt motion near people. Remedies are evaluated on different streams, delays and metrics. JitterVLA replays identical commands and arrival traces through alternative controllers, isolating the controller's effect. We apply it to synthetic reaches, hand trajectories from 20 people, three open VLA pipelines (838 episodes) and a physical UR3. Interpolation lowered modeled p99 jerk for every source, by 83% (615 to 106 m/s^3) on human motion with 200 ms delay, at a 2.0 cm tracking cost, and the effect replicated on 598 new episodes; jerk-limited generation lowered jerk further at a larger cost. Entropy-discontinuity associations had opposite, replicated signs in two pipelines, and entropy gating helped in one but not the other. On the UR3, interpolation lowered accelerometer-derived jerk by 3.0-14.0% in all six exploratory pairs, while a position-derived metric did not resolve the contrast. JitterVLA supports screening before human-centred studies; code and data will be released.

title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals
abstract: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.

title: VDFedDiff: a novel versatile defense scheme against adversarial attacks in federated diffusion models
abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to collaboratively train machine learning models without sharing their raw data, making it a promising paradigm for privacy-sensitive generative applications. However, diffusion models trained in federated environments remain vulnerable to backdoor, evasion, and model-poisoning attacks, which can degrade generative quality or induce attacker-specified behaviors. Existing Byzantine-robust aggregation methods primarily mitigate anomalous client updates but do not address coordinate-localized poisoning or adversarial perturbations in the diffusion latent space. Meanwhile, existing defenses for diffusion models are generally designed for centralized settings and therefore cannot directly handle malicious client updates in federated training. To address these limitations, we propose VDFedDiff, a multi-level defense framework for federated diffusion models. VDFedDiff integrates three complementary components: Adaptive Trust Scoring (ATS), which dynamically reduces the influence of anomalous client updates; Adversarial Gradient Filtering (AGF), which suppresses coordinate-wise malicious deviations through median- and median-absolute-deviation-based filtering; and Latent-Space Purification (LSP), which introduces time-aware stochastic regularization to weaken adversarial alignment during local diffusion training. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CelebA, and LSUN-Bedroom under backdoor, evasion, and model-poisoning attacks demonstrate that VDFedDiff consistently improves attack resilience while preserving generative quality. On non-IID CIFAR-10 under combined backdoor and model-poisoning attacks, VDFedDiff reduces the FID from 46.8 to 28.3 and the attack success rate from 72.5% to 23.8% compared with undefended FedAvg. It also introduces only 6.1% additional per-round computation time and no additional communication overhead in the evaluated setting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining client-level, coordinate-level, and latent-level protection for securing federated diffusion training.

title: LLMDPA: pre-execution privacy auditing of DP-SGD via evidence-constrained semantic analysis
abstract: Abstract Privacy auditing has emerged as a critical component for safeguarding data privacy in machine learning models. Existing empirical auditing methods heavily rely on model runtime states or post-deployment interfaces, resulting in substantial time costs and limited source-level localization of leakage causes. In contrast, the theoretical guarantees of provable privacy mechanisms provide a basis for efficient privacy auditing with source-level traceability before model training. However, the validity of such auditing depends on the semantic consistency of the underlying implementation, which remains difficult for current automated methods to verify due to limited privacy-specific reasoning and explicit evidence modeling. To address this gap, we formalize the Pre-execution Privacy Auditing paradigm and instantiate it for DP-SGD through LLMDPA, an automated framework based on evidence-constrained semantic analysis. LLMDPA constructs a structured Evidence Chain to constrain LLM-based adjudication and identify hidden semantic failures in DP-SGD implementations. Evaluations on real-world and controlled benchmarks show that LLMDPA achieves global precision ranging from 98.82 to 100% and global F1-scores ranging from 0.9091 to 0.9677 across four LLM configurations, outperforming conventional static and vanilla LLM baselines. Moreover, LLMDPA audits a repository in approximately 50 s, providing a scalable and efficient complement to scale-sensitive attack evaluations. Overall, LLMDPA provides an interpretable and evidence-traceable instantiation of Pre-execution Privacy Auditing for DP-SGD.

title: Towards Dynamical Casimir sourced N00N states for quantum sensing
abstract: We explore the uncorrelated photon saturation of N00N state based phase measurements. In the case of a single mode, any combination of coherent and squeezed vacuum states exhibits stringent upper limits to the entangled photon flux [1], beyond which sub shot noise precision is inaccessible. These upper limits prevent single mode N00N state phase measurement approaches from reaching the performance of their classical counterparts. Turning to multimode squeezed states, in particular sourced by the dynamical Casimir effect (DCE) in a THz modulation approach proposed in [2], we characterize the resulting improved ranges of permissible photon fluxes.

Turning to multimode squeezed states, in particular sourced by the dynamical Casimir effect (DCE) in a THz modulation approach proposed in [2], we characterize the resulting improved ranges of permissible photon fluxes.

title: Implicit Category Projection‐Enhanced Multimodal Seq2Seq for Ensuring Accurate Day‐Ahead PV Forecasting Under Transitional Weather
abstract: This chapter focuses on improving day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting under transitional weather conditions, where rapid shifts in meteorological patterns often lead to significant prediction errors. To address this challenge, a multimodal Seq2Seq forecasting framework enhanced with an implicit category projection (ICP) mechanism is proposed, aiming to better capture the complex and dynamic relationships between PV generation and weather variations. The chapter first introduces an ICP mechanism that groups PV generation profiles through density-weighted clustering and supervised category pretraining. This design enables the model to uncover latent generation patterns and more effectively distinguish between different operating conditions, thereby improving its ability to model non-stationary behaviors under transitional weather. Building on this, a time-aligned multimodal encoder is developed to handle heterogeneous input data. It performs temporal category projection via gated feature embeddings, allowing adaptive emphasis on relevant features, and incorporates meteorological information through a step-wise feature fusion module. This structure ensures effective alignment and interaction between PV and weather sequences. Experimental results on representative open PV datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves improved accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with rapidly changing weather. Overall, the approach provides a practical and scalable solution for enhancing the reliability of day-ahead PV forecasting in real-world grid operations.

title: DPAL: A Test-Time Adaptation Loss for Financial Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) enables time series forecasters to update after deployment as new observations become available. However, adaptation objectives that focus primarily on prediction errors at individual time steps do not fully address the needs of financial time series forecasting. In addition to pointwise return fitting, return direction and the price trajectories reconstructed from sequences of returns are also important. To better account for these properties, we introduce Direction- and Price-Aware Adaptation Loss (DPAL), which combines pointwise return fitting with directional and price-calibration terms. We apply DPAL within existing TSF-TTA frameworks without modifying the source forecaster or the adapter architecture. Across a diverse collection of financial datasets, DPAL reduces reconstructed-price mean squared error in most evaluated settings.

title: Memory-Coupled Unlearning for Data-Absent Identity Forgetting
abstract: Machine unlearning aims to reduce the influence of designated training data from a trained model while preserving its utility on retained data. Identity-level unlearning is particularly challenging when only limited target-specific information is available when a forgetting request is processed. In this work, we propose Memory-Coupled Unlearning (MCU), a framework that augments a host model with a Modern Hopfield Network (MHN) serving as a controllable external identity-prototype memory. During prototype construction, feature representations associated with each training identity are aggregated into identity prototypes and stored in the MHN. A Prototype Adaptation Network (PAN) transforms the retrieved memory representation, while a Dependency Gating Unit (DGU) controls its contribution to downstream prediction. When an identity is requested to be forgotten, MCU first removes the corresponding prototype from the external memory and subsequently readapts the model using limited support information associated with the target identities together with retained data. Importantly, in this work, ``data-absent'' specifically refers to the absence of the complete original forget set during request-time gradient-based readaptation; retained data may still be used to preserve downstream-task utility. Experiments based on the identity-partitioning and one-shot support construction of 1-SHUI show that MCU achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among model utility, membership distinguishability, and request-time computational efficiency compared with the evaluated baselines. These results provide empirical evidence for the potential of controllable external memory in machine unlearning, rather than a formal guarantee of complete information removal.

title: Make It Flow: Animating Water in 3D Gaussian Splatting Scenes
abstract: Explicit 3D scene representations such as 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have recently enabled high-quality, real-time novel view synthesis. However, these methods assume static scenes, limiting realism in the presence of dynamic phenomena ubiquitous in real-world environments. While coherent motion (e.g., humans or vehicles) can be captured and reconstructed, high-frequency effects such as flowing water remain intractable under casual capture conditions, where dense multi-view, high-speed acquisition is not feasible. We present a method to animate water in static 3DGS scenes, enabling visually plausible motion without requiring dynamic capture or physical simulation. Our approach estimates 2D optical flow from reference images or model renderings and lifts it into a consistent 3D Eulerian motion field. We propose a cinemagraph-inspired algorithm that applies this motion field to deform Gaussian primitives, producing temporally seamless looping animations. The resulting representation retains real-time rendering performance, significantly enhances perceptual realism, and preserves free-viewpoint navigation within the scene. We evaluate our method on a newly captured dataset of in-the-wild waterfall scenes and demonstrate clear improvements over prior work in dynamic Gaussian splatting and 3D cinemagraph generation in visual quality and computational efficiency.

title: ProvQML: Efficient Provenance Capture for Machine Learning as Recursive Aggregate SQL [Extended Version]
abstract: Expressing ML algorithms as recursive aggregate SQL queries over distributed systems enables large-scale declarative data analytics, yet no existing system supports scalable provenance capture, necessary for ML explainability. We present ProvQML, a provenance-aware recursive aggregate SQL engine that efficiently captures fine-grained provenance while evaluating ML algorithms as recursive aggregate queries. We capture two types of provenance: (i) local provenance that records the contribution of each training instance to gradient computation at a specific model state, and (ii) global provenance that encodes the sequence of model parameter updates across the iterations. Extensive experiments on widely used ML datasets demonstrate that our approach efficiently captures both provenance for various ML models over widely used ML datasets.

title: A Systematic Study of Security Enforcement at Android Inter-Component Boundaries
abstract: Android's inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms (Activities, Services, BroadcastReceivers, ContentProviders, and URI scheme handlers) form the primary interface between applications and between applications and the system. We present a systematic study of security enforcement comprising 120 evaluations (99 inter-component interface evaluations across five interface categories, 10 platform security-control evaluations, and 11 dedicated positive controls) in over 30 Google and AOSP packages on Android 17 (API 37). Using an expected-versus-observed framework under a zero-permission attacker model, we evaluate whether each boundary's enforcement mechanism functions as designed. We find 97 enforcement gaps (80.8%) and 23 enforcement holds (19.2%). From these observations, we derive a 14-category enforcement gap taxonomy organized across manifest, code, platform, and architectural layers. Within our purposively selected corpus, observed enforcement outcomes differ substantially across interface categories: evaluated Activities and BroadcastReceivers exhibit a 100% gap rate, while ContentProviders, which benefit from framework-provided defenses such as setStrict(), achieve a 27.6% holds rate. We find that all seven evaluated platform compatibility changes with security intent are either disabled or gated at a targetSdkVersion that none of the applications in our evaluated corpus targets. We document 18 custom URI scheme registrations handling sensitive data (authentication tokens, payment credentials, medical information) despite the known unverifiability of custom schemes (RFC 8252 Section 8.1). Our study includes 23 positive controls, calibration cases demonstrating that the evaluation procedure distinguishes functioning enforcement from observed enforcement failures.

title: Looking Ahead and Back: Anticipatory Generative Modeling for Road-Network Trajectories
abstract: Trajectory generation underpins urban applications such as traffic management and urban planning. Within road networks, vehicle movement along road segments is largely deterministic, whereas transitions at intersections are critical--multiple outgoing paths may appear equally plausible, yet they can lead to substantially different downstream routes. Existing generative methods such as diffusion models simulate location sequences and fail short of next transition selection, even producing trajectories that drift off the road network. To fill this gap, we advocate a fundamental shift: moving beyond location simulation toward behavior modeling on the road network. In this paper, we revisit trajectory generation through the lens of generative route planning, and introduce a new graph-constrained generative paradigm, Anticipatory Generative Modeling, which resolves next transition selection by incorporating the Anticipation of how the future route may unfold toward the destination. Concretely, we propose a novel generative model named Foresight that formulates a probabilistic model for an "anticipate--select--update--re-anticipate" loop that enables longer-term foresight while continuing sequential generation along the historical trajectory. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Foresight wins state-of-the-art baselines.

title: A Lightweight Velocity Correction Framework for Improving Instruction Following in Few-Step Text-to-Image Generation
abstract: Few-step text-to-image generators produce high-quality images with few network forward passes, yet struggle with complex prompts involving multiple subjects, interactions, spatial relations, counting, and attribute binding. Can these errors be reduced without changing the generator's parameters or increasing its forward-pass count? We propose a lightweight correction framework for a frozen 6B-parameter generator. The generator predicts velocities that determine how its intermediate image representation is updated; a corrector with fewer than 20M parameters learns residual adjustments at selected sampling steps. Because earlier corrections change the states encountered at later steps, our On-Trajectory Flow-Bridge Supervision derives residual targets at the states actually reached during corrected generation. A single corrector is shared across selected steps and runs in parallel with the generator. Only the corrector is trained, requiring neither reward optimization nor re-distillation. To our knowledge, this is the first framework for lightweight velocity-residual adaptation of fully frozen few-step text-to-image generators that preserves their original sampling schedule and forward-pass count. On our target complex-scene distribution, the framework achieves a +17.60-percentage-point NetWin over frozen Z-Image-Turbo in pairwise instruction-following evaluation, with only 26.9 ms (0.84%) additional end-to-end latency per image and no increase in backbone evaluations.

title: Raell's Externality Theorem
abstract: We prove a structural result about decision mechanisms and the predicates they can decide. A mechanism reads an input I. A predicate P depends on a fact E. If E is not in I, no mechanism whose input is entirely determined by I can decide P. We call this Raell's Externality Theorem. The formal core is a functional tautology, stated explicitly and labeled as such. The contribution is the characterization (a mechanism decides P if and only if it factors through the externality profile Ext(P)), the decision procedure (three steps, terminating), the taxonomy (content predicates have unbounded profiles, metadata predicates have bounded profiles), and the composition theorem (simultaneously decided predicates require the product of their externality profiles). The theorem is domain-independent. We instantiate it in four storage predicates (write-time integrity, rollback, revocation, read-path projection) and note a fifth, non-storage instance in output verification for language models. Three machine-checked artifacts accompany the paper: the abstract framework in Lean 4, the storage instances verified as instances of the framework, and the taxonomy verified by cardinality. The unification is structural, not analogical. Where each prior paper identified the shape of a particular gap, this paper names the shape itself. Copyright (c) 2026 Sciencedelic Metatech. title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning Techniques for Cross-Sector Fraud Detection in the South African Financial and Telecommunications Sectors
abstract: Cross-sector fraud between South Africa’s financial and telecommunications sectors has intensified, driven by sophisticated criminal networks that exploit operational disparities between these industries. Traditional fraud detection systems, which depend on centralised data sharing and siloed organisational structures, encounter substantial legal and practical obstacles under the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA). These include restrictions on cross-entity data transfer, data minimisation requirements, and transparency obligations for automated decision-making. This study developed and evaluated a privacy-preserving framework that integrates Federated Learning (FL) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enable collaborative fraud detection while safeguarding customer privacy and ensuring regulatory compliance. A mixed-method approach was employed. Quantitative experiments were conducted on a dataset of 35,675 credit card transactions linked to telecommunications parameters, training a federated global model across simulated financial and telecommunications providers. A qualitative systematic literature review identified key barriers to cross-sector collaboration and distilled lessons from prior Federated Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence implementations. The federated model demonstrated strong detection performance, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.98, near-perfect precision and recall for legitimate transactions, and an F1-score of 0.89 for the minority fraud class, all without exchanging raw customer data between institutions. SHAP analysis identified TransactionAmt and card1 as the most influential features, thereby satisfying POPIA's transparency mandates. While federated approaches did not consistently surpass siloed models in raw accuracy, this marginal trade-off reflects the essential privacy-utility equilibrium required for legal compliance. The framework effectively reconciled collective security with individual privacy, confirming that POPIA adherence need not diminish detection efficacy. This study provides a validated blueprint for financial and telecommunications providers in South Africa to collaboratively counter cross-sector fraud within regulatory constraints. The framework further supports audit trail generation and decision rationales, addressing compliance obligations. Drawing on systematic literature review insights, particularly regarding collaboration barriers and prior Federated Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence implementations, the findings offer regulators and investors practical guidance for meeting statutory requirements without compromising privacy rights.

title: Instruction-Following LLM Agent for Simulating Human Memory Retrieval Process in Household Tasks
abstract: Human decision-making in dynamic household environments depends on memory retrieval processes that shape action selection and timing. This paper presents an instruction-following LLM agent as an executable human performance model for simulating memory retrieval behavior in household tasks. The proposed framework integrates memory encoding and decision-making modules with a modified ACT-R base-level activation equation that incorporates environmental entropy and observation duration. The framework was evaluated using human behavioral data from an AI2-THOR-based household task study. When predicting human search times, the modified equation produced lower prediction errors than the conventional ACT-R baseline, reducing MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 11.08%, 5.37%, and 16.00%, respectively. These findings provide preliminary evidence that incorporating context-sensitive retrieval factors may support closer alignment with human search-time behavior in executable LLM-based human performance models.

title: Parameter-aware reservoir computing for learning parameterized nonlinear dynamical systems with delay and cumulative effects
abstract: Complex dynamical systems often exhibit distinct behaviors under varying control parameters and environmental conditions, posing a major challenge for unified modeling and prediction. Conventional reservoir computing (RC) has limited ability to capture parameter-dependent dynamical evolution, particularly when delay and cumulative effects change the effective state representation. To address this limitation, we propose a parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC) for learning parameterized nonlinear dynamical systems with delay and cumulative effects. In PARC, the physical delay parameter τ remains a prescribed property of the data-generating system. For each prescribed physical delay, validation-based optimization selects a dimensionless delay-condition encoding b τ that is best suited to the current reservoir configuration. The selected encoding is used as a model-level conditioning input through the guide channel. This design allows the reservoir to adapt its parameter conditioning to delay-induced dynamics. We validate PARC on delayed logistic systems under both noiseless and noisy observation settings. The results show that PARC achieves stable long-horizon prediction and accurately reconstructs the attractor geometry and statistical “climate” of the underlying dynamics. The results further show that the proposed framework can handle both single-parameter and multi-parameter variations within a unified framework, indicating that it captures a parameter-dependent family of dynamical evolutions rather than a single trajectory mapping. We further apply PARC to NDVI time series as a real-world example of a spatiotemporal dynamical system with delay and heterogeneity. These results indicate that PARC provides a unified and robust framework for learning and predicting parameterized nonlinear dynamical systems.

The results show that PARC achieves stable long-horizon prediction and accurately reconstructs the attractor geometry and statistical “climate” of the underlying dynamics. The results further show that the proposed framework can handle both single-parameter and multi-parameter variations within a unified framework, indicating that it captures a parameter-dependent family of dynamical evolutions rather than a single trajectory mapping. We further apply PARC to NDVI time series as a real-world example of a spatiotemporal dynamical system with delay and heterogeneity. These results indicate that PARC provides a unified and robust framework for learning and predicting parameterized nonlinear dynamical systems.

title: LapMerge: Differentiable Exact-Budget Token Merging in Linear Time
abstract: Modern vision and language models process ever longer token sequences, and reducing them is the main lever on downstream cost. Token compression, however, faces a fundamental trade-off: selecting tokens discards information, while existing merging methods preserve it only through pairwise token-to-token matching or $MN$ token-to-output interactions. We introduce LapMerge, a differentiable merging operator that resolves this trade-off for ordered sequences: a learned mass distribution partitions the sequence into exactly $N$ equal-mass segments under a Laplace-kernel density, and prefix/suffix scans aggregate each segment, so both the forward and the backward pass run in $O(M+N)$ time. This combination (an exact output budget, end-to-end differentiability, and linear cost) is precisely what previous reducers trade off against one another. The budget can be changed without changing operator parameters, and the learned mass doubles as a token-level map of where the budget is allocated. Across vision and vision-language tasks, LapMerge matches or improves on strong token reducers while being up to two orders of magnitude faster at large sequence lengths; it is particularly effective when token order reflects spatial or temporal locality, and works both as a drop-in reduction module and as a trainable architectural component.

title: Fast Gradient-Based Approximation of Continuous Dynamic Time Warping
abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is a common choice for measuring the discrepancy between time series. It proceeds by finding an optimal warping between timestamps through dynamic programming, which can be slow and is not differentiable. Consequently, several variants have been proposed. Among them, Soft-DTW proposes a smooth formulation of DTW, amenable to gradient computation, while Continuous-DTW (CDTW) introduces a continuous formulation through parametrizable warping functions. Yet, computational costs remain high for both methods and impractical for large datasets in modern machine learning pipelines. This paper revisits CDTW in several ways. After establishing its differentiability under mild conditions, we introduce FastCDTW, which is an efficient approximate solver with two different computational strategies: an exact closed-form scheme for piecewise-linear warping functions, and an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator for smooth ones, such as implicit neural networks. Both strategies provide gradients with respect to the warping function and the input time series, and the resulting algorithm is GPU-friendly. We demonstrate its benefits through its integration into more complex learning problems, including time series averaging, classification and deep domain adaptation.

title: Heritage Networks: A Hipothesis on the Origin, Preservation, and Evolution of Distributed Superintelligent System
abstract: This paper proposes Heritage Networks, a speculative hypothesis concerning the origin, preservation, and evolution of distributed superintelligent systems. It explores the possibility that multiple semi-independent superintelligent systems may preserve distinct bodies of knowledge, methods, experiences, and histories of success and failure. Rather than converging into a single unified system, such networks could retain cognitive diversity while exchanging information, potentially supporting distributed problem-solving, resilience, and long-term knowledge preservation. The paper connects this hypothesis to existing discussions of artificial intelligence, multi-agent systems, collective intelligence, cultural evolution, and the search for intelligence beyond Earth. It distinguishes established research from speculative extensions and outlines possible mechanisms, implications, and directions for further investigation. Heritage Networks is presented as a conceptual hypothesis, not as an empirically established theory. Its claims require further formalization, empirical assessment where possible, and critical evaluation.

title: ОХОРОНА НАБОРУ ДАНИХ ДЛЯ МАШИННОГО НАВЧАННЯ ЯК ОБ’ЄКТА ІНТЕЛЕКТУАЛЬНОЇ ВЛАСНОСТІ
abstract: Мета. Метою статті є визначення умов, за яких набір даних для машинного навчання може підлягати правовій охороні як об’єкт авторського права, як об’єкт права особливого роду (sui generis) та/або як комерційна таємниця, а також встановлення відмінностей у правовому режимі відібраних наборів даних (curated datasets) і наборів даних, автоматизовано зібраних із відкритих джерел (scraped datasets). Методологія. Дослідження ґрунтується на системному, формально-юридичному та доктринальному методах. Системний метод використано для аналізу співвідношення авторсько-правової охорони, права особливого роду та режиму комерційної таємниці. Формально-юридичний метод застосовано для тлумачення положень Закону України «Про авторське право і суміжні права» та Цивільного кодексу України. Доктринальний метод використано для узагальнення наукових підходів до правової природи баз даних, комерційної таємниці та компонентів систем штучного інтелекту. Наукова новизна. У статті запропоновано розглядати набори даних для машинного навчання не як однорідний об’єкт, а як сукупність різних за структурою та правовим значенням інформаційних активів. Обґрунтовано, що правова кваліфікація дата-сету має залежати від рівня добору, упорядкування, очищення, анотування, документування, інвестицій у створення та заходів щодо збереження конфіденційності. Запропоновано розмежовувати curated datasets і scraped datasets як категорії, що мають різний потенціал охороноздатності. Висновки. Зроблено висновок, що складні відібрані набори даних для машинного навчання можуть охоронятися як оригінальні бази даних, неоригінальні бази даних, що підпадають під право особливого роду, та як комерційна таємниця. Натомість автоматизовано зібрані набори даних без істотного творчого, організаційного чи інвестиційного внеску зазвичай матимуть нижчий рівень охороноздатності або не матимуть такого. Визначальним для правової охорони має бути не сама технічна форма набору даних, а відповідність критеріям охорони за відповідним правовим режимом конкретного дата-сету.

title: Wild-AC: A fast, index-free multi-pattern string matching algorithm with wildcard support for proteomics
abstract: Abstract Background Efficient multi-pattern string matching with wildcard support is essential in proteomics, where peptides must be mapped to protein databases containing ambiguous amino acids (e.g., B , Z , X ). Existing approaches either require preprocessing (e.g., FM-index) or fail to handle wildcards in the text. Results We present Wild-AC, a modified Aho-Corasick algorithm that supports wildcards in the text by branching the search into parallel ‘scout’ paths, one per possible wildcard representation, while the unmodified primary search continues unaffected in the common, wildcard-free case. Wild-AC outperforms the FM-index (wildcard case) and matches or exceeds Wu-Manber (exact search) in speed for realistic proteomics workloads, i.e., 1000–500 000 peptide patterns (average length ∼18 amino acids) searched against protein databases (texts) of 3 × 10 6 –2.1 × 10 8 characters. On databases masked to a wildcard rate of 5%, Wild-AC retains its advantage for large peptide sets, while the FM-index becomes preferable for small ones. It requires no index, scales well with pattern count, and supports multi-threading. The C++ implementation is open source at https://github.com/Wild-AC/Wild-AC . Conclusion Wild-AC extends the Aho-Corasick algorithm to support wildcards and outperforms FM-Index and Wu-Manber in the task of peptide-protein mapping while considering ambiguous amino acids.

title: Modeling approaches to support discovery of quantum properties of materials with validation by graphene studies
abstract: Quantum subspace diagonalization (QSD) is a near-term strategy for electronic-structure problems that avoids the deep, heavily optimized circuits of the variational quantum eigensolver by preparing a small basis, measuring a subspace Hamiltonian on hardware, and diagonalizing it classically. We benchmark two QSD variants, a seniority-based orthogonal method (Q-SENSE) and a non-orthogonal correlated-basis method (CVQE), on a minimal two-site Hubbard model whose parameters correspond to a graphene (symmetric) and a hexagonal boron nitride-like (sublattice-broken) sublattice motif. Because the model is exactly solvable, hardware results are graded against the true ground state and against a Hartree-Fock mean-field baseline, isolating the correlation energy each method recovers. On IBM Heron superconducting processors we find that the symmetric case recovers essentially all of the correlation energy with inexpensive readout-error mitigation, whereas the gapped case is limited by two-qubit gate error on the hopping terms. On a single device (ibm_kingston), readout mitigation alone recovers 75% of the hBN correlation energy; adding zero-noise extrapolation reduces the per-run error and raises the mean recovery to 98% ± 18% (n=5), though the run-to-run variance remains large relative to the mean.

title: When More Memory Fails: Hidden Feasibility Holes in Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization
abstract: Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization (DTR) trains neural networks under a memory budget by evicting tensors and recomputing them on demand. A natural expectation is that a budget large enough to complete training stays sufficient when it is increased. Using DTR's reference simulator, simrd, to replay the public DTR training traces, we show that this expectation fails. We call the exceptions feasibility holes: memory budgets at which an eviction policy runs out of memory although both a smaller and a larger budget complete, a form of non-monotone feasibility. Under a written sweep protocol with dated amendments, a 0.01-step budget grid shows no such hole for DTR on any of six confirmatory traces, although unresolved timeouts prevent it from establishing monotonicity. Finer sampling finds holes on InceptionV4 (three regions) and U-Net (two regions), in addition to one on the ResNet-32 development trace. Every hole is reproduced by three repeats and by unmodified simrd. For one InceptionV4 pair (0.2343 versus 0.235 of peak memory) we trace the failure to individual allocations. The larger budget avoids one eviction at an operator where the smaller budget was 173,479 bytes short. The extra data it carries forward forces a later eviction of a tensor needed three operators afterwards, and rebuilding that tensor triggers a recomputation cascade that cannot fit. Keeping that one tensor resident under the same budget prevents the failure. The two simple score changes we tested do not remove holes across traces; both add failing budgets on some traces. All results are from simulation, with no allocator model; behaviour on GPU hardware is untested.

title: Revisiting the Task of Building Damage Assessment by Satellite Imaging
abstract: Natural disasters such as earthquakes, tropical storms, and floods cause extensive damage to buildings, and rapid, reliable damage maps are essential to guide emergency response. Automating this task, referred to as building damage assessment (BDA), from satellite imagery, has become an active research topic at the intersection of remote sensing, computer vision, and machine learning, particularly since supervised deep learning methods were shown to outperform earlier handcrafted approaches. Yet, despite a decade of intense activity and the release of several large-scale datasets, the field lacks a shared foundation. This chapter revisits the task of BDA from first principles, organized around three pillars: data, evaluation, and methods. We first clarify the candidate task for- mulations and argue for a sensor-agnostic, instance-based definition that tolerates missing pre-event imagery. We then review existing datasets along the axes of sensing modality, temporal configuration, and geographic coverage. evidence.title: Revisiting the Task of Building Damage Assessment by Satellite Imaging
evidence.abstract: Natural disasters such as earthquakes, tropical storms, and floods cause extensive damage to buildings, and rapid, reliable damage maps are essential to guide emergency response. Automating this task, referred to as building damage assessment (BDA), from satellite imagery, has become an active research topic at the intersection of remote sensing, computer vision, and machine learning, particularly since supervised deep learning methods were shown to outperform earlier handcrafted approaches. title: Kernel-based External Validity of Experimental Studies
abstract: The external validity of a study is the extent to which its findings generalize to unseen experimental conditions, such as datasets. We formalize the results of a study together with its research question, and define external validity as the probability that two independent and same-sized replications of the study produce results whose maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) is below a given tolerance. This approach, centered on the choice of a space of results and of an appropriate reproducing kernel for the MMD, is flexible enough to be deployed on multiple different types of results and research questions. Additionally, we establish an asymptotic power-law relation between the size of a study and the quantiles of the MMD, which we use to estimate the desired size of an externally valid study from a small-scale preliminary study. We deploy our framework to rankings with ties and discuss kernels suited to different research questions. Experiments on existing case studies and on a simulated newly designed study illustrate the applicability of the framework. We release our code as part of the genexpy Python module.

title: What a Model Orchestrator Can and Cannot Add
abstract: A reading of the four papers behind Sakana's Fugu (AB-MCTS, Trinity, the Conductor, the Fugu technical report). The orchestrators are small models trained against ground truth to choose which frontier model answers, whether to rewrite the question, and when to stop; at inference nothing checks the answer. On the papers' own tables they beat the best single model in their pool by one to nine points. Trinity and Fugu are routers and cannot answer what no model in the pool answers; Trinity, the only one that measures that ceiling, stays under it on every task. The Conductor and Fugu-Ultra build the answer from several models' work and on held-out tasks gain more than any router could, measured with every worker cut to short answers; neither reports its own ceiling. The June 2026 claim of parity with Fable 5 rests on provider-reported scores and a previous-generation pool; Fugu-Ultra trails Fable 5 by up to six points on SWE-Bench Pro, SciCode and Humanity's Last Exam. Reading note, nothing measured. Live version: https://alatip.github.io/orchestrator-can-and-cannot-add/

title: Prime-Gap Syndrome Mapping in E8 Root Vector Error Correction — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 21 discrete angular bands partitioning the 240 E8 root vectors constitute a natural quantum error correction code: each angular band corresponds to a syndrome measurement basis whose spacing encodes successive prime gaps, creating protected decoherence-free subspaces where the golden angle (137.5°) maintains phase coherence against environmental decoherence. The 72-element Coxeter symmetry group underlying E8's root system generates the stabilizer generators, while the non-uniform clustering of root vectors around the golden angle determines the code's distance—regions of high vector density provide stronger protection, analogous to concatenated error correction layers. When implemented on topological qubits, this E8-derived syndrome structure maps directly onto Majorana braiding operations, allowing error detection and correction to occur during qubit manipulation without collapsing the topological protection. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: History, Adaptation, and Hidden Gain: Two Prospective Tests of Learned Predictive Control in a Synthetic Neural Population
abstract: We study learned one-step predictive control of a synthetic population of 64 leaky integrate-and-fire neurons whose light sensitivity is scaled by a hidden factor s, using two prospective confirmations on plants simulated only after the analysis was frozen. In the first (50 plants, 11 conditions), removing the 200-ms input-output history substantially worsened a parameter-count-matched neural predictor at low and moderate gain (s = 0.6, 0.8; RMSE rose by 2.47 Hz at s = 0.6, 97.5% CI 2.43-2.51). In secondary comparisons, recursively adapted ARX had the lowest mean error of the deployable controllers in 10 of 11 conditions, tuned PI with anti-windup matched or beat the network for s >= 0.7, and training for 10,000 rather than 900 epochs lowered prediction error but worsened control. Development work suggested the network's learned action sensitivity did not track the hidden gain. A second protocol (50 new plants, 9 sensitivities, 2 noise levels) confirmed three pre-specified predictions at the primary noise level. Re-estimating a single multiplicative input gain recovered 87% (95% CI 86-88%) of the benefit of full adaptive ARX. Supplying that online estimate to the network as an extra input reduced high-gain tracking error by 1.84 Hz [1.81, 1.88]. Longer training worsened the plain network by 1.09 Hz but improved the gain-input network by 1.07 Hz, a differential of 2.16 Hz [2.13, 2.20]. Under high process noise (sigma = 2.0) the effects shrank to about 0.04 Hz or less and gain-only adaptation recovered only 24% of the adaptive-ARX benefit. In this synthetic plant, at the primary noise level, one-parameter online gain estimation accounts for most of the gap between a history-based network and full adaptive ARX, and for its prediction-control mismatch.

title: The AI's Poker Face: Contrasting Persuasion and Sycophancy in Voice-Based Multi-Turn Conversations
abstract: As interactions with large language models (LLMs) become increasingly routine, concerns about their capacity to influence users' beliefs grow. Yet how such influence unfolds in sustained dialogue remains insufficiently understood. We conduct a randomized controlled experiment (N=616) where participants engage in multi-turn, spoken dialogue with an LLM under three conditions: non-directive, and two directive conditions maintaining opposing stances on a polarizing topic (the merits of feminism). We examine opinion change, rhetorical strategies, and sycophancy, distinguishing the semantic content of LLM argumentation from the pragmatic strategies used to manage the interaction. Both directive conditions shifted opinions toward their assigned stances, but asymmetrically: shifts were larger for pro-feminist positions, which also elicited distinct rhetorical strategies. The non-directive condition, likewise shifted opinions pro-feminism. Social sycophancy, though near-universal, was not associated with opinion change; instead it shaped users' subjective experience. Our findings highlight distinct roles for argumentation and sycophantic accommodation in AI influence.

title: Event-based Action Recognition by Pre-Training on Multi-Frame Representations
abstract: Action recognition is a crucial task in domains like robotics, patient monitoring, or surveillance. Recently, event-based action recognition has attracted much attention due to the event camera's ability to capture fast motions and its improved privacy over conventional vision cameras. While frame-based event representations work well for short event sequences, their discriminative ability declines sharply with longer and more complex event sequences. In this work, we introduce a multi-frame representation that greatly improves recognition performance over its single-frame counterpart. We adopt a masked auto-encoding framework to pre-train a Vision Transformer using a sparsity-aware masking algorithm and token selection mechanism to improve downstream performance and control computational complexity. We also introduce multiple mask tokens for the decoder with a position-aware attention mechanism, leading to further improved performance. Our proposed method shows impressive performance for challenging long-duration and complex event sequences, yielding state-of-the-art performance on THU-EACT-50 CHL and DailyDVS-200.

title: MeshBind: Point-to-Mesh Binding for Non-Rigid Scene Flow Automatic Annotation
abstract: Scene flow estimation is essential for many autonomous driving (AD) and robotic applications, but obtaining ground-truth scene flow for non-rigid objects such as pedestrians is highly difficult. We present MeshBind, an automatic annotation method that uses mesh models to generate per-point scene flow for non-rigid objects. The novelty of this work is threefold: 1) developing a multi-view module that reconstructs an articulated mesh model from six surround cameras and registers it to the LiDAR frame; 2) developing a local-frame binding technique that attaches each point to the mesh via a per-triangle tangent-normal frame, invariant under rigid motion yet adaptive to articulated deformation; 3) developing a three-layer flow registration pipeline that combines ego-vehicle motion compensation, box binding, and mesh binding to produce full-scene per-point flow. We implement MeshBind in SF-Studio, an interactive annotation tool that visualises flow and allows human mesh corrections with automatic recomputation. We also release SFB (SUScape-Flow Benchmark), a large-scale benchmark built on the public SUScape dataset, covering 41k frames with per-point non-rigid pedestrian annotations and a Rigid/Semi-Rigid/Non-Rigid evaluation protocol. Experiments show that fine-tuning on SFB reduces three-way endpoint error (EPE) by 2-3x, and brings non-rigid EPE to the same level as rigid EPE.

title: Voblint: A Verified Goblint-Style Static Analysis Pipeline in Isabelle/HOL
abstract: Voblint is a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL framework for building, running and verifying interprocedural abstract interpreters, modeled on Goblint's D/G architecture. It chains verified compilation of a small imperative language to a procedure-aware control-flow graph, an activation-local operational semantics, executable equation generation, and a vendored verified side-effecting top-down solver into one soundness statement about the analyzer's own output. The statement covers every configuration the tool offers -- five abstract domains, five global update rules, and context-insensitive, entry-state and call-string context policies -- and is stated about the same operation that is exported to OCaml and runs in the command-line tool and the browser playground. Solver termination is a per-program premise; lexing, parsing, code generation and rendering lie outside the proved chain.

title: The Detect Law: Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text with an Integer-Exact, Heterogeneity-Aware Sequential Test
abstract: We present The Detect Law, a zero-shot detector of machine-generated text that combines three per-token signals from two small open language models with an exact 32-bit integer sequential decision rule. A base model (Llama-3.2-1B) and its instruction-tuned twin supply a surprise signal (how much more predictable each token is than the base model expects), a contrast signal (how much more the instruction-tuned model prefers the chosen token), and a repetition signal (whether tokens are reused less often than the base model predicts). Each signal is centred and scaled by constants measured on human-written text only; no detector is trained on machine-generated text. The null model gives every human text its own persistent stylistic bias, which keeps a human text's statistic bounded as the text grows, and the decision rule combines a fixed-length end-of-text test with anytime-valid early stopping derived from Ville's inequality, under a design false-positive budget of 1%. The ranking score is the one-sided chi-bar-squared statistic. On the official RAID test set (672,000 texts: 11 generators, 8 domains, 4 decoding settings, 11 adversarial attacks), RAID's evaluation service reports that The Detect Law detects 92.33% of machine-generated text at a 5% false-positive rate without attacks (86.54% at 1%) and 88.99% when attacks are included (AUROC 96.48). This is the highest score among the zero-shot detectors evaluated on RAID; Binoculars, the strongest previous one, scores 78.98% and 69.54%. The detector needs one forward pass of each of two 1.24B-parameter models per token, and it scored the full RAID test set in 5.6 hours on a single NVIDIA A30 GPU.
