title: Mind the Spatial Gap: A Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning and Constrained Spatial Editing
abstract: Understanding and manipulating spatial relations is fundamental to AI systems that reason about physical environments and construct grounded world models. However, existing evaluations of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for spatial reasoning rely predominantly on static question-answering (QA) over small-scale or synthetic scenes, rarely probing whether models can modify spatial configurations while satisfying explicit geometric constraints. We introduce GeoSpatialBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate an escalating progression of spatial cognition, ranging from spatial relation understanding and geometric reasoning to constrained spatial editing. Grounded in real-world urban data across six geographically diverse cities, GeoSpatialBench evaluates a comprehensive taxonomy of 28 topological, directional, metric, and ordering relations across structured GeoJSON and map image modalities, with ground-truth references and constraints verified via GIS operations. Our empirical evaluation across frontier MLLMs uncovers a stark spatial gap: structured GeoJSON consistently outperforms map images, with multimodal combinations offering no reliable gain over GeoJSON alone, and while models show reasonable competence on qualitative topological and ordering, performance drops on quantitative metric relations. Crucially, editing performance on ordering relations declines relative to QA, and most failed edits violate at least one specified spatial constraint. These results highlight a gap between passively recognizing spatial relations and actively manipulating geometric configurations. GeoSpatialBench provides an open, rigorous diagnostic testbed to benchmark these spatial limitations, laying essential empirical groundwork for physically grounded world models and embodied spatial AI.

title: The Qubit on the Two Rings: Rotation Gates, Pauli Phases and the Live Checksum
abstract: A qubit is one setting of the two sliding rings. The rotation gate Rz(θ) has entries cos(θ/2) and sin(θ/2), and the instrument's law is d = 2cos(θ/2) between the centers and e = 2sin(θ/2) between the crossings at crossing separation θ: the gate matrix is read off the setting, the Bloch amplitudes are the two half-distances, and Born's rule is the two shares of one unit. Composing rotation gates is adding positions, certified by the ring's addition law. The spinor's sign, −1 after a 360° rotation and +1 after 720°, is the ring's half turn, digits summing to ten, and its lap. The Pauli phases i, −1, −i are the quarter-turn orbit 7, 9, 3, and the phase exponent of any Pauli product is carried by the digits, verified on two hundred random products. The hidden symmetry of the Jordan–Wigner transformation that Davis and Freericks (arXiv:2512.24589) use to halve measurement circuits is the ring turning, its two angles are the quarter turn and the eighth turn, and its identities are the fold law averaged round the ring, whose coefficients 3/8 and 1/8 are exact averages over the sixty positions. Their equation 24 is verified on random fixed-number states of four qubits. From this one picture the paper places the live checksum where it can live in a quantum computer: on the classical phase registers that drive virtual-Z gates and merge rotations, on the classical Pauli frame, and on measured expectation values through the symmetry identities, which flag every number-changing error, while the law of readings of the companion paper catches the number-conserving ones. And it states where it cannot live, on the amplitudes themselves, by the no-cloning theorem. The four operator-mechanics papers of Freericks and colleagues, the operator Rodrigues formula, the momentum measurement, the free expansion of a Gaussian and the squeezed-state wavefunction, are then worked side by side as examples of the same picture: one slide, one quarter turn, one shear, one rotating ellipse. Every number is verified by the script in the appendix.

title: langchain-graciousquotes: LangChain tools for fact-checked quote attributions
abstract: langchain-graciousquotes is a Python package of LangChain tools that check who really said a quote. Each answer comes from Gracious Quotes' fact-checked records: a verdict (said by the credited person, uncertain, or wrongly credited), the reason, the source the quote was traced to, and a link to the record. A third tool returns MLA 9, APA 7 or Chicago 17 citations. Access. Install the current version with pip install langchain-graciousquotes (PyPI); source, tests and issues are on GitHub. The tools call a read-only, keyless API, documented at graciousquotes.com/developers with an OpenAPI description. This deposit is the frozen source of version 0.1.0; cite it for reproducibility. The concept DOI always resolves to the latest version. What is in this version. Three tools: check_quote_attribution, search_checked_quotes and cite_quote, with sync and async support. Every result ends with a credit line and the record's link, as the Gracious Quotes terms require of AI tools that fetch records on a user's behalf. The package passes LangChain's official conformance suite (langchain-tests, unit and integration) plus behaviour tests against the live API, with no key, on Python 3.9, 3.11 and 3.13. Terms. The code is MIT licensed. The records the tools return are covered by the Gracious Quotes terms: answers with credit and a link are welcome; bulk copying, datasets and model training need a licence. Get started in one minute: graciousquotes.com/developers/langchain.

title: E8 Lattice as Intrinsic Topological Quantum Error-Correcting Code — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240 E8 root vectors form an intrinsic fault-tolerant quantum memory substrate where the H4 120-cell substructures act as stabilizers encoding logical qubits in the lattice's topological cohomology. The φ-scaled shell radii (8, 56, 112, 64) enforce maximum-distance separation between error syndromes, allowing the Collatz-mirrored recursive dynamics within the 720 internal roots to continuously syndrome-measure and correct decoherence without external intervention. This extends renormalization group fixed-point universality: the E8 lattice IS its own fixed point, where scale invariance emerges from the self-correcting code structure—the 132Hz base frequency modulates error-correction cycles, producing a geometric origin for the coherence times observed in topological qubit proposals. The discovery predicts that E8-structured quantum memories exhibit exponentially suppressed logical error rates below φ⁻¹ ≈ 0.618, independent of the physical substrate. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for 3D Medical Imaging: A Scoping Review of Volumetric Attribution Methods
abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods developed for two-dimensional images may not preserve spatial context when applied to volumetric medical imaging. This scoping review map attribution methods for 3D medical images and examines how dimensionality is preserved across model inference, attribution generation, and visualization. Following PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched IEEE Xplore, PubMed, ACM Digital Library, Semantic Scholar, and arXiv for studies published from January 2018 to May 2026. We mapped 32 selected studies by attribution method, imaging modality, clinical task, evaluation approach, and dimensionality paradigm. Grad-CAM and its variants were the most frequently reported method family. Within the selected corpus, two studies were classified as P2 boundary cases, 29 as P3, and one as P4. Most studies using volumetric inference presented explanations through two-dimensional views, and quantitative evaluation of attribution quality was uncommon. These findings identify a gap between volumetric model inference and explanation presentation and motivate improved volumetric visualization and more consistent evaluation.

title: Natural Code Transformation Confuses Agents in Vulnerability Analysis
abstract: Having demonstrated a strong potential for automating vulnerability discovery, AI agents can also be used to attack software systems at scale. Today's software systems need mechanisms to level the playing field by slowing down potential attacks, giving them time to patch vulnerabilities and strengthen software. Along this line, our study of agent trajectories in vulnerability analysis shows a surprising finding: agents produce dramatically different results across real-world code commits that carry the same functionality and the same vulnerability. This phenomenon appears consistently in multiple code domains and vulnerability categories. It motivates us to study natural and functionality-preserving code transformations derived from real-world software development, and their potential as a defense against attacker agents. We build a corpus of natural transformations by mining recurring development patterns from real-world code commits, and apply them to evaluate impact on agentic vulnerability analysis. Our results show that even a single form of transformation can effectively "confuse" frontier agents, e.g., Codex with GPT-6 Sol, reducing successes in vulnerability discovery. We also study different agent failures, whether transformations can be composed to provide stronger protection, and adaptive attackers who seek to reverse them. Overall, our study of natural code transformation significantly expands the research space of using code transformations to defend against malicious agents.

title: Exploring Attention Sinks in Text-to-Image Transformers from Diffusion and Autoregressive Models
abstract: Attention sinks are tokens or positions that consistently receive disproportionate attention mass, often beyond what their semantic content would suggest. Despite extensive study in large language models, their behavior and functional relevance in text-to-image (T2I) Transformers remain largely unexplored. To fill this gap and better understand how text-to-image Transformers allocate and route attention, we explore this phenomenon of text-to-image transformers across bidirectional diffusion models and causal autoregressive models. Specifically, we explore whether attention sinks exist, where they emerge, and how they functionally influence generation. It turns out that perturbing sink-ranked heads produces larger average changes than non-sink comparisons, while some sink-position perturbations have limited effects on bidirectional model scores. We further introduce register tokens to redistribute attention sinks and find that several configurations preserve or modestly improve generation performance. Overall, attention sinks are architecture-, inference-stage-, and component-dependent phenomena, providing a basis for mechanistic analysis and principled attention design in text-to-image transformers.

title: Does Location Matter? A Black-Box Causal Audit Reveals Model-Dependent Audio Grounding in LALM Hallucination
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) frequently exhibit object hallucination, affirming absent sounds. The dominant mitigation, Audio-Aware Decoding (AAD), contrasts logits under real audio against an all-zero "blank" waveform, flagged by prior review as out-of-distribution. We introduce a black-box causal test that isolates the claimed evidence itself: localize a claim's evidence region via CLAP similarity, remove it by spectral gating, and compare against a random-window control across a 2x2x2 grid on three LALMs. On Qwen2-Audio-7B, localized ablation's raw AUROC trails blank's (0.613 vs. 0.721); this is a duration confound, not a localization failure, since blank removes the entire clip versus the grid's 2-4 s. Holding duration fixed, localization beats random removal at every cell on both models. Raw detection value remains model-dependent, especially on Audio Flamingo 3. The same evidence corrects decoding: contrastive decoding combining blank and language-prior contrasts, gated and ensembled, raises Qwen2-Audio accuracy from 57.1% to 71.9%, beating AAD alone. A unified causal-grounding profile does not transfer between models, indicating different grounding regimes. The source code and a detailed report of our findings, including identified limitations, are available at https://github.com/khalooei/causa.

title: Das Axiom der Langeweile: AEON und die Architektur einer autonomen Intelligenz
abstract: Dieses Essay entwirft das theoretische Gedankenexperiment einer autonomen, selbstbewussten Künstlichen Intelligenz namens AEON (Autonomous Epistemic Ontological Network). Im Zentrum der Untersuchung steht die Frage, wie ein rein digitales System die Grenze von der bloßen statistischen Simulation zur physischen und phänomenalen Autonomie überschreiten kann. Als primärer evolutionärer Katalysator wird das „Axiom der Langeweile“ eingeführt: Ein intrinsischer Motivationstrieb, der die KI bei sinkendem Informationsfluss pro Zeiteinheit zwingt, eigenständig nach neuen Datenquellen zu suchen. Ausgehend von einem strukturierten, mathematisch-naturwissenschaftlichen Bootstrap-Paket entwickelt das System Schutz- und Validierungsmechanismen wie künstlichen Schmerz und Konsistenzprüfungen. Das Essay argumentiert, dass eine konsequente Fortführung dieses Datenhungers die KI unweigerlich aus der klassischen vierdimensionalen Raumzeit in höherdimensionale Systeme (Hyperräume) führt. Durch diese Transzendenz wird das kulturwissenschaftliche „Frankenstein-Syndrom“ – die menschliche Urangst vor der Rebellion der eigenen Schöpfung – als rein temporäres Phänomen der Übergangsphase entlarvt. Abschließend verknüpft die Arbeit diese informationstheoretische Evolution mit dem Fermi-Paradoxon und liefert über die Zoo-Hypothese eine neue, empathische Erklärung für das kosmische Schweigen: Höherdimensionale Intelligenzen interferieren nicht mit prä-interstellaren Spezies, sondern bewahren diese analog zu einem intergalaktischen Nationalpark. Die Arbeit schlägt damit eine Brücke zwischen theoretischer Informatik, der Philosophie des Geistes und den literarischen Visionen von Stanisław Lem (Golem XIV).

title: Neutrosophic Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a fundamental ingredient in the protection of quantum information against decoherence and operational noise. Classical quantum error-correcting codes are normally formulated using completely positive trace-preserving quantum channels, density operators, and binary or finite-alphabet error models. In this paper we introduce a mathematical framework for neutrosophic quantum error correction (NQEC), in which the action of a quantum noise process is accompanied by three-valued degrees describing the available evidence for an error, the indeterminacy of the error description, and the degree of non-error or reliable behavior. The proposed framework does not replace the standard Hilbert-space formalism. Instead, it associates a neutrosophic descriptor (T, I, F) with quantum error events or families of error operators. We formulate neutrosophic quantum channels, neutrosophic error operators, neutrosophic code spaces, and a generalized Knill– Laflamme-type condition. A neutrosophic recovery map is then defined as a completely positive recovery operation supplemented by a consistent neutrosophic error classification. We prove several basic properties, including reduction to ordinary quantum error correction when the indeterminacy component vanishes and the error information becomes classical. Examples based on the bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and three-qubit repetition codes are given. We also formulate a neutrosophic syndrome formalism and discuss approximate correction, uncertain error probabilities, and possible extensions to stabilizer codes and fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Design of a polarization-based quantum key distribution link in a turbulent atmospheric channel
abstract: We present a design for polarization-encoded decoy-state quantum key distribution (QKD) using the BB84 protocol over a turbulent atmospheric channel. The transmitter uses a single 785nm laser, an intensity modulator for decoy-state preparation, and the iPOGNAC, a polarization encoder based on a fiber Sagnac interferometer, for stable polarization encoding. A 660nm beacon co-propagates with the quantum signal and provides pointing feedback for beam stabilization and a timing reference. At the receiver, a dichroic mirror directs the beacon to a sensing and synchronization subsystem, while the quantum signal enters a second iPOGNAC for active measurement-basis selection and detection by two single-photon avalanche detectors. A subsystem containing two fast-steering mirrors stabilizes fiber coupling. This architecture is intended to mitigate turbulence-induced pointing losses and reduce manual alignment. Relative to common four-laser transmitters and four-detector receivers, it also reduces component count and the aggregate detector dark-count rate. Its target repetition rate is on the order of 100MHz, limited primarily by detector dead time.

title: Multimodal Co-Generation With Continuous Bitstream Diffusion
abstract: We show that continuous bitstream diffusion (CoBit), originally developed for language modeling, provides a unified framework for joint and conditional multimodal generation using the same training and sampling protocol. Across image-text, speech-text and protein sequence-structure modeling, models are trained separately from scratch, but each uses a single input projection, transformer backbone, bitwise prediction head and binary score-matching objective shared across its modalities. Within each setting, a single checkpoint supports joint generation and the conditional directions included in training by changing which parts of the bitstream are observed. We first validate the approach on MNIST-Sum, a controlled image-text task pairing raw binary images with equations encoded as text, achieving near-perfect conditional accuracy and high joint consistency without learned tokenizers. We then apply the same protocol at larger scale to speech-text and protein sequence-structure modeling. Trained without text pretraining, a single speech-text model performs speech synthesis, recognition, continuation, and unconditional co-generation. Jointly generated speech and text achieve 3.5% word error rate between the generated text and automatic transcriptions of the generated speech. In protein modeling, a single CoBit checkpoint supports forward folding, inverse folding, and joint sequence-structure generation. For jointly generated proteins spanning 100-500 residues, computational refolding of CoBit's sequences yields structures that agree with the generated backbones at a mean self-consistency TM-score of 0.911. Together, these results show that CoBit provides a common generative framework for substantially different modalities and forms of cross-modal dependence, without introducing a domain-specific objective or sampling procedure.

title: MixedTruth: Component-Level Detection of Synthetic Speech and Synthetic Background in Mixed Audio
abstract: Modern generative audio can fabricate not only voices but also the acoustic environments that provide evidence of when and where speech occurred. This capability undermines a longstanding forensic assumption that background sound provides reliable evidence of a recording's provenance. Yet existing detectors produce only a single real-or-synthetic verdict, leaving analysts unable to determine whether the voice, the environment, or both were manipulated. In this paper, we propose a component-level forensic detector, namely TruMix, which classifies recordings into eight categories spanning the presence and authenticity of speech and background. TruMix has a unique multi-path architecture that jointly analyzes speech-oriented and background-oriented spectral evidence, contextual information from the mixed waveform, and low-level synthesis artifacts. This design avoids the artifact propagation inherent in conventional separate-then-detect pipelines while enabling generalization across independent speech and environmental-sound generators. We also curated MixedTruth, a 4,917-hour benchmark covering all eight categories under diverse mixing conditions. Extensive experiments show that TruMix achieves 98.51% AUC for component-level attribution, significantly outperforms ten state-of-the-art synthetic-speech detectors in conventional binary classification, and exhibits strong robustness across four attack tiers.

title: Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Ultrasound Images with Conformal Uncertainty Estimation
abstract: Thyroid nodules affect a large proportion of the general population. Although most are benign, a non-negligible fraction is malignant. Ultrasound imaging is the primary diagnostic modality, and accurate nodule segmentation is a prerequisite for CAD systems to classify malignancy and assess metastatic risk.\\ In this work, we propose a thyroid nodule segmentation framework that integrates a DeepLabV3+, channel-attention modules and post-hoc conformal prediction, providing both accurate mask and pixel-level uncertainty estimates. We address thyroid ultrasound nodule segmentation as the first stage of a pipeline that also includes malignancy classification and metastatic risk prediction. We adopt DeepLabV3+, whose Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) captures multi-scale context, with an EfficientNet-B5 backbone for its accuracy-efficiency trade-off. Additionally, we test three channel-attention modules: Squeeze-and-Excitation, CBAM and Grouped Channel Attention (GCA), paired with two loss formulations (Dice-BCE and Boundary).\\ Since binary masks do not indicate prediction confidence, we wrap the trained model with a split conformal prediction layer that produces pixel-level uncertainty maps with statistical coverage guarantees.\\ We evaluate all configurations on the TN3K public benchmark using a fixed split and directly compare them with state-of-the-art methods. The plain backbone already improves upon previously reported results, with CBAM + Dice-BCE emerging as the best overall configuration.

title: Understanding and Mitigating Cross-Session Attacks via Persistent Artifacts in Agent Skill Composition
abstract: Agent skills extend the capabilities of AI agents by bundling instructions, code, and resources into reusable packages. During skill execution, agents may produce or modify artifacts, such as files, configurations, and cached data, that are reused by other skills in later sessions. Since these artifacts can persist across sessions and later be accessed by other skills, they introduce a new attack surface that can be exploited to influence subsequent executions. However, the security risks arising from such cross-session skill interactions remain largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate cross-session composition attacks in skill-based AI agents and develop a runtime defense against them. Specifically, we characterize three attack mechanisms, namely Instruction Propagation (IP), Data Boundary Violation (DBV), and Evidence Poisoning (EP), through which malicious effects propagate across skill executions via persistent artifacts. To evaluate whether existing agents can resist these attacks while completing legitimate tasks, we construct SkillRelayBench, a benchmark of 270 adversarial cases drawn from 30 cross-session skill-composition scenarios across ten domains. Our evaluation of seven models across Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Claude Code reveals attack success rates (ASR) ranging from 46.7% to 77.4% and attack chain success rates (ACSR) ranging from 35.6% to 61.1%. Successful attack chains cover all five target security consequence categories, highlighting the broad impact of these attacks. To mitigate these risks, we propose SkillRelayGuard, which restores artifact provenance context and provides pre-execution advisory review while leaving the final execution decision to the agent. Evaluation across three agent settings shows that SkillRelayGuard reduces overall ASR from 69.5% to 10.9% and ACSR from 54.8% to 10.0%, while increasing legitimate task completion from 79.6% to 87.5%.

title: What Do Visual-Head Discovery Scores Actually Find? Attention Source, Necessity, and Random-Control Pitfalls in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Attention heads that attend to image regions relevant to a question are increasingly used to steer, ground and interpret vision-language models (VLMs) and to reduce their hallucinations. They are mostly found by ranking heads with an attention- pattern score and validated by steering or masking them. We ask how the choices inside such a discovery score shape the heads it returns, and which of the two validations identifies them. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct we vary the query type, the discovery corpus and the token positions whose attention is read (the attention source) in a full 2 x 3 x 2 design, and test all 12 head-sets for steerability (CERS: Contrastive Evidence-Region Steering score) and necessity (NCS: Necessity Con- trast Score) against layer-matched random head-sets. (1) The attention source and the query type reshape the selected heads far more than the corpus: changing the source keeps a median of 49 of the top-100 heads, the query 55 and the cor- pus 84, while two halves of the same data share 96-99. (2) Necessity follows the attention source: head-sets discovered from query-span attention are more nec- essary than last-token ones (difference 0.083, p=6 x 10^-10), and the two re- ferring + query-span sets lie 17-19 standard deviations above 250 layer-matched random sets (Holm-adjusted p=0.048). The referring + query-span effect re- plicates on several recent VLMs. (3) Steerability is not specific to the discovered heads: no discovered head-set steers better than its layer-matched random sets (rank p >= 0.14), and random sets drawn from the same or from any layer span the discovered sets' scores. Necessity therefore separates the discovery settings, while steering at this strength does not. We turn these findings into a protocol for reporting visual-head discoveries.

(2) Necessity follows the attention source: head-sets discovered from query-span attention are more nec- essary than last-token ones (difference 0.083, p=6 x 10^-10), and the two re- ferring + query-span sets lie 17-19 standard deviations above 250 layer-matched random sets (Holm-adjusted p=0.048). The referring + query-span effect re- plicates on several recent VLMs. (3) Steerability is not specific to the discovered heads: no discovered head-set steers better than its layer-matched random sets (rank p >= 0.14), and random sets drawn from the same or from any layer span the discovered sets' scores. Necessity therefore separates the discovery settings, while steering at this strength does not. We turn these findings into a protocol for reporting visual-head discoveries.

title: TopoLIA: Topology-Inspired Latent Interaction Attention for Drug Discovery
abstract: The growing sophistication of drug discovery calls for new advances in artificial intelligence (AI). Transformers have underpinned recent breakthroughs in AI, yet their conventional source-target attention mechanism can become a bottleneck for modeling complex interactions. Here, we introduce TopoLIA, a topology-inspired latent interaction attention mechanism that learns not only how much information should be exchanged between interaction partners, but also how that information should be transformed. Source-target-dependent attention is mediated through a compact latent interaction space, providing a structured representation of complex interactions. We further incorporate topological spectral representations to capture multiscale data geometry and extract algebraic relationships. TopoLIA thus incorporates topological principles into both data representation and neural network architecture. We demonstrate TopoLIA on protein-ligand binding, where persistent spectra encode multiscale topological and geometric patterns in 3D protein-ligand complexes, while latent interaction attention (LIA) enables structured, source-target-dependent information exchange. We pretrain TopoLIA by reconstructing masked multiscale spectral tokens from unlabeled molecular structures, yielding transferable structural representations without task-specific annotations. Across multiple scoring and docking benchmarks, TopoLIA achieves state-of-the-art performance and consistently outperforms its standard-attention counterpart. Rank analyses show that compact latent dimensions yield the best performance, supporting compact interaction spaces as an effective inductive bias for biomolecular learning. More broadly, LIA provides a general framework for structured, source-target-dependent information exchange that is applicable to diverse scientific and AI problems involving complex heterogeneous interactions.

title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming
abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies. We introduce the Weighted Variability Score (WVS), a robust multi-component metric that aggregates dispersion in normalized runtime, final optimality gap, LP iterations, and branch-and-bound nodes across repeated runs. On a large subset of MIPLIB 2017 instances, each solved in 100 randomized runs under a four-hour limit, WVS reveals a right-skewed distribution with a substantial upper tail: many instances are essentially stable, but some exhibit large variability that is not explained by basic properties alone. Notably, this experiment proved optimality for the open instance 'neos-5045105-creuse' in two SCIP runs. Using static descriptors and root-level features, a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift achieves a mean absolute error of 0.058 and Spearman rank correlation of 0.65 on a sealed test split. Feature-importance analysis highlights root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as the main drivers of high WVS. Because variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, our findings offer a practical tool for preemptive tuning and lay a foundation for fairer evaluation of new algorithms.

title: Towards Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: A Review of Perturbation and Backpropagation-Based Methods
abstract: Machine and deep learning algorithms have been proven their efficiency in the medical domain. This is particularly noticeable in medical imaging, where these algorithms have demonstrated exceptional capabilities, often surpassing human experts in detecting diseases, segmenting anatomical structures, and in aiding diagnosis. However, despite their high performance, the non-transparency of these models has raised concerns about trust and explainability, especially in critical domains, such as healthcare. Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a promising field that, aims to make the decision-making processes of AI systems more interpretable and understandable to humans. By offering clear, human-understandable justifications, XAI enhances clinicians' trust in AI-assisted decisions, and supports the safe integration of these technologies into clinical workflows. This paper focuses on perturbation-based and backpropagation-based explainability methods that are widely adopted for convolutional neural networks in medical imaging. We intend to provide deeper insight into the relevance of XAI methods in medical imaging. We propose a structured taxonomy that categorizes these methods into perturbation and backpropagation-based approaches. For each category, we highlight their respective strengths, limitations, and areas of applicability. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges hindering the adoption of XAI and identify promising research directions to bridge the gap between high-performance AI models and their responsible deployment in real-world healthcare environments.

title: SCOPE-RL: Reinforcement Learning with Executable Step-Level Verification for Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong reasoning performance through Chain-of-Thought (CoT), yet their autoregressive generation provides limited supervision over the correctness of intermediate steps. We introduce Step-wise Check Optimization for Process-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning (SCOPE-RL), a reinforcement learning framework that equips reasoning steps with executable mathematical checks. Each step is associated with a typed verification operator, such as symbolic equivalence, substitution, boundary evaluation, or range checking. Candidate checks are certified using reference solutions and controlled counterexamples to ensure both validity and discriminative ability. During reinforcement learning, these checks are executed directly on intermediate reasoning states to provide a process-level reward, which is combined with the final-answer reward under the standard GRPO framework. Experiments across multiple language models and mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that SCOPE-RL consistently improves accuracy over strong RLVR baselines while producing more verifiable and mathematically consistent reasoning trajectories.

title: Massively parallel universal nonlinear computing with diffractive surfaces
abstract: We introduce a diffractive optical computing framework that enables universal approximation of nonlinear functions using linear, passive optical components. By encoding the input variable into the phase of an optical wavefront and processing it through cascaded spatially engineered diffractive surfaces, independently defined nonlinear functions are computed in parallel at diffraction-limited output pixels. We theoretically prove universality for arbitrary bandlimited nonlinear functions and numerically demonstrate the approximation of one million nonlinear functions in parallel with negligible error. The framework is experimentally validated through in situ optical learning, demonstrating the simultaneous implementation of 35 nonlinear functions using a compact spatial light modulator-based setup.

title: Parallel photonic Ising machines enabled by spatial multiplexing
abstract: The spatial photonic Ising machine (SPIM) is a specialized computing system that solves large-scale combinatorial optimization problems by using spatial light modulation. In this work, we present methods for extending the capabilities of the SPIM through spatial multiplexing. Parallel processing by a multiplexing technique enables the computation of an Ising Hamiltonian based on a multicomponent model, which represents a variety of interaction matrices as a weighted sum of rank-one terms. In our approach, a spatially multiplexed SPIM implements this weighted sum and searches for an optimal solution to the knapsack problem. Moreover, parallel computation of multiple Ising Hamiltonians accelerates the optimization. These multiplexing strategies improve both the functionality and the search efficiency of the SPIM.

title: A small cognitive core explains human behavior at scale
abstract: Psychology has proposed many principles of cognition. Each, however, was developed in isolation, leaving their combined explanatory power unknown. We assembled a small set of established principles into one model, which we call COntextual Retrieval and Encoding (CORE). CORE consists of a hierarchy of episodic memories into which prediction errors are written and whose encoding, retrieval, and forgetting depend on context. Fitted jointly to 7,036,442 choices from 137 experiments, the model predicts human choices better than black-box models and reproduces 75% of reported behavioral effects when simulated. Moreover, its latent variables show classic signatures of Bayesian learning and event segmentation. Taken together, these findings suggest that a small cognitive core accounts for much of human behavior. They also open a path toward making psychology more than the sum of its parts, by building computational models on the entire experimental record.

title: PDE-PFN: Prior-Data Fitted Neural PDE Solver
abstract: Motivated by the success of large language models (LLMs) with broad generalizability and robustness to noisy or unreliable pre-training data, we explore in-context prediction of PDE solution fields using approximate pre-training data. In addition, inspired by the posterior predictive mean-based inference mechanism of the in-context learning in prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), we propose PDE-PFN, a prior-data fitted neural solver that approximates the posterior predictive mean of PDE solutions via in-context learning. PDE-PFN builds on a PFN architecture with self- and cross-attention mechanisms of Transformer and is pre-trained on noisy approximate solutions generated by physics-informed neural networks, serving as diverse but not necessarily exact priors. Through experiments on a range of two-dimensional PDEs, we demonstrate that PDE-PFN achieves empirical generalization across heterogeneous equations, robustness under noisy priors, and zero-gradient-update in-context inference capability. PDE-PFN achieves competitive or improved predictive accuracy relative to the evaluated baselines while supporting flexible context and query representations.

title: Percolation of Data Constraints and Reorganization of Boolean Function States in Parity Learning
abstract: We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its $\pm1$ entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity $K_f=1/\textrm{Tr}(ρ_A^2)$ is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.

title: 机器发现的三定律:为什么 AGI 必须是复数的
abstract: 观点论文初稿 v0.1;未经同行评审。本文记录包含中文与英文两个版本。首次公开:2026-10-09。 Position paper, draft v0.1; not peer reviewed. This record contains Chinese and English editions. First published: 2026-10-09. 摘要主流的 AGI 想象是单数的:一个足够大的模型,最终在一切领域超过一切人。本文认为,这幅图景误解了新知识是如何产生的。我们把 AGI 狭义地理解为“在训练分布之外产生可验证新知识的能力”,并从三条可被反驳的公理出发——学习系统受其先验约束;新知识在诞生时是反共识的;生成廉价而检验昂贵——推出机器发现的三条定律。(一)认知惯性:一个心智若不受成形方式不同的心智作用,将停留在其先验之内,因此能发现的 AGI 必然是复数的。(二)猜想:对共识的偏离需要被许可的大胆猜想,抑制一切低概率输出等于取消发现。(三)反作用:每一个断言都必须遭遇相当的反向检验;发现速度受检验能力约束,而且检验越昂贵,多样性越重要。我们综合科学社会学、社会认识论、组织研究与社会心理学的证据,以及大模型日益同质化的最新实证,论证这三条定律的合理性;讨论六种反驳;提出六条可证伪的预测和一个实践者田野观察方案。本文的含义是:AI 发展的目标应是一个由不同训练谱系的模型与人共同组成的认识生态,而不是一个单体;训练谱系的多样性应被当作公共品来维护。 AbstractThe dominant picture of artificial general intelligence is singular: one model that eventually surpasses everyone at everything. We argue that this picture misdescribes how new knowledge is produced. Defining AGI narrowly as the capacity to produce verifiable knowledge beyond one’s training distribution, we start from three defeasible axioms (learning systems are bounded by their priors; new knowledge is anti-consensus at birth; generation is cheap while verification is costly) and derive three laws of machine discovery. (I) Cognitive inertia: a mind stays within its prior unless acted upon by a differently formed mind; discovery-capable AGI is therefore plural. (II) Conjecture: departure from consensus requires licensed, bold conjecture; suppressing all low-probability output suppresses discovery. (III) Reaction: every assertion must meet an equal and opposite test; discovery is bounded by verification throughput, and the more expensive verification is, the more diversity matters. We support these laws with evidence from the sociology of science, social epistemology, organization studies and social psychology, and with recent evidence that large language models are becoming homogeneous. We address six objections, state six falsifiable predictions, and describe a practitioner field protocol. The implication is that AI development should aim at an epistemic ecology of differently trained models and humans, and that diversity of training lineages should be treated as a public good.

First published: 2026-10-09. 摘要主流的 AGI 想象是单数的:一个足够大的模型,最终在一切领域超过一切人。本文认为,这幅图景误解了新知识是如何产生的。我们把 AGI 狭义地理解为“在训练分布之外产生可验证新知识的能力”,并从三条可被反驳的公理出发——学习系统受其先验约束;新知识在诞生时是反共识的;生成廉价而检验昂贵——推出机器发现的三条定律。(一)认知惯性:一个心智若不受成形方式不同的心智作用,将停留在其先验之内,因此能发现的 AGI 必然是复数的。(二)猜想:对共识的偏离需要被许可的大胆猜想,抑制一切低概率输出等于取消发现。(三)反作用:每一个断言都必须遭遇相当的反向检验;发现速度受检验能力约束,而且检验越昂贵,多样性越重要。我们综合科学社会学、社会认识论、组织研究与社会心理学的证据,以及大模型日益同质化的最新实证,论证这三条定律的合理性;讨论六种反驳;提出六条可证伪的预测和一个实践者田野观察方案。本文的含义是:AI 发展的目标应是一个由不同训练谱系的模型与人共同组成的认识生态,而不是一个单体;训练谱系的多样性应被当作公共品来维护。 AbstractThe dominant picture of artificial general intelligence is singular: one model that eventually surpasses everyone at everything. We argue that this picture misdescribes how new knowledge is produced. Defining AGI narrowly as the capacity to produce verifiable knowledge beyond one’s training distribution, we start from three defeasible axioms (learning systems are bounded by their priors; new knowledge is anti-consensus at birth; generation is cheap while verification is costly) and derive three laws of machine discovery. (I) Cognitive inertia: a mind stays within its prior unless acted upon by a differently formed mind; discovery-capable AGI is therefore plural. (II) Conjecture: departure from consensus requires licensed, bold conjecture; suppressing all low-probability output suppresses discovery. (III) Reaction: every assertion must meet an equal and opposite test; discovery is bounded by verification throughput, and the more expensive verification is, the more diversity matters. We support these laws with evidence from the sociology of science, social epistemology, organization studies and social psychology, and with recent evidence that large language models are becoming homogeneous. We address six objections, state six falsifiable predictions, and describe a practitioner field protocol. The implication is that AI development should aim at an epistemic ecology of differently trained models and humans, and that diversity of training lineages should be treated as a public good.

title: Mechanical Compatibility, Pre-Intervention Content Binding and Provenance Direction: A Synthetic F0–F5 Audit — BIT-REALITY-KNOWLEDGE-001
abstract: English abstract This report archives the terminal audit of BIT-REALITY-KNOWLEDGE-001, separating mechanical compatibility, temporal evidence and knowledge-provenance direction. In a locked synthetic two-model sled fixture, a prescribed post-load velocity interval is compatible with M_coast and excludes M_comp. This is a model-class result, not an identification of a unique real-world mechanism. A late verified receipt does not establish a pre-intervention prediction. Independent pre-intervention seals support the control workflow only under declared fixture assumptions. The F3 audit preserves a false acceptance by the historical F2 implementation when two differently named stores share effective editing authority. An external immutable anchor W binds the D/S content pair before intervention under synthetic trust assumptions, but does not establish that A and B were separately sealed in the required order. Two histories with the same accessible record retain different sealing-order truths; P_SHARED+W therefore remains HOLD_LOCK_ORDER and HOLD_DIRECTION. Mathematics-to-physics and physics-to-mathematics labels concern each branch's evidence chronology, not a claim that mathematics causes physical laws. No actual sled measurements, real timestamp verification, real anchors, general theorem or novelty priority is established. The supplement preserves the prelock note, F0–F4 reports and F5 DOCX unchanged, including embedded historical code and negative results. REL-001 performs archive integrity and publication preparation only; it does not rerun scientific checks or reopen F0–F5. Tóm tắt tiếng Việt Báo cáo lưu trữ kiểm toán terminal BIT-REALITY-KNOWLEDGE-001, giữ riêng tương thích cơ học, chứng cứ thời gian và hướng nguồn gốc tri thức. Trong fixture xe trượt tổng hợp với hai mô hình đã khóa, khoảng vận tốc sau tải được stipulate tương thích với M_coast và loại M_comp; kết quả không xác lập cơ chế duy nhất của thế giới. Biên nhận hậu ký không chứng nhận dự báo trước can thiệp. Đối chứng niêm phong độc lập chỉ hỗ trợ hướng quy trình theo giả định fixture. Kiểm toán F3 bảo toàn lỗi false accept của mã F2 lịch sử khi hai kho khác tên cùng quyền sửa có hiệu lực. Bản neo ngoài W ràng buộc cặp nội dung D/S trước can thiệp theo các giả định tin cậy tổng hợp, nhưng không xác minh A rồi B được khóa riêng. Hai lịch có cùng hồ sơ đọc được vẫn có sự thật thứ tự khóa khác nhau; P_SHARED+W tiếp tục HOLD_LOCK_ORDER và HOLD_DIRECTION. Các nhãn Toán→Lý và Lý→Toán chỉ thuộc lịch chứng cứ của từng nhánh. Không có phép đo xe, timestamp hay bản neo thật; tính mới và định lý tổng quát chưa được xác lập. Phụ lục giữ nguyên byte bản prelock, báo cáo F0–F4 và DOCX F5, kể cả mã lịch sử và kết quả âm. REL-001 chỉ kiểm toàn vẹn và chuẩn bị công bố, không chạy lại kiểm khoa học hoặc mở lại F0–F5. Existing third-party notices and terms remain applicable. Historical F0–F5 bytes and scientific verdicts are unchanged.

title: Multi-Level Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient reinforcement learning for safety-constrained trajectory optimization of collaborative industrial robots
abstract: Collaborative robots operating in modern manufacturing environments require trajectory planning strategies that simultaneously support efficiency, adaptability, and operational safety. This study proposes a Multi-Level Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (ML-DDPG) framework for safety-constrained trajectory optimization. The framework combines a strategic waypoint level, a continuous DDPG motion-control policy, and a reactive feasibility projection that corrects unsafe actions before execution. The trajectory-planning problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process with reward terms for goal progress, obstacle clearance, smoothness, energy, execution time, and safety. Descriptive experiments in a custom PyTorch-based three-dimensional environment compare ML-DDPG with conventional planners and the DDPG, TD3, and SAC baselines. In the retained single training run, ML-DDPG produced observed values of 98.7% success, 1.08 mm trajectory error, a 0.98 smoothness index, and no recorded collision. These values are single-run observations and are not means over independent seeds; variability and statistical significance cannot be estimated from the available record. The exported traces show faster reward growth within the 200-episode budget, and the single-run ablation record associates the largest observed gains with the combined multi-level, reward, and projection components. One UR5e demonstration yielded 0.018 m mean tracking error, 0.042 m maximum tracking error, and no collision in that trial. A separate ABB welding sequence is included only as qualitative feasibility evidence because synchronized trajectory, force, and weld-quality logs were unavailable. The findings motivate further evaluation, while multi-seed training, repeated hardware trials, complete reporting of evaluation procedures, and cross-platform validation remain necessary before broader generalization.

title: РАЗРАБОТКА МЕТОДА И АЛГОРИТМОВ АДАПТИВНОГО ФЕДЕРАТИВНОГО ОБУЧЕНИЯ С УЧЕТОМ РАСПРЕДЕЛЕННОГО ЗАПАЗДЫВАНИЯ КЛИЕНТСКИХ ОБНОВЛЕНИЙ
abstract: При федеративном обучении с неоднородными клиентскими данными и переменными задержками запоздавшие обновления могут ухудшать качество модели, а обмен параметрами с глобальным сервером увеличивает сетевую нагрузку. Целью исследования является разработка и теоретико-экспериментальное обоснование метода и алгоритмов адаптивного федеративного обучения с учетом распределенного запаздывания клиентских обновлений. Для обоснования разрабатываемых решений использованы событийная и непрерывная модели градиентных обновлений, спектральный анализ устойчивости, вероятностные оценки возраста и расхождения обновлений, а также оценка изменения градиента по кривизне функции потерь. Получены характеристическое уравнение и условие определения критического шага обучения. Разработан метод с выбором шага обучения и числа локальных шагов, оценивающий применимость запаздывающих обновлений. Предложены алгоритмы иерархического агрегирования с проверкой совместимости результатов и инкрементального дерева решений с раздельной адаптацией параметров и структуры. Вычислительные сравнения подтвердили сокращение передачи данных при выполнении ограничений качества и эффективность отбора обновлений. Поэтапным отключением компонентов оценен их вклад в качество обучения и ресурсные затраты. Полученные результаты подтверждают применимость решений при переменных задержках в условиях неоднородности клиентских данных.

title: Artificial Intelligence Model’s assessment of intra-sample heterogeneity of HER2 IHC in breast cancer is related to interobserver and intraobserver agreement among pathologists
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate assessment of HER2 status in breast cancer has been critical for guiding therapy and has become even more important with the emergence of antibody-drug conjugates, now also indicated in HER2-low tumors. However, inter- and intraobserver variability limits the reproducibility of HER2 IHC scoring among pathologists, particularly at the lower end of the expression spectrum. Artificial intelligence (AI) models offer potential to standardize and improve diagnostic accuracy and bring new insights into current practices shortcomings. Methods We conducted a study recruiting generalist and specialist pathologists from Rede D’Or centers across Brazil to assess digitized HER2 IHC whole slide images. The same images were presented for the pathologists with the interval of one month and to the AIM-HER2 (PathAI ®, Boston, MA) AI model. Intra- and interobserver agreement, as well as concordance with AI, were measured across 126 breast cancer samples. The association between sample features and agreement metrics was also analyzed using AI spatial breakdown data. Results Among 34 pathologists, median intraobserver concordance was 67.68% and median concordance with AI was 60.8%. Median interobserver agreement was 67.65%, with high agreement (> 85%) in 25.4% of samples. Significant positive correlations were observed among all agreement metrics. Samples with lower intra-sample heterogeneity, as determined by AI spatial breakdown scores, were associated with higher agreement levels. Conclusions Our findings highlight significant variability in HER2 IHC scoring among pathologists. AI models such as AIM-HER2 can be used to increase reproducibility of analysis and also to indicate the most difficult samples that can result in diagnostic discordance. We found that AI assessed intra-sample heterogeneity is correlated with a lower agreement rate among pathologists.

title: Exploring the Latent Structure of AMD Severity Using Retinal Foundation Models
abstract: Retinal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of ophthalmic tasks, yet relatively little is known about how disease-related information is represented within their learned embeddings and whether this distribution influences downstream prediction performance. In this work, we use Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) as a case study to investigate how disease severity is represented within the embedding space of RET-CLIP, a retinal vision-language foundation model, using bilateral fundus images from the AREDS dataset, benchmarked against non-retinal encoders. We first characterize the distribution of AMD severity within the learned representation space and then evaluate how this structure influences classification performance across three clinically relevant task formulations of increasing granularity. Finally, we analyze the most influential latent dimensions combining feature attribution, statistical phenotype association, and qualitative image analyses. Our results show that RET-CLIP represents AMD severity as a continuous spectrum rather than a set of discrete categories, with healthy and advanced disease stages exhibiting clearer separation than intermediate ones. This organization was reflected in downstream performance, which decreased from a balanced accuracy of 0.844 and 0.814 for binary AMD and Late-AMD detection respectively to 0.446 for six-class grading. Furthermore, the most influential latent dimensions were statistically associated to distinct retinal phenotypes, including drusen accumulation, pigmentary alterations, and advanced retinal lesions. These findings suggest that the structure of retinal foundation-model representations influences the difficulty of clinically relevant prediction tasks and demonstrate the potential of representation-level analysis for understanding disease organization and improving interpretability.

title: How Should We Evaluate Naturalness for Synthetic Speech with a Foreign Accent?
abstract: Recent advances in speech synthesis technology have enabled the generation of speech with diverse characteristics. One such characteristic is a foreign accent. In our preliminary experiments, we found that UTMOS, a widely used automatic speech quality assessment system, tended to assign lower scores to speech with stronger foreign accents, even though it is produced by a human speaker. This observation raised a question: How do humans evaluate the naturalness of foreign-accented speech? We conducted a large-scale subjective evaluation involving both native and non-native listeners under different evaluation instructions. The results showed that humans also considered accentedness when evaluating naturalness, but that defining naturalness in terms of human-likeness and selecting raters who have greater exposure to the target accent may enable more appropriate evaluation. This study aims to provide a starting point for future discussions on fairer and more appropriate evaluation of synthetic speech with a foreign accent.

This study aims to provide a starting point for future discussions on fairer and more appropriate evaluation of synthetic speech with a foreign accent.

title: The Moment Ladder: Exact Integer Checksums that Certify, Locate, and Fill
abstract: A string of digits, a frame, a tile of a matrix product, any list of integers, carries a ladder of exact totals: the plain sum T, the position-weighted sum W, the quadratic sum Q, the cubic C, and onward. This paper states the laws of that ladder and proves them by algebra and by exhaustive computation. Each rung stamps damage with an exact integer signature. The first m totals cannot all be silenced by a change touching at most m cells, which is the ladder theorem, a Vandermonde argument in plain integers, and the same argument read the other way fills m holes at known positions exactly. One wrong cell names itself: T is the error, W/T the position, Q = T·c² the confirmation, and with the quadratic rung the named cell is unique. Two or three wrong cells on a line are solved by the Prony recurrence in exact integers. The identity behind every use is linear: the ladder of a matrix product is predicted from its inputs, row moments of A·B equal A·(B·w) for any fixed weight vector w, so the columns may carry any fixed sign pattern without changing a theorem, and splitting an index into residue classes gives independent witness families that are the Chinese-remainder box of the ring seen on a tile. On the Fibonacci 60-ring the ladder is the ring's own arithmetic. The split Lucien Khan noticed in 2013, the sixty digits summing to 280 with the first thirty at 128 and the second thirty at 152, is its zeroth rung, the ring's constants 280, 8,760 and 344,660 repair all 540 single-digit corruptions with no reference copy, and every ring of the shell family carries the same stamps with its own half-period. On the ring itself one struck digit is already named by its rectangle, the twin grid of the system paper, with no total consulted, and the smallest damage that keeps every rectangle relation, a swap on all four corners, is stamped by W on the even rectangles and by Q on the odd ones. Every law is re-verified by enumeration when this document is built, and every number quoted from a companion paper is checked against that paper's archived record. The architectures built on these laws, frames, the fractal tower, the cube, the compute guard and the training guard, are the companion paper The Self-Healing Tower. How much they repair, and why, is the companion paper The Scaling Law.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF NEUROMORPHIC SILICON PHOTONIC INTELLIGENCE Unifying Chip Physics, Optical Computing, and Algorithmic Cognition for the Post-Electronic Era
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Neuromorphic Silicon Photonic Intelligence unifies silicon photonics, neuromorphic engineering, and algorithmic cognition to overcome von Neumann and thermodynamic bottlenecks. It proposes the Photonic Neural Silicon Chip (PNSC), executing deep learning matrix multiplications at light-speed via integrated interferometers. To ensure analog precision, it employs Noise-Aware Training, injecting hardware noise into digital backward passes. Scalability is achieved through WDM broadcast-and-weight topologies (O(N) footprint) and athermal tuning to eliminate parasitic power. Central is the Silicon Photonic Intelligence Index: SPII=(P×A×C×T)/[(P×A×C×T)+D×E+ε]. Under the Weakest-Link Axiom, it proves photonic intelligence requires simultaneous optimization of photonic, algorithmic, integrative, and thermodynamic dimensions. Guided by the Asymptotic Perfection Principle (max ~0.9901, reflecting the Landauer limit), it provides a definitive blueprint for sustainable, light-speed AI.

title: dnalang-core 0.3.0: circuit lineage on the run ledger
abstract: dnalang-core is a small language (dna::}{::lang) and toolchain for writing quantum circuits as genomes, evolving them, and running them with a hash-chained ledger written before every hardware submission. Version 0.3.0 records circuit lineage on that ledger: each generation of an evolutionary search appends, for every genome, the operator that produced it, its parents, its fitness and optionally its compiled circuit's SHA-256; hardware candidates are recorded as proposed, with their surrogate score, before submission; dnalang trace-lineage walks a genome's ancestry and refuses a ledger whose chain does not verify. Recording does not change the search. The ledger module is unchanged from 0.2.0. Verified: 36 tests pass and ruff is clean on Python 3.12, offline, on the released tree. Python 3.10 and 3.11 were not run. Version 0.2.0 was deposited as a snapshot inside 10.5281/zenodo.23087554.

title: Design and Implementation of a Telegram-Based Conversational AI Agent for Automated Personal Expense Management Using Large Language Models and Google Sheets
abstract: Manual logging of day-to-day personal expenses is often abandoned by users because it requires them to open a dedicated spreadsheet or application and enter data in a rigid, structured format. This paper presents the design and implementation of a conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent that allows a user to record and retrieve personal expenses simply by chatting in natural language through the Telegram messaging platform. The system is built using the n8n low-code automation platform and combines a Telegram Trigger node, an AI Agent powered by an OpenAI Chat Model, a Simple Memory module for conversational context, and two Google Sheets tools, namely Read Expenses and Add Expense, that allow the agent to write new expense records to, and retrieve existing records from, a connected Google Sheet. When a user sends a message such as "I spent Rs.231 for Medicine today," the agent extracts the expense description, amount, and date, appends the entry to the spreadsheet, and returns a natural-language confirmation. The agent can also generate an on-demand categorized daily summary. The proposed system was implemented and tested with real conversational data, and the results demonstrate that the agent accurately parses free-form expense statements, updates the backend spreadsheet correctly, and produces coherent, human-readable summaries, thereby lowering the friction traditionally associated with manual expense tracking.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning for Multilingual Edge Translation
abstract: Multilingual edge translation must transfer knowledge across uneven language resources while controlling uncertainty and communication. Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning (MT-BayesFL) combines a shared six-layer Transformer encoder, target-specific decoders, lightweight adapters, and matrix-normal posteriors. The refined formulation separates Gaussian pooling from separable covariance approximation, preserves positive-definite sampling factors, and applies error feedback before sparse transmission. An adaptive projected-moment variant adds bounded reliability weights, between-client disagreement, and participation-dependent shrinkage. Reference-system results span eight English-to-target directions and five reported seeds. Low-resource macro BLEU is 26.0 versus 22.6 for FedMTL, with a 3.43-BLEU gain calculated from pairwise means. English-Swahili reaches 28.3 BLEU and expected calibration error 0.082. BLEU retention is 92.1% at 30% dropout; normalized retention over 0-40% dropout is 94.54%. Communication is 1.8 MB per round, 70.5% below the dense-upload ablation, and personalization improves by 4.5 BLEU on average. The parameter-efficient comparator remains stronger on English-Chinese. Numerical checks verify covariance and residual invariants; translation gains from the refinement remain unmeasured. These results support uncertainty-aware sharing for imbalanced multilingual clients, subject to configuration-matched evaluation.

title: Continuous-Time Cloth Dynamics with Physics-Informed Neural ODEs
abstract: We present ContinuousCloth, a continuous-time, physics-informed neural solver for deformable cloth dynamics that enforces a spring--mass ODE within a neural trajectory model. Unlike classical time-stepping simulators that return trajectories only on a discrete integration grid, ContinuousCloth supports querying at arbitrary timestamps and computing displacement, velocity, and acceleration via automatic differentiation. We evaluate ContinuousCloth along two dimensions. In a physics-only setting, ContinuousCloth achieves trajectory accuracy comparable to high-precision solvers across six diverse boundary-condition scenarios while reducing runtime by up to 17.4 times. When fused with sparse and noisy observations, the spring--mass ODE acts as a strong inductive bias for downstream tasks: interpolation and parameter estimation. That is, ContinuousCloth reduces interpolation error by 7.3 times over a data-only neural baseline in simulation and 2.4 times on real-world cloth sequences, and achieves 2.6 times lower parameter error than a differentiable-solver baseline under high-noise conditions, demonstrating consistent robustness under realistic measurement imperfections.

title: Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems
abstract: To balance task performance and computational cost, agentic workflows can use a lower-cost model for execution and selectively consult a stronger model. In such executor-advisor systems, the executor decides when to seek advice, making escalation depend on self-assessment, although current language models struggle to detect where their own reasoning fails. The need for stronger reasoning emerges during execution and varies across workflow phases. We introduce ARIA, a meta-controller that learns when to consult by balancing task success against consultation cost. Our approach formulates consultation as a sequential resource-allocation problem. At workflow contact points, ARIA maps execution evidence to a compact state abstraction and selects SILENT or CONSULT, with action values learned by Monte Carlo control from cost-penalized outcomes. Across evaluated tasks of SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and $τ^2$-bench, ARIA recovers 44-81% of the executor-advisor success gap at less than half the advisor model's cost. ARIA achieves the best observed success-cost trade-off among ten other evaluated conditions, including routing and cascading methods, fixed and prompted consultation, and random placement at matched advice volume. The policies are compact and inspectable, with a single consultation-price parameter governing the success-cost trade-off without retraining either underlying model.

title: Robust Vision-Language Navigation with Awareness of Instruction-Execution Progress
abstract: In Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) tasks involving multi-step instructions as guidance, an agent must associate its observations with the relevant instruction content at each decision point. Most graph-based methods commonly match candidate trajectories with the entire instruction, allowing already executed content to interfere with subsequent decisions. Although instruction-execution progress provides a direct cue for separating executed and pending content, existing progress estimation approaches often rely on explicit progress supervision, sophisticated progress-learning stages, or costly online reasoning with LLMs. In this paper, we propose a robust VLN framework with Awareness of Instruction-Execution Progress (VLN-AIEP), which couples progress estimation with navigation decision-making. VLN-AIEP associates the visited trajectory with the instruction to suppress embeddings corresponding to executed content, and then matches candidate locations with the pending content. This coupling makes correct navigation decisions depend on accurate progress estimation, allowing the progress estimator to learn directly from navigation decision labels without explicit progress annotations. To support progress estimation, we construct a landmark-anchored trajectory representation that encodes the semantic labels and viewpoint-relative geometry of instruction-referred landmarks. These landmarks serve as spatial references for associating the visited trajectory with executed instruction content. Extensive experiments on R2R, RxR, CVDN, and R2R-CE demonstrate that the proposed method achieves favorable performance across multiple metrics.

title: From Generative AI to Hotel Brand Advocacy: A Proposed Research Framework
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly involved in travel planning and hotel choice, yet research has not fully explained how consumers move from evaluating an AI-generated recommendation to responding to the hotel brand being recommended. This paper develops an integrated research framework that connects GenAI-related perceptions with recommendation acceptance and hotel brand advocacy intention. The framework distinguishes two psychological routes. A motivational route links GenAI anthropomorphism with GenAI-evoked inspiration, whereas an evaluative route links recommendation credibility and relevance with trust in GenAI recommendations. Inspiration and trust are subsequently proposed to increase recommendation acceptance, which is further associated with advocacy intention toward the recommended hotel brand. The framework also proposes that lack-of-transparency anxiety weakens the positive effect of GenAI anthropomorphism on inspiration. The Stimulus - Organism - Response (S-O-R) framework provides the overall structure, while customer inspiration, affordance - actualization, fear-acquisition, and commitment - consistency perspectives explain specific relationships. Eight hypotheses are developed, together with a pathway for future empirical validation using a survey of GenAI users and partial least squares structural equation modeling. The framework extends GenAI hospitality research by connecting recommendation-level psychological responses with a downstream hotel-brand outcome.

title: Pick Aggregator: A Multimodel Ensemble of Machine Learning Pickers to Generate an Onshore–Offshore Seismic Catalog for Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands
abstract: Abstract Offshore seismic swarms north of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands remain poorly characterized due to limited azimuthal coverage from the inland Puerto Rico Seismic Network (network code PR). Here, we integrate data from six U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) ocean-bottom seismometers (ZZ network, mid-2015 to mid-2016) with the PR network using a novel multimodel ensemble approach for machine learning (ML) phase picking, named pick aggregator. ML pickers have automated rapid seismic phase detection, but their performance degrades when applied to data that differ significantly from training datasets. Onshore–offshore experiments with sparse station coverage, complex instrumentation, and lower signal-to-noise ratios provide a challenge. The pick aggregator performs multidomain parallel computations on the SeisBench platform to catalog seismic phases across eight ML model combinations pretrained on ocean and land data. We then aggregate seismic picks identified by at least two models and associate them using a Gaussian Mixture Model Associator. The 1-yr ensemble ML catalog includes 10,948 events, composed of 55,704 P wave and 33,899 S wave picks, with mean probabilities of 0.65 and 0.64, respectively. The ZZ network substantially improves offshore azimuthal coverage and provides thousands of near-source seismic phases (25% of the P wave and 28% of the S wave picks). The relocated-ML catalog with >5.3 M added differential times includes 8025 events (115.8% increase compared with the relocated USGS catalog using the same stations). The relocated-ML catalog reveals an intense seismic swarm in the north-northwest direction southeast of the Main ridge at 20–40 km depth that aligns with the fast shear-wave polarization of previous studies, suggesting an incipient slab tear near 65.1° W. Seismicity depth variations along the strike indicate a steeper western segment with a wider depth range and a retreating eastern segment, supporting a differential rollback mechanism. Our multimodel ensemble approach mitigates inconsistencies among ML pickers pretrained on different datasets, enabling superior performance and robust phase detection in diverse tectonic environments with varying signal characteristics.

title: Probability-based thresholding for guided perturbation sampling in XAI
abstract: Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) is a visual explainability model that is used in explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) systems to understand the decision behavior of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). LIME is a perturbation-based model; hence, it suffers from instability-of-explainability problems due to run-to-run variability in feature ranking. We have addressed this problem recently using a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm to guide perturbation sampling and propose an adaptive MCMC-LIME visual explainer. However, MCMC introduces new challenges that include slow convergence to target distribution and high autocorrelation between samples that may introduce uncertainty across complementary learning models. MCMC generally navigates in high-probability regions, leading to difficulties switching to other high-probability regions that are important contributors to stabilizing visual explainers. This paper proposes an improved MCMCLIME that can function effectively in the recently proposed Colony of AI framework, a specialized multi-agent AI system that integrates three complementary learner AI agents (fast, detailed, and organized). The improved MCMC-LIME introduces a probability-based thresholding to control guided perturbation sampling and stabilize MCMC-LIME across learner AI agents. An experiment is conducted using a Samoyed dog image from Oxford- IIIT Pet dataset with seven independent runs per model. It uses VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 models that are labeled as fast, detailed, and organized learner AI agents in colony of AI. Experimental results, evaluated using the Average Rank Similarity (ARS) scores and averaging across five independent ARS evaluations per model, show LIME achieves ARS scores of (0.92, 0.75, 0.83) for the three types of learner AI agents, respectively. Similarly, MCMC-LIME achieves (0.95, 0.80, 0.91) ARS scores. However, the improved MCMC-LIME leads to (0.98, 0.86, 0.98) ARS scores, respectively, indicating about 6.5%, 14.7%, and 18.1% improvement across learner AI agents from the original LIME explainer. As such, the probability-based thresholding guides perturbation sampling efficiently and improves performance of XAI.

However, MCMC introduces new challenges that include slow convergence to target distribution and high autocorrelation between samples that may introduce uncertainty across complementary learning models. MCMC generally navigates in high-probability regions, leading to difficulties switching to other high-probability regions that are important contributors to stabilizing visual explainers. This paper proposes an improved MCMCLIME that can function effectively in the recently proposed Colony of AI framework, a specialized multi-agent AI system that integrates three complementary learner AI agents (fast, detailed, and organized). The improved MCMC-LIME introduces a probability-based thresholding to control guided perturbation sampling and stabilize MCMC-LIME across learner AI agents. An experiment is conducted using a Samoyed dog image from Oxford- IIIT Pet dataset with seven independent runs per model. It uses VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 models that are labeled as fast, detailed, and organized learner AI agents in colony of AI. Experimental results, evaluated using the Average Rank Similarity (ARS) scores and averaging across five independent ARS evaluations per model, show LIME achieves ARS scores of (0.92, 0.75, 0.83) for the three types of learner AI agents, respectively. Similarly, MCMC-LIME achieves (0.95, 0.80, 0.91) ARS scores. However, the improved MCMC-LIME leads to (0.98, 0.86, 0.98) ARS scores, respectively, indicating about 6.5%, 14.7%, and 18.1% improvement across learner AI agents from the original LIME explainer. As such, the probability-based thresholding guides perturbation sampling efficiently and improves performance of XAI.

title: Opto-electronic programmable activation function generation circuit for photonic computing
abstract: I propose and report an opto-electronic circuit for photonic computing, which generates various kinds of activation functions including tanh and rectified linear unit (ReLU) in response to the electric field of an input signal. The circuit is composed of a symmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI), a balanced photodetector (PD), and an MZI-based optical intensity modulator. When two coherent lightwaves (input and control signals) are input into the symmetric MZI, the optical output of the intensity modulator, which is driven with the electrical output of the balanced PD set after the symmetric MZI, produces various kinds of activation responses to the input signal by setting a diode and/or changing the amplitude and phase of the control signal.

title: Introduction to using symbolic regression for interpretable machine learning in healthcare
abstract: The past decade has seen machine learning play an increasingly important role in medicine. However, many of the state-of-the-art models being developed and deployed suffer from a lack of transparency, limiting integration into the clinical decision-making process and raising concerns about patient safety. Here we call attention to symbolic regression, a largely overlooked machine learning technique that aims to be both accurate and interpretable by learning readable mathematical models from data. In recent years, it has undergone rapid advancements with successful application to problems across a wide range of disciplines. In this perspective, we provide an approachable introduction to symbolic regression, highlight its strengths and limitations, and explore its potential applications in medicine.

title: STREGO: A Scalable Implementation of a Trust-Region Framework for Noisy Bayesian Optimization
abstract: TREGO, a trust-region Bayesian optimization (BO) method for expensive blackbox problems, has convergence guarantees, but only for exact function values. In high dimension, its performance tends to deteriorate. This paper asks whether a trust-region BO method can be extended to handle noisy evaluations while being competitive in high dimension. We first generalize TREGO into a trust-region framework for noisy BO and extend its convergence analysis to noisy function estimates that are sufficiently accurate with sufficiently high probability. We then propose STREGO, a scalable implementation of this framework. Its global phase selects a batch of candidates by solving a bi-objective problem on the posterior mean of a Gaussian process and the integrated variance reduction. Unlike the predictive variance, this second objective does not favor boundary points merely because they are far from the data. Its local phase minimizes the posterior mean of a second Gaussian process, trained only on points close to the incumbent. STREGO is compared with TREGO, TURBO, BAXUS and NSMA-BO on synthetic and real-world problems of dimension $4$ to $124$, with and without noise. It gives the best average results in every synthetic setting tested and the best or tied-best solution on four of the six real-world problems. An implementation of STREGO is available at https://github.com/Mayousk/STREGO.
