title: التطبيقية: الإنتاجية الذكية وهندسة البرمجيات ChatGPTموسوعة
abstract: يقدم هذا المستند "موسوعة ChatGPT التطبيقية: الإنتاجية الذكية وهندسة البرمجيات" (من إعداد د. عابدة الحناوي) دليلاً علمياً وعملياً شاملاً لاستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي وتطبيقاته في هندسة الأوامر، أتمتة المهام، ودورة تطوير البرمجيات. يتكون المرجع المرفق من أربعة أدلة علمية وتطبيقية رئيسية تغطي جوانب مختلفة لاستخدام ChatGPT والذكاء الاصطناعي: 1. دليل ChatGPT للاحتراف العملي (الدليل العام) يركز على إتقان الأساسيات وهندسة الأوامر واستخدام الميزات المتقدمة: المقدمة والأساسيات: التعريف بنموذج ChatGPT، كيفية إنشاء الحساب، الواجهة الرئيسية، الفرق بين النماذج المتوفرة ($GPT-4o$, $GPT-4o\ mini$, $o1-preview$, $o1-mini$) وإدارة المحادثات وتثبيتها. هندسة الأوامر (Prompt Engineering): القواعد الذهبية لصياغة الأوامر القوية ($Role$, $Context$, $Task$, $Format$, $Constraints$)، استخدام تقنيات $Few-Shot Examples$، التعديل التكراري، وتجنب الأخطاء الشائعة. الإبداع البصري عبر DALL-E: توليد الصور، ضبط الأساليب الفنية والإضاءة والزوايا، تعديل الصور وإضافة/حذف العناصر، وحالات الاستخدام في التصميم والتسويق. تحليل البيانات والملفات: رفع ملفات Excel وPDF، استخدام $Code Interpreter$ لتحليل البيانات وبناء المخططات البيانية، واستخراج البيانات المتقدمة. بناء مساعد مخصص (Custom GPTs): طريقة تصميم وتدريب مساعد خاص بك عبر رفع المعرفة والتعليمات الدقيقة وتفعيل القدرات والمشاركة. المهارات المتقدمة وحالات الاستخدام: استخدام التصفح التلقائي للويب، الذاكرة طويلة المدى، تنظيم المشاريع، واختصارات الإنتاجية، بالإضافة لتطبيقات عملية للكتّاب، الإعلاميين، والمسوقين. 2. دليل ChatGPT للبرمجة (للمطورين) مخصص لمهندسي البرمجيات لتعزيز الإنتاجية وكتابة الأكواد: الإعداد وصياغة أوامر الكود: تخصيص $Custom\ Instructions$ للبرمجة، اختيار النموذج الأنسب للكود المعقد أو السريع، وصياغة الأوامر البرمجية الاحترافية. توليد الأكواد وإكمالها: توليد الدوال والوحدات البرمجية، التحويل بين لغات البرمجة المختلفة (مثل Python إلى Go أو Rust)، شرح الكود المعقد وتوليد هيكل المشاريع ($Boilerplate$) والتطبيقات الكاملة. التنقيح ومراجعة الكود (Debugging & Review): تحليل رسائل الأخطاء، إيجاد السبب الجذري للـ Bugs، المراجعة الأمنية للكشف عن ثغرات OWASP، وتحليل وتعقيد الأداء ($Big\ O$). الاختبارات وجودة الكود: كتابة اختبارات الوحدات ($Unit\ Tests$) بـ pytest، اختبار الحالات الحدية ($Edge\ Cases$)، وتحليل التغطية ($Coverage\ Analysis$). إعادة الهيكلة والأتمتة: تطبيق أنماط التصميم ($Design\ Patterns$)، إعادة الهيكلة الذكية، وأتمتة سير العمل البرمجي ($CI/CD\ Pipelines$, $Pre-commit\ hooks$). 3. دليل ChatGPT للإضافات وبروتوكول MCP يشرح ربط الذكاء الاصطناعي بالأدوات والأنظمة الخارجية: مقدمة في MCP والإضافات: مفهوم بروتوكول context Model Protocol (MCP) والفرق بينه وبين $Plugins$ و$Custom\ GPTs$. إعداد title: Error Propagation in AI Models: How Small Mistakes Accumulate, Spread and Grow
abstract: This presentation examines the mechanisms through which errors originate, propagate, accumulate, and amplify in artificial intelligence models. It distinguishes three interacting sources of error: biases and limitations in training data, hallucinations, and context fading. Particular attention is paid to causal relationships between these error types and their implications for the reliability of AI-generated outputs. The presentation introduces methodological approaches to estimating error probabilities, assessing cumulative risks, and analyzing error propagation across reasoning steps, interconnected AI modules, and successive model generations. It discusses error reproduction, feedback mechanisms, and strategies for monitoring and mitigating systemic failures. The findings contribute to understanding AI reliability and risk assessment, particularly in applications involving cybersecurity, critical information infrastructure, and other high-stakes decision-making environments. Presented in connection with the V International Conference “Challenges and Reality of the IT-Space: Software Engineering and Cybersecurity” (SECS-2026), October 29–30, 2026, Kyiv, Ukraine (online).

title: Explainable Disease Classification via Multi-Ultrasound Images using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown promise in computer-aided diagnosis from multiple ultrasound images. However, their patient-level predictions do not reveal which images contribute to the result, limiting interpretability. We present an explanation framework that adapts Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to graph-level prediction by perturbing each patient’s image set. Instead of superpixels, we sample image subsets, reconstruct their graphs, and estimate image-level influence. To generate informative perturbations, we propose a two-stage Adaptive Class-Balanced Sampling: Stage I samples randomly, and Stage II employs class-biased sampling, drawing 85% of images from the minority class pool to ensure an informative design matrix. Ridge and 10-fold cross-validated Elastic Net quantify conditional influence, while Pearson correlation describes marginal association. We evaluated the framework on 135 positive-label patients with 3,072 ultrasound images from the Taiwan Biobank. Adaptive sampling moved predicted class proportions closer to balance in 126 patients, but random sampling yielded lower mean Ridge probability-surrogate error (0.066 versus 0.119). For both sampling schemes, deleting images in descending coefficient order lowered model output more than random deletion in all patients. The framework provides image-level visual explanations and a statistical basis for examining how sampling, approximation and ranking contribute to interpretation of multi-image predictions.

title: Klasifikasi Sentimen Pengguna Platform X Terhadap Isu Geopolitik Israel–Palestina Menggunakan BERT
abstract: The geopolitical issue between Israel and Palestine has sparked a wide range of public reactions on social media, particularly on the platform X. Sentiment analysis is a widely discussed topic in Natural Language Processing. This study develops a sentiment classification model for that issue using the BERT Base Uncased architecture, with data labeled automatically through the VADER approach. Data were collected via scraping with Tweet-Harvest, yielding 3.172 tweets, later reduced to 2.362 after preprocessing stages including cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, stopword removal, and stemming. VADER labeling produced a distribution of 73.7% negative sentiment and 26.3% positive sentiment. The model achieved 86.92% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-Score for the negative class of 90%, 93%, and 91%, respectively, while the positive class obtained 77%, 71%, and 74%. The average F1-score reached 88%. These results indicate the model correctly predicts most of the data, although a slight indication of overfitting appeared, with no significant impact on validation accuracy. This confirms that combining VADER and BERT Base Uncased is effective for sentiment classification on international geopolitical issues.

title: Integrating Linguistic Features with IndoBERT for Detecting Underage-Associated Comments in Indonesian YouTube
abstract: Indonesia has issued Government Regulation No. 17 of 2025 on Electronic System Governance for Child Protection (PP TUNAS), which prohibits independent access to digital platforms for individuals under 16. However, age verification remains difficult since users may provide fake birth dates during registration. This study aims to develop a hybrid text classification framework that integrates IndoBERT contextual embeddings with eight handcrafted linguistic features (teen_score, adult_score, emotion_score, grammar_score, word_count, exclamation_count, question_count, and teen_adult_ratio) to identify underage-associated comments on Indonesian YouTube. This study collected 37,450 comments from 271 videos using the YouTube Data API v3 and validated annotation consistency through manual labeling of 500 stratified samples, achieving Cohen's Kappa of 0.853 (almost perfect agreement). To address severe class imbalance, in which under-16 samples accounted for only 1.64%, then applied stratified 5-fold cross-validation with weighted sampling. The hybrid model achieved F1-scores of 0.7777 ± 0.0680 (cross-validation) and 0.9609 (test set). Ablation experiments confirmed explicit age disclosures are essential for the current annotation strategy. Although no significant performance difference was observed versus IndoBERT-only (p = 0.5743), the hybrid model provides explicit linguistic evidence through SHAP and LIME analyses, substantially improving interpretability. This makes the proposed framework suitable for transparent policy-oriented comment screening under PP TUNAS.

title: Intraoperative margin assessment in colorectal cancer via AI-enhanced multiphoton microscopy
abstract: Significance: Identifying residual tumors at the resection margins is crucial for individuals undergoing colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Accurate margin assessment can help minimize residual tumor while avoiding unnecessary removal of healthy tissue. Aim: This study uses label-free multiphoton microscopy to visualize collagen architecture and develops a feature-enhanced deep-learning model to distinguish CRC from margin-adjacent normal tissue. Approach: Margin-adjacent normal and carcinoma tissues were imaged using multiphoton microscopy, and 142 quantitative collagen features were extracted from SHG images. We propose PVT-Enhanced, a feature-fusion model that integrates handcrafted collagen features with deep image features derived from PVTv2-b5 through an attention-based fusion strategy. Its performance was compared with LASSO-LR, three convolutional neural networks, and image-only PVTv2-b5. Results: SHG imaging showed relatively coherent fiber orientation, longer and more continuous collagen fibers, and higher fiber density in margin-adjacent normal tissue, whereas carcinoma tissue showed more disorganized orientation, shorter and more fragmented fibers, and lower fiber density. The PVT-Enhanced model achieved an accuracy of 86.9%, an AUC of 0.923, and a specificity of 96.4%. Only 5 of 137 margin-adjacent normal images were misclassified as CRC. Conclusions: Our findings suggest that the PVT-Enhanced framework combined with SHG imaging allows accurate, rapid, and label-free tissue characterization that may support intraoperative margin assessment in CRC surgery.

title: Affective directions in activation space: An interpretable inference-time control mechanism
abstract: Emotion is a fundamental component of human communication, shaping understanding, trust, and engagement across domains such as education, healthcare, and mental health. Although large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong reasoning and knowledge-generation capabilities, they still struggle to express emotions in a consistent, controllable, and contextually appropriate manner. This limitation restricts their potential for authentic human–AI interaction. We propose a controllable emotion generation framework based on Emotion Vectors (EVs) —latent representations derived from internal activation shifts between neutral and emotion-conditioned responses. By injecting these vectors into the hidden states of pretrained LLMs during inference, our method enables fine-grained, continuous modulation of emotional tone without any additional training or architectural modification. We further provide a first-order theoretical analysis of emotional steering and its interaction with a semantic readout under explicit local assumptions. Experiments across multiple LLM families demonstrate adjustable emotional expression and characterize the model-dependent trade-off between steering strength, topical relevance, and fluency. The framework provides a general, training-free control interface with explicit intensity scaling and vector composition. Comparisons with prompting and fine-tuning characterize the emotional and quality effects of the evaluated configurations. Emotion Vector (EV) steering thus offers an efficient and interpretable means of bridging rational reasoning and affective understanding in large language models, and points to a promising direction for building emotionally resonant AI systems capable of more natural human–machine interaction.

title: EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference
abstract: Foundation models like V-JEPA are increasingly deployed across a heterogeneous edge-cloud continuum spanning smart glasses, phones, robots, and servers. Yet, they are typically trained as rigid, fixed-capacity networks bound to one device, supporting neither reconfigurable compute budgets nor collaborative execution. Existing approaches address only one axis at a time: slimmable and NAS-based methods provide width elasticity but assume single-device inference, whereas split-computing methods enable cross-device collaboration only for fixed partitions and static capacities. We introduce Elastic V-JEPA (EV-JEPA), a single model trained once and deployable everywhere along the continuum. Its width is reconfigurable, and it is natively partitionable across heterogeneous devices. At its core is Transition-Aware Triplet Training (T3). At each step we pick a narrow and a wide width, and train three paths: each width alone, plus a hybrid path that runs the early layers narrow and the rest wide. The hybrid switch point is where one device hands off to another, so the same weights learn both single-device and cross-device execution. Across various benchmarks, EV-JEPA falls within 1 accuracy point of independently trained baselines while improving over previous elastic training approaches by up to 11 accuracy points. Narrow-to-wide cross-device hybrid execution recovers to within 1.1 points of the highest-capacity standalone model and supports many-to-one, any-to-any, and variable-split configurations. Finally, we show that the elastic principle extends beyond the backbone to an elastic token compression mechanism that exposes controllable trade-offs among on-device computation, latency, and accuracy.

title: Spanning Diffusion and Flow-based Posterior Sampling via Exact Gaussian Conditioning
abstract: Flow-matching and diffusion models are increasingly used as priors for linear inverse problems, however, most methods are bespoke to one class of trajectory prior. Plug-and-play methods have been proposed, however these implicitly decorrelate the guided trajectory, resulting in broad priors that can struggle when data is sparse. This work proposes $β$-Flow: a general plug-and-play method indexed by a correlation parameter $β$ that generalises over flow, diffusion, and decorrelated priors, and a confidence parameter $κ$ that controls how strongly the path distribution is enforced. Each step requires only one forward evaluation of a denoising network, followed by a Gaussian conditioning step. This step is an exact Kalman update that is not dependent on network gradients. We show that many existing guided samplers can be interpreted as instances or approximations of our method, each implicitly using a different trajectory prior and operator in place of the Kalman gain. From this viewpoint, we provide a qualitative comparison of methods in terms of their implicit biases and assumptions. We demonstrate consistently state-of-the-art level performance across 7 inverse problems over 4 datasets in terms of PSNR and SSIM. Moreover, we demonstrate the utility of this prior control, by showing that confident high correlations (strict priors) work best when observations are less informative, while low correlation is preferred when observations are more informative, reflecting the complementary roles of the prior and likelihood in Bayesian inference.

title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
abstract: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.

title: VLMs are Native Action Models: Unleashing the Manipulation Capabilities of VLMs with Explicit Action-Space Grounding
abstract: Pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) already exhibit strong visual, spatial and reasoning capabilities relevant to robotic manipulation. The key challenge in turning pretrained VLMs into generalist manipulation policies is to expose these capabilities through an appropriate action interface. Vision-language-action (VLA) models provide a unified trainable policy, but typically introduce learned action tokens, action heads, or action experts whose semantics must be learned from robot data pretraining. In contrast, modular foundation-model-based manipulation methods can exploit pretrained VLM capabilities for zero-shot manipulation, but rely on external planning and control scaffolds that are not end-to-end trainable as a unified continuous-action policy. In this work, we introduce EASG, an Explicit Action-Space Grounding framework that bridges these two paradigms. By projecting a tool center point (TCP)-centered action frame into the wrist camera observation and expressing actions in the form of VLM's native textual generation interface, EASG makes the semantics of a continuous robot action space directly observable in the VLM's perceptual context. This allows pretrained VLMs to directly generate executable robot actions using their existing visual-spatial reasoning capabilities, without robot-action pretraining or additional action modules. Besides, the same action interface supports direct fine-tuning with robot trajectories, allowing the models to continuously improve beyond their manipulation capabilities unleashed by EASG. Overall, EASG enables zero-shot manipulation and generalization across object positions, categories, and robot embodiments, while supporting effective fine-tuning in the same continuous action space. These results demonstrate that, given an appropriate action interface, pretrained VLMs can themselves serve as native action models for robotic manipulation.

title: A7 — Operational Will. Commitment, Initiative, and the Question of What an Agent Does Next.
abstract: An agent can remember an obligation and still never return to it. A daily schedule can keep it busy while important work slips away. I call the missing capacity operational will: not a private feeling or a claim of personhood, but a system-level ability to carry legitimate commitments across pauses, initiate within their scope, reconsider attention, and explain both action and deliberate non-action. I propose a bounded architecture: persistent commitments, time and event signals, an active decision model, and an I-Entity, a read-only reviewer that asks questions but cannot command tools. Earlier work on intention and BDI agents already covers much of this territory; the contribution here is a separable, auditable cross-commitment review interface and a falsifiable way to test whether it improves decisions. Dated ZAI records supply difficult design cases: a blocked proposal queue, restraint after permission, and a scheduler that reported success without acting. A proposed seven-condition test asks whether broader attention actually improves decisions over ordinary checklists and critics; the evaluation has not yet been run.

title: IRCM-FS: Reproducibility Package for Compact and Stable Wrapper Feature Selection
abstract: This record provides the reproducibility package for IRCM-FS, a confidence-aware intervention–response contextual memory method for compact and stable wrapper feature selection. The package contains the frozen IRCM-FS implementation used in the independent benchmark, benchmark and baseline code, verification scripts, processed experimental results, statistical analysis outputs, reproducibility documentation, environment specifications, tests, and manuscript figure-generation scripts. The benchmark covers 11 public classification tasks, six methods, five random seeds, and 330 fresh runs under a common nominal evaluation budget. Raw UCI datasets are not redistributed and can be obtained from their original sources as documented in the package.

title: QOIDAVIY KKT FORMALIZMI VA YIRIK TIL MODELLARI INTEGRATSIYASI: ARXITEKTURA VARIANTLARI TASNIFI VA BAHOLASH MEZONLARI
abstract: Tezisda ijtimoiy ahamiyatli sohalar raqamlashtirilishi sharoitida kam resursli o‘zbek tili uchun qoidaviy mashina tarjimasi bilan yirik til modellarini (YTM) birlashtirish masalasi ko‘riladi. Prof. M. X. Hakimov ishlab chiqqan kengayuvchi kirish tili (KKT) formalizmiga asoslangan o‘zbekcha–inglizcha tizim negizida integratsiyaning olti arxitektura varianti yagona tasnifga keltiriladi. Tasnif ikki savolga javob beradi: har konfiguratsiyada KKT nima qiladi va YTM nima qiladi. Sof qoidaviy va sof neyron chegara-holatlardan tortib, YTM realizator, tahlil-iste’molchi, verifikatsiya sikli ostidagi tarjimon va yozma qoida-matn ijrochisi vazifasini bajaradigan konfiguratsiyalar ko‘rib chiqiladi; har biri uchun mehnat taqsimoti, kutiladigan afzallik va ishlash-sharti aniqlanadi. Tasnifga ortogonal ravishda tarjima vaqtidan tashqari yo‘nalish — tasdiq-darvozali oflayn resurs to‘ldirish — ajratiladi. Gibrid tizimlarni baholashda yagona avtomatik ball yetarli emasligi asoslanib, to‘rt o‘qli mezon ramkasi taklif etiladi: sifat, formalizm-sodiqlik, determinizm va terminologik izchillik. Miqdoriy taqqoslash natijalari oldindan ro‘yxatga olingan protokol asosida alohida ishda e’lon qilinadi.

title: ИССЛЕДОВАНИЕ ДАТАСЕТОВ ДЛЯ РАЗДЕЛЕНИЯ ИСТОЧНИКОВ РЕЧИ И ИЗУЧЕНИЕ ВЛИЯНИЯ КРИТЕРИЕВ КАЧЕСТВА ДАННЫХ НА ОБУЧЕНИЕ
abstract: Данная статья исследует датасеты для разделения источников речи, оценивая объективные критерии качества и разнообразия данных, а также оценивает влияние каждого критерия на эффективность обучения, что может быть полезным для дальнейшей разработки или модификации данных для работы с речью. Были рассмотрены базовые критерии качества данных, а также характеристики, которые можно оценить статистически. Для оценки качества разделения, датасеты были обучены на нейросетевых моделях, и протестированы на общем тестовом наборе данных. Была проведена оценка влияния медианной составляющей и разброса в каждом критерии на качество разделения, а также с помощью количественной оценки корреляции в виде критерия Пирсона. Итоговый результат показал, что сильнее всего качеством модели положительно коррелирует средний процент речи и перекрытия двух спикеров.

title: Online comprehensive identification algorithm for seafloor hydrothermal plumes based on anomaly detection
abstract: The detection of hydrothermal plumes is crucial for discovering active seafloor hydrothermal fields and exploring seafloor resources. To enable autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to adapt their survey strategies in real time, this study proposes an integrated online identification algorithm that couples real-time anomaly detection with fluid-type classification using deep learning models trained on historical data from the Qianlong-II AUV. The algorithm combines sliding-window statistical features, gated recurrent unit networks for sensor-specific anomaly detection, and a multi-layer perceptron that fuses the anomaly probabilities to classify the fluid types of the plumes. Training labels are generated by offline algorithms tailored to different anomaly types, K-medoids clustering for point anomalies (temperature, turbidity) and adaptive iterative fitting for subsequence anomalies (methane, oxidation-reduction potential). Experimental evaluation under a leave-one-field-out protocol demonstrates that the online algorithm replicates the offline labeling logic with 98.67% fidelity, with ablation studies confirming the critical contribution of the anomaly detection stage. The proposed algorithm offers an effective, real-time deployable solution for autonomous hydrothermal exploration, significantly enhancing AUVs’ operational autonomy.

title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong results in classical code generation and are increasingly used to write the unit tests that safeguard that code. Whether they can do the same for quantum software is less clear, because quantum programs are probabilistic, depend on numerical tolerances, and are judged by domain-specific checkers, so a well-formed test can still disagree with the benchmark's verdict. Existing quantum benchmarks measure whether a model produces a correct solution, but not whether its tests can distinguish correct implementations from faulty ones. We introduce QTestBench, a framework that evaluates LLM-generated quantum test suites against independent benchmark checkers, never treating the tests themselves as ground truth. For each task, QTestBench prompts models to produce syntactic, semantic, and behavioral tests, injects candidate solutions at runtime, and compares each test verdict with the checker's label under three validation cohorts, each answering a distinct diagnostic question. We benchmark five LLMs on eight PennyLane QHack challenges and ten Qiskit HumanEval tasks. Generated suites almost always execute, but discrimination lags behind: the best generator reaches a test quality of 0.71 on QHack and 0.34 on Qiskit HumanEval, so executability alone overstates test quality. Oracle-verified synthetic mutants stabilize bug-detection estimates when natural faulty solutions are scarce, as on three of ten Qiskit tasks that yield none. QTestBench offers a reproducible, cross-framework benchmark for the trustworthiness of LLM-generated quantum tests.

title: NovaSplat: Model-Free 6D Object Pose Estimation via 3D Gaussian Splatting Onboarding and Refinement
abstract: 6D pose estimation of novel objects without CAD models remains an open challenge: model-free methods must build the object representation from scratch during onboarding and have long trailed their model-based counterparts. We present NovaSplat, a model-free pipeline that closes this gap. From a short smartphone video captured at onboarding, we train a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model that serves both as a template source for detection and coarse pose estimation and as a differentiable backbone for pose refinement. Our refiner optimizes the object-to-camera pose with combined photometric and geometric losses under a continuous rotation parametrization free of gradient singularities. On a household-object benchmark, NovaSplat surpasses all model-based methods. On a challenging industrial benchmark with textureless and specular surfaces, it outperforms all model-free competitors while substantially narrowing the gap to model-based ones. We further introduce NovaSplat-Lite, an inference variant that is $3.1\times$ faster at negligible accuracy cost. Code will be made available at \href{https://github.com/POSE-Lab/novasplat}{https://github.com/POSE-Lab/novasplat}.

title: Universal Bounds for Self-Normalized Kullback-Leibler Estimation
abstract: This work studies an entropy-based estimator of Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence constructed from normalized importance weights. We prove a universal finite-sample bound showing that its expectation can exceed the target-proposal KL divergence by at most $\log 2$ for any sample size. We then characterize the KL divergence between the distribution induced by importance-weighted resampling and the proposal, showing that it is upper bounded by both the expectation of the entropy-based estimator and the target-proposal KL divergence. Importantly, these bounds require neither bounded importance weights nor finite higher moments. We apply these results to test-time alignment of generative models via Soft Best-of-$N$ sampling, an importance-sampling-based scaling technique proposed by Verdun et al. (2025), and to relative entropy coding, obtaining finite-sample policy-divergence certificates and moment-free bounds on coding cost.

title: A Scalable Clustering-Based Approach for Efficient Mining of Large Datasets
authors: Harshita Koushal, Dr. Harsh Lohiya, Mr. Manoj Kumar Yadav
abstract: Clustering is an unsupervised machine learning technique used to identify and group similar data points within large datasets without relying on predefined class labels or target outcomes. It plays an important role in data mining by facilitating the discovery of meaningful groups, hidden patterns, and relevant data distributions. Traditional clustering methods generally assume that clusters are spherical and have relatively similar sizes, which can reduce their effectiveness when dealing with irregularly shaped clusters or datasets containing outliers. To address the challenges associated with clustering large databases, several approaches employ random sampling and partitioning techniques. In such methods, a large dataset is first divided into smaller partitions, and each partition is clustered independently. The resulting partial clusters are subsequently combined and clustered again to generate the final set of clusters. This approach reduces the computational burden associated with processing the entire dataset simultaneously. With the rapid growth of data volumes, several parallel clustering techniques based on the Map Reduce framework have also been proposed to improve scalability. However, applying the conventional K-Means algorithm to large datasets in a parallel environment may require the repeated reading and processing of data during each iteration. Consequently, this iterative process can significantly increase input/output operations and network communication overhead. To overcome these limitations, a series-based K-Means clustering approach, referred to as CBK Means, can be employed to reduce the amount of data processed while maintaining or improving clustering quality. evidence.title: A Scalable Clustering-Based Approach for Efficient Mining of Large Datasets
authors: Harshita Koushal, Dr. Harsh Lohiya, Mr. Manoj Kumar Yadav
evidence.abstract: Clustering is an unsupervised machine learning technique used to identify and group similar data points within large datasets without relying on predefined class labels or target outcomes. It plays an important role in data mining by facilitating the discovery of meaningful groups, hidden patterns, and relevant data distributions. Traditional clustering methods generally assume that clusters are spherical and have relatively similar sizes, which can reduce their effectiveness when dealing with irregularly shaped clusters or datasets containing outliers. To address the challenges associated with clustering large databases, several approaches employ random sampling and partitioning techniques. In such methods, a large dataset is first divided into smaller partitions, and each partition is clustered independently. The resulting partial clusters are subsequently combined and clustered again to generate the final set of clusters. This approach reduces the computational burden associated with processing the entire dataset simultaneously. With the rapid growth of data volumes, several parallel clustering techniques based on the Map Reduce framework have also been proposed to improve scalability. However, applying the conventional K-Means algorithm to large datasets in a parallel environment may require the repeated reading and processing of data during each iteration. Consequently, this iterative process can significantly increase input/output operations and network communication overhead. To overcome these limitations, a series-based K-Means clustering approach, referred to as CBK Means, can be employed to reduce the amount of data processed while maintaining or improving clustering quality. The method uses representative data verification to effectively reduce the dataset size before or during the clustering process. Experimental results indicate that CBK Means provides improved efficiency and scalability compared with the conventional K-Means algorithm, while also achieving better clustering accuracy.

title: A Competence-Based Architecture for Personalized Adaptive Learning
abstract: Traditional e-learning systems often provide limited personalization and adaptation to individual student needs. This paper presents a competence-based architecture for personalized adaptive learning in higher education that integrates an ontology-based content model, practical-skill verification, a learning-analytics-based student model, and explainable adaptive recommendations. The novelty lies in integrating these components into a single assessment-driven architecture in which a competence-and-depth content ontology, a mastery-and-attainment student model, and an ontology-grounded explainable recommendation layer operate together on real course data. The architecture was evaluated as a proof of concept using records from two undergraduate computing courses representing different computing subdomains. Student activity and assessment data were used to estimate mastery, distinguish demonstrated competence mastery from depth-level attainment, and generate prerequisite-aware recommendations from ontology relations. The results show that the proposed approach provides interpretable mastery estimates and ontology-grounded recommendations, offering initial evidence for the feasibility of competence-based adaptive learning in real course settings. A student feedback survey (n = 86) indicated positive perceptions of the clarity, relevance, and usefulness of the generated recommendations. The main contribution is a working, interpretable pipeline that transforms verified assessment evidence into mastery estimates, behavioral student types, and explainable learning recommendations.

title: Preregistration: Block IV Adaptive Agency and Structural Generalisation - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
abstract: This preregistration freezes the first confirmatory study for Experimental Block IV of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. Block IV tests whether artificial agents can adapt to previously unseen causal structures, compositions and problem families, and whether explicit predictive modelling and counterfactual rollout make selective causal contributions beyond serious model-free and heuristic alternatives. Seven hypotheses (H4.1-H4.7), twenty held-out seeds, confirmatory-only structural task variants, architecture classes, compute/storage matching rules, model-corruption and correction interventions, primary estimands, thresholds and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules are frozen before confirmatory execution. Development-only simulations were used to validate the implementation and choose prospective thresholds; their outcomes are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence. No Block IV confirmatory seed had been executed when the protocol was frozen. A positive result would support only scoped causal contributions to structural generalisation in the registered artificial environments. It would not establish general intelligence, universal necessity of world models, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness. Related methodological framework: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.

title: DASL-Net: adaptive streaming learning for robust robot perception under concept drift
abstract: Robots operating in dynamic environments often encounter concept drift caused by sensor noise, environmental changes, mechanical wear, and evolving task requirements, which can degrade perception and decision-making performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes DASL-Net, an adaptive streaming learning network for robust robot perception under concept drift. DASL-Net enables robots to continuously update their perception models from streaming sensory data while preserving previously learned knowledge. The network adaptively deepens existing branches for gradual concept evolution and creates new branches for emerging concepts. To reduce catastrophic forgetting and negative interference, DASL-Net uses Fisher information to measure the importance of historical parameters and guides branch generation by comparing Fisher information with current gradients. Experiments on multiple streaming classification benchmarks show that DASL-Net achieves better adaptability and long-term accuracy than conventional deep learning and incremental learning methods, demonstrating its potential for reliable robot perception in non-stationary environments.

title: Motion uncertainty visualization based on Gaussian process regression
abstract: In the context of image-guided soft-tissue intervention and surgery navigation, soft tissue motion estimation for a deformed/registered pre-operative/pre-interventional medical image may suffer from multiple sources of uncertainty. Visualizing the uncertainty in the deformed image is of great interest because it conveys the uncertainty in the registered pre-interventional/pre-operative navigation information on deformable soft-tissue organs governing the decisions of the surgeon or intervention specialist. We address the problem of propagating the uncertainty from a Gaussian process (GP)-based motion estimation of an input image. To visualize the deformed image itself, we show its maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate. To convey the overall uncertainty in the MAP deformed image estimate, we apply a spatially-varying blur (according to the uncertain motion estimate) to an image containing a grid and combine it with the MAP deformed image itself. We show 2D cross sections of the final image that convey both the deformed image and its uncertainty. We further extend our approach to local investigations of points or regions of interest (e.g., a tumor). To visualize where a point/region of interest (POI/ROI) is after deformation, we estimate marginal (i.e., per voxel) label (e.g., for being a tumor) probabilities (MLPs) based on an input probabilistic segmentation of the ROI in the non-deformed pre-interventional/pre-operative image and the input GP posterior distribution over deformation fields and show 2D cross sections of visually mapped MLPs or MLP isocontours.

title: MvFFN: Multi-view Floor plan Feed-forward Network for Unposed Wide-Baseline Panorama Layout Reconstruction
abstract: Reconstructing accurate camera poses and floor-plan layouts from sparse, unposed, wide-baseline RGB panoramas remains a challenging open problem. Direct multi-room floor-plan prediction is especially difficult in this setting: pose, geometry, semantics, and global layout structure are tightly coupled, yet a complete floor-plan is hard to learn as a single global output. Our key insight is to keep the model's predictions strictly local. Multi-view Ordered Wall Instance Segmentation (MOIS) is designed around this concept. Each panorama column predicts only the wall it observes plus the next two adjacent walls in clockwise order. The global wall partition, room layouts, and shared coordinates emerge from deterministic aggregation of overlapping local predictions. Building on MOIS, we propose Multi-view floor-plan Feed-Forward Network (MvFFN), which jointly predicts coarse camera poses, dense global geometry, and per-wall semantic outputs. A downstream Layout Chaining (LC) post processing pipeline then assembles these predictions into multi-room floor-plans with shared global coordinates, consistent wall identities, and connected room structure. The dense MOIS predictions recover cross-view wall identity and local within-room connectivity more accurately than composed modular baselines, and the assembled layouts substantially outperform prior methods on wall and junction level accuracy. We also introduce the ZInD-CrossView dataset, which augments ZInD with globally unique wall instances and cross-view segmentation labels for this task.

title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are now a standard source of query expansion terms but they hallucinate. They inject non existent entities and off-topic terms that add ranking noise and can hurt strong retrievers. Existing remedies such as corpus grounding, mutual verification and preference alignment treat hallucinated terms as an undifferentiated nuisance to be filtered by agreement heuristics, without a mechanistic account of why a given term appears or a principled criterion for how many terms to keep. We propose Subsequence-Association Filtered, breadth-aware query expansion (SAFE-QE), a training-free, retriever agnostic method that draws on the subsequence-association account of hallucination. We score each candidate expansion term by its corpus conditioned cross-context reproducibility, terms that reappear under randomised query contexts yet lack support in the pseudo-relevant set are flagged as products of dominant hallucinatory associations and down-weighted. Drawing on the characterisation of language generation as a trade-off between consistency (no hallucination) and breadth (coverage), we cast term selection as constrained coverage maximisation over the pseudo-relevant set, keeping a set that is approximately broad but consistent and stable across resampling. We also introduce the Hallucinated Expansion Term Rate, a query side faithfulness metric that counts injected expansion terms no relevant document supports. We evaluate our approach on benchmarked TREC and BEIR collections. Our SAFE-QE is statistically indistinguishable from generative and corpus-steered expansion on nDCG@10 while injecting fewer unsupported terms 4.3 per query against 27.8 for Query2doc and 57.5 for HyDE and on a strong learned sparse retriever, where every expansion method regresses. Faithfulness is therefore available at no measurable cost in ranking quality.

title: Correlation-Based Measurement of Entanglement in Rank-2 Mixed States
abstract: We study correlation-based entanglement evaluation in rank-2 mixed states of two- and multi-qubit systems. The relevant two-dimensional subspace is treated as a logical qubit embedded in the physical Hilbert space, and factorizable realizations of its logical Pauli operators are classified. For two qubits, this yields nontrivial canonical encodings related by local Clifford transformations. The relation between logical and physical Bloch vectors admits a geometric interpretation as a transversely deformed Bloch sphere, leading to closed-form expressions for two-qubit concurrence and generalized concurrence across $N$-qubit bipartitions. The entanglement scaling factor is obtained directly from complementary-subsystem correlations, without prior calibration of state-preparation parameters. Noisy simulations using the IBM Quantum FakeKingston backend model, with readout-error mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation, confirm the analytical results up to $N=10$ qubits. The protocol therefore enables entanglement estimation from only a small number of measurement settings for this class of rank-2 logical states.

title: RARA: Robust Policy Fine-Tuning through Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Pre-trained robot policies, such as Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, provide a strong foundation for generalist robotic manipulation, but adapting them to new tasks with only a few demonstrations remains challenging. Directly fine-tuning a pre-trained policy often achieves strong in-distribution performance, yet it can distort the representations learned during pre-training and weaken the model's generalization ability under out-of-distribution shifts. We propose Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment (RARA), a two-stage adaptation method, to address this issue. First, RARA retrieves representation features from pretraining with similar task intent and motion, and aligns the policy's representations of the target demonstrations with the pre-trained representations of the retrieved demonstrations. Second, RARA fine-tunes the policy on the target demonstrations while limiting how much its representations of the retrieved demonstrations change during fine-tuning. By reducing the representation mismatch before action learning and preserving pre-trained knowledge during adaptation, RARA limits unnecessary representation drift during fine-tuning. Experiments with Diffusion Policy and GR00T on 13 tasks in RoboTwin, RoboCasa, and on a real robot show that RARA improves the average success of fine-tuning by 9.5 points in-distribution and 13.6 points out-of-distribution, and outperforms all compared baselines. Project page: https://shua-kang.github.io/RARA_robot/

title: Sustainable Cloud-Fog-Edge Systems for Smart Buildings: Algorithmic Adaptation under Memory Constraints and Dynamic Orchestration Strategies
abstract: The escalating environmental footprint of the Information and Communication Technol- ogy (ICT) sectorwith global Data Center electric- ity usage potentially reaching 3% by 2030 and the imperative for real-time responsiveness in smart buildings demand a foundational shift towards Edge Computing. This article proposes a holis- tic architectural and algorithmic approach for cre- ating autonomous, resilient, and privacy-preserving learning systems within smart buildings, advancing the core concept of the building itself as the data center. Our contributions, demonstrating originality compared to conventional centralized systems, are structured around three main pillars: 1) Validation of resilient data acquisition chains using the af- fordable Arduino ecosystem (Uno R4 WiFi/BME280) and secure persistence solutions including centralized archiving (Node-RED/MySQL) and secure remote transfer (Python/rsync/SSH). 2). The proposal of a lightweight, KOptim orchestration framework, inter- operable with the FIWARE standard, for the dynamic management of Service Level Agreements (SLA). 3) The adaptation and experimental valida- tion of the Generalized Hebbian Algorithm (GHA) for Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on low- power microcontrollers,We introduce and compare an iterative learning strategy using data buffers, featuring sorting and explicit preservation of extreme samples to maintain diversity. Experimental results on the high-dimensional Tour Perret sensor data confirm that this novel method, despite introducing a necessary temporal complexity of O(W log W ) due to sorting, achieves convergence and final result quality that is visually equivalent to processing the entire dataset in full memory, reliably identifying two distinct operational states.

title: Two-way Guidance: Simultaneous Learning of Summary Statistics for Generative Bayes
abstract: Bayesian simulation-based inference (SBI) can struggle to recover increasingly concentrated posteriors as observation size grows. We consider learning sufficient summary statistics jointly with the posterior as a general principle for scalable inference in various SBI methods. A common measure taken in SBI is dimension reduction through predetermined summaries, which may partially discard posterior information. Our approach instead imposes structure on how the posterior learner depends on a learned summary (e.g., affinity), and learns the summary simultaneously with the posterior. We identify an important mechanism named two-way guidance: under a structural restriction on the summary, the posterior sufficiency of the learned summary simplifies posterior learning, whereas a suitable posterior objective guides the learned summary towards posterior sufficiency. This mechanism explains a counterintuitive finding that the structural restriction on the summary statistics improves posterior learning, rather than limit its performance. We establish theoretical guarantees on both posterior estimation error and the learned summary's departure from sufficiency, thus identifying conditions on the simulation budget for recovering increasingly concentrated posteriors as observation size grows.

title: Pointwise Structures and Background Perturbation Analyses for Thermal Non-equilibrium Irrotational Flows in Three Space Dimensions
abstract: In this paper, both the pointwise space-time structures of the solution for a three-dimensional model describing gas dynamics in thermal non-equilibrium and the corresponding background stabilities within the L^p framework are investigated under the small initial perturbation assumption and the irrotationality condition. Our main tools are the modified Green's function according to the irrotationality condition, a priori energy method and a refined decay estimates of products composed of the entropy function and high-order derivatives.

title: How many labelers do you have? A closer look at gold-standard labels
abstract: The construction of most supervised learning datasets revolves around collecting multiple labels for each instance, then aggregating the labels to form a type of “true” label. We question the wisdom of this pipeline by developing a (stylized) theoretical model of this process and analyzing its statistical consequences, showing how access to non-aggregated label information can make training well-calibrated models more feasible than it is with cleaned labels. The entire story, however, is subtle, and the contrasts between aggregated and fuller label information depend on the particulars of the problem, where estimators that use aggregated information exhibit robust but slower rates of convergence, while estimators that can effectively leverage all labels converge more quickly if they have fidelity to (or can learn) the true labeling process. The theory makes several predictions for real-world datasets, including when non-aggregate labels should improve learning performance, which we test to corroborate the validity of our predictions.

title: Recipient of the 2026 Alumni Trailblazer Award
abstract: Jared Kaplan is Chief Science Officer and Co-Founder of Anthropic, an AI lab dedicated to developing safe, beneficial AI. His research on scaling laws revolutionized the field by providing a framework for understanding and predicting advanced AI systems, guiding resource allocation and technological development. He also helped pioneer Constitutional AI, an approach designed to align AI systems with predetermined principles and values. A theoretical physicist for 15 years, Jared helped build GPT-3 and Codex at OpenAI before co-founding Anthropic. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University, where he teaches deep learning foundations. Jared holds a Ph.D. in physics from Harvard and bachelor’s degrees in physics and mathematics from Stanford. Named to Time’s 2025 list of the Top 100 AI people, Jared exemplifies IMSA’s vision of alumni shaping the future through groundbreaking science, global influence, and responsible innovation.

title: WHOT-ML: A Configurable Partially Observable Multi-Agent Environment for Machine Learning Research
abstract: We introduce WHOT-ML, a formalized computational environment based on the widelyplayed card game in Nigeria, WHOT, designed for research in machine learning under partialobservability, stochasticity, multi-agent interaction, and configurable rule systems. Unlikeconventional benchmarks that feature fully observable board states or fixed rule engines,WHOT provides an extensive-form game with private player hands, hidden draw decks,dynamic action masking, sequential multi-agent decisions, and asymmetric informationrevealed incrementally through play.We formalize WHOT as a finite, stochastic, sequential, multi-agent partially observableMarkov decision process (POMDP) and introduce WHOT-NG-v1.0, an open-source, deterministic reference environment featuring strict information isolation, bitwise state serialization,action masking, and modular rule configuration. We conduct a full-scale empirical campaigncomprising 12, 350 production runs executed in containerized cloud environments to establishthe empirical baseline of the environment.Our findings demonstrate that: (1) WHOT-ML provides an uncompromised informationboundary with 0.0% measured information leakage; (2) unobserved world states sharingidentical public observations induce an 84.63% trajectory divergence rate under deterministicrollout policies; (3) baseline heuristic agents significantly outperform uniform random playin asymmetric matchups (65.4% win rate in 4-player games, 86.3% in heads-up play), whilesymmetric heuristic self-play exposes an emergent defensive stall (43.6% truncation rate)driven by retaliatory penalty loops and market recycling; (4) player count scaling exhibits anempirical regime shift as the initial opponent-to-market card ratio exceeds unity (ρ0 > 1.0),resulting in severe market exhaustion; (5) modular rule ablations reveal that removinglast-card declarations shortens games by 49.9 turns while penalty card stacking remainsbehaviorally dormant against random opponents; and (6) the environment achieves 100.0%bitwise reproducibility across 200 independent replay and mid-game state restoration trials.WHOT-ML establishes a rigorous, reproducible laboratory for subsequent research inbelief-state estimation, opponent modeling, self-play, and reinforcement learning in imperfectinformation games.

title: Replication package: Sentiment Instruments Are Not Interchangeable — Audited Validity, Its Descriptive Consequences, and Its Correction in Airline-Directed Twitter Discourse
abstract: Replication package for a validation study of three off-the-shelf sentiment instruments (SenticNet 9, VADER, Twitter-RoBERTa) against blind three-coder human annotation on a stratified audit sample of 504 tweets, drawn from a collection of English-language tweets directed at six European airlines in the summers of 2018-2022 (252,650 user tweets after removal of re-captured records). The package contains, with no tweet text: tweet-level labels of all three instruments for every collected record (re-captured records and truncated author identifiers flagged); the 504 audited items with all three coders' original ratings, the original majority consensus, the post-audit adjudications and completed ratings, and a text-free linkage summary of each audited item's capture multiplicity; the codebook; the VADER and Twitter-RoBERTa scorers with the model revision; a conda environment manifest; and a single script (code/reproduce_all.py) that regenerates every statistic in the manuscript's tables, including the multiplicity-adjusted stratified difference estimates. See README.md for the layout, the sampling note, and the reproducibility boundaries (the historical SenticNet API run cannot be re-executed; the corpus cannot be rehydrated because platform identifiers were truncated at collection).

title: Neuro-symbolic cognitive attention model for embodied cognitive agents
abstract: Attention in humans is dynamic by nature and largely context-dependent. However, current embodied cognitive agents in XR systems mostly rely on static rules or neural models. Thus, it limits their interpretability and adaptability in immersive simulations. To address the problem, we propose a neuro-symbolic cognitive attention model for virtual agents in brain simulation and XR systems that integrates temporal neural predictions with proper reasoning to drive adaptive avatar behavior in virtual environments. Our model employs an LSTM network to generate continuous attention estimate with a taxonomic attention model that interprets attention for virtual agents in the context of task relevance, environmental saliency, cognitive load, and surrounding distraction intensity, producing context-aware attention states that guide the agent towards decision making and task adaptation. Our work implements a fully integrated and scalable design for attention-aware neuro-symbolic Digital Twin in cyber-physical and virtual environments, highlighting both novel model integration and practical system deployment.

title: Sparsity-accelerated offset-diagonal optical processors
abstract: Sparse neural networks facilitate accelerated computation and reduced energy consumption by minimizing the total number of operations required. However, conventional digital and analog computing platforms typically yield only modest performance gains when executing sparse models due to hardware primitives that remain unoptimized for these data structures. This work demonstrates a high-performance, diagonal-sparsity-accelerated optical computing system utilizing an offset-diagonal architecture that achieves near-ideal reductions in compute time as sparsity increases. Experimental validation on MNIST benchmarks confirms that the system maintains performance parity with digital baselines across a wide range of sparsity levels, from 0 % (dense) to 99 %. By concurrently leveraging intrinsic optical parallelism and high-performance structured sparse models, this platform establishes a strategic pathway for next-generation optical accelerators capable of delivering substantial improvements in both computational speed and energy efficiency.

title: BGVD-State: Replayable middleware for evidence-gated handoffs in third-party software security review
abstract: Third-party software security review is iterative: models, tools, and people raise suspected-risk candidates, test them against evidence, and hand the evolving review state to subsequent reviewers. Conversation logs preserve observations but may lose track of which candidates remain active, which evidence is current, which paths failed, and which decision controls reporting. BGVD-State is open-source, model-independent middleware for making these handoffs replayable and auditable. It preserves submitted event sequences, reconstructs candidate and evidence lifecycles, retains failed paths, persists checkpoints, applies an evidence-based reporting gate, and generates a handoff package. In a local review of fixed TypeScript, Django, and ECC revisions, 22 records reconstructed six suspected-risk candidates; a subsequent event completed the final candidate’s evidence-supported disposition. Automated regression tests and offline replay check the implementation, including rejection of invalid events without residual state changes. Separate continuation experiments compare model-maintained memory representations: schema-guided memory outperformed matched free-form memory on selected high-state-pressure fixtures, whereas information-equivalent prose tied and a cross-family source-audit setting did not reproduce the advantage. These experiments inform the state-contract design, rather than establish the middleware’s causal effect on model performance. BGVD-State does not discover vulnerabilities autonomously; it preserves evidence and review decisions for later models or human reviewers.

title: $L_0$ Feature Selection via Monte Carlo Tree Search in High-Dimensional Financial Regression
abstract: Feature selection is a central problem in high-dimensional financial regression, where large numbers of engineered variables and strong correlations among predictors reduce model stability and interpretability. $L_1$ regularization (Lasso) is widely used for sparse regression, but its shrinkage can be restrictive when informative signals are spread across correlated variables. Exact sparse regression avoids this shrinkage but requires solving a combinatorial optimization problem that is computationally difficult and is typically fit to minimize in-sample rather than out-of-sample error. This paper presents a feature selection framework based on Monte Carlo Tree Search with Generalized Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation (GNRPA). Feature selection is formulated as a sequential decision process, and candidate subsets are scored by their out-of-sample validation performance rather than training error. The method also supports a lexicographic objective accounting for subset size and multicollinearity. We study this approach on a contemporaneous explanatory regression task: explaining the weekly return of the NASDAQ-100 index from 1,072 engineered features spanning market, macroeconomic, and factor data. This isolates the value of subset selection under multicollinearity from the separate problem of predictive forecasting. On this task, the proposed method identifies sparse feature subsets with higher out-of-sample explanatory power than an optimized Lasso baseline, reaching an out-of-sample $R^2$ of 0.6961 versus 0.6313 for Lasso. These results suggest that Monte Carlo Tree Search is a practical alternative to convex regularization for sparse explanatory feature selection in financial regression, with potential value for factor attribution and risk decomposition where transparency matters as much as out-of-sample fit.

title: E3-System: Expressive EmoData, Explicitly Controllable, Easy-to-Use TTS
abstract: Recent zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems can clone unseen speakers, yet controllable expressiveness remains limited by a gap between semantic intent and acoustic realization. Text descriptions offer a natural control interface but provide weak acoustic grounding, whereas speech style prompts provide concrete prosody but entangle style with the prompt speaker's timbre. To bridge this gap, we propose E3-System, a unified intent-to-speech framework for expressive zero-shot TTS that couples three requirements: Expressive style modeling, Explicit timbre-style control, and Easy-to-use natural-language interaction. Given a target speaker and either a natural-language style description or a speech style prompt, E3-System generates expressive speech while preserving the target timbre. The key idea is to close the full control loop: building a large expressive style space, grounding user intent into usable acoustic style references, and synthesizing speech with disentangled timbre and style. To realize this loop, EmoData provides a thousand-hour multilingual emotional speech dataset, Style-RAG grounds text descriptions into high-quality acoustic style prompts from these data, and Dual-TTS transfers the grounded style to arbitrary target speakers through VC-augmented timbre-style disentanglement. Experiments show that E3-System achieves strong speech quality, speaker preservation, and explicit expressive controllability.

title: Co-Modifying Application Code and Deployment Infrastructure: A Causal Study of AI Agent Pull Requests
abstract: Current software engineering agents are evaluated predominantly inside isolated sandboxes against synchronous local tests. However, deploying features in collaborative repositories requires modifying continuous integration (CI/CD) pipelines, containers, and provisioning manifests alongside application logic. Because agents lack deployment awareness, attempting cross-domain modifications introduces unverified dependencies into asynchronous integration pipelines. To isolate the causal integration overhead of dual-scope pull requests (PRs)-modifying both application code and deployment infrastructure-we evaluated 26,999 PRs across two large datasets (AIDev v5 and MOSAIC-3M) encompassing six agent architectures and an aligned human baseline. Using a deterministic four-tier file taxonomy and an exact 4D strata-matching framework, we isolated integration metrics under conditional exchangeability while controlling for application volume. We find agents operate primarily as application coders or chore workers, with maintenance tasks capturing 17.70% to 25.41% of agent PRs. Dual-scope modifications represent only 4.48% to 4.55% of agentic PRs, yet trigger bimodal integration outcomes. In the first mode, explicitly reviewed contributions experience protracted delays, adding a median penalty of +13.13 hours and multiplying time-to-merge by 3.24x, driven mechanically by CI/CD and provisioning manifests. In the second mode, maintainer gatekeeping exhibits a structural bypass: even for external contributors lacking repository write access, agent identity reduces the odds of human review by 63.7% compared to human peers. Consequently, 43.1% to 56.2% of dual-scope PRs bypass inspection to merge silently in a median of under 31 minutes. These uninspected modifications compromise build verification, demonstrating the need for deployment-aware benchmarks and strict path-based access controls.

title: State Transfer in Discrete-Time Quantum Walks via Projected Transition Matrices
abstract: In this paper, we analyze state transfer in quantum walks by using combinatorial methods. We generalize perfect state transfer in two-reflection discrete-time quantum walks to a notion that we call peak state transfer; we define peak state transfer as the highest state transfer that can be achieved between an initial and a target state under unitary evolution, even when perfect state transfer is unattainable. We give a spectral characterization of peak state transfer that allows us to fully characterize peak state transfer in the arc-reversal (Grover) walk on various families of graphs, including strongly regular graphs and incidence graphs of block designs (assuming that the walk starts at a point of the design). In addition, we provide many examples of peak state transfer, including an infinite family where the amount of peak state transfer tends to $1$ as the number of vertices grows. We further demonstrate that peak state transfer properties extend to infinite families of graphs generated by vertex blow-ups, and we characterize periodicity in the vertex-face walk on toroidal grids. In our analysis, we make extensive use of the spectral decomposition of a matrix that is obtained by projecting the transition matrix down onto a subspace. Though we are motivated by a problem in quantum computing, we identify several open problems that are purely combinatorial, arising from the spectral conditions required for peak state transfer in discrete-time quantum walks.

title: A rank collapse in a sedenion Module-LWE proposal, and why a uniform matrix does not repair it
abstract: We report a negative result on SLWE, a Module-LWE variant over the sixteen-dimensional sedenion algebra that the author proposed in an earlier paper with a claim of NIST Cate-gory 5 security. Its public matrix is built from orbits of an order-7 coordinate permutation(a “Singer cycle”). First, the flattened public matrix factors through a fixed 256 × 112 integer matrix of rank 76, so its rank over Fq is at most 76 for every module rank k, and exactly 76 for generic seeds once k ≥ 7, whereas a uniform matrix of the same shape has rank 16k. This invalidates the security claim at both published parameter sets. Recovering the noise then reduces to an LWE instance of dimension 76, which the lattice estimator places at about 239 operations at the first set (n = 512, q ≈ 232). Second, replacing the matrix by a uniform one does not help at that set (centred binomial noise with η = 2, ternary secrets of weight 64): the estimator gives about 251. Third, decryption at those parameters is deterministic: the noise is bounded by 258, far below q/4; a failure rate of 2−6.4×1015 reported earlier came from a Gaussian tail evaluated outside the support of a bounded sum. All computations are reproducible from public scripts.

title: Fuzzifier-Induced Robustness Phase Transitions in Median-Centred Fuzzy Block Aggregation
abstract: Fuzzifier-Induced Robustness Phase Transitions in Median-Centred Fuzzy Block Aggregation develops and tests a robust fuzzy aggregation framework for data divided into blocks, where some blocks may be contaminated, extreme, or otherwise unreliable. The central problem is that fuzzy membership weighting does not automatically guarantee robustness. Depending on how rapidly the membership assigned to a distant block decays, an extreme contaminated block may have vanishing influence, bounded influence, or unbounded influence on the final aggregate. The framework provides a mathematical characterisation of these regimes through a tail-leverage criterion. For the standard noise-cluster membership law, the analysis yields a sharp robustness phase transition governed by the fuzzifier and aggregation power. On the robust side of the transition, sub-majority block contamination remains bounded; beyond the transition, a single sufficiently extreme block can cause breakdown. The framework also establishes a fuzzy-to-crisp limit in which graded memberships converge to hard residual trimming, together with finite-sample replacement-breakdown results, adaptive-scale extensions, vector-valued aggregation, and finite-variance concentration guarantees. The archive contains the complete computational material used for the numerical study: make_figures.py: generates all numerical experiments and publication figures. regression_tests.py: runs the numerical regression and edge-case tests used to check the theoretical results computationally. numerical_summary.txt: records the principal numerical outputs from the experiments. Six figure files in PDF format corresponding to the numerical illustrations. requirements.txt: lists the Python package dependencies required to run the code. environment.txt: records the software environment used for the archived computations. A regression report recording the outcome of the automated numerical checks. No external dataset is required. All numerical data used in the experiments are generated synthetically by the supplied code. The software is provided as research code for transparency and reproducibility. It is released as-is and will not be maintained, updated, extended, or supported. Compatibility with future versions of Python or its dependencies is not guaranteed.

The framework provides a mathematical characterisation of these regimes through a tail-leverage criterion. For the standard noise-cluster membership law, the analysis yields a sharp robustness phase transition governed by the fuzzifier and aggregation power. On the robust side of the transition, sub-majority block contamination remains bounded; beyond the transition, a single sufficiently extreme block can cause breakdown. The framework also establishes a fuzzy-to-crisp limit in which graded memberships converge to hard residual trimming, together with finite-sample replacement-breakdown results, adaptive-scale extensions, vector-valued aggregation, and finite-variance concentration guarantees. The archive contains the complete computational material used for the numerical study: make_figures.py: generates all numerical experiments and publication figures. regression_tests.py: runs the numerical regression and edge-case tests used to check the theoretical results computationally. numerical_summary.txt: records the principal numerical outputs from the experiments. Six figure files in PDF format corresponding to the numerical illustrations. requirements.txt: lists the Python package dependencies required to run the code. environment.txt: records the software environment used for the archived computations. A regression report recording the outcome of the automated numerical checks. No external dataset is required. All numerical data used in the experiments are generated synthetically by the supplied code. The software is provided as research code for transparency and reproducibility. It is released as-is and will not be maintained, updated, extended, or supported. Compatibility with future versions of Python or its dependencies is not guaranteed.

title: MammoShift-YOLO: Code, Models, Results, and Website for Case-Disjoint Mammographic Lesion Localization under Cross-Dataset Domain Shift
abstract: This reproducibility package accompanies a study of mammographic lesion localization under strict case/report-disjoint internal evaluation and completely locked external transfer. The scientific contribution is an auditable transportability analysis rather than a claim of transformer superiority or clinical readiness. Version 1.2 is the complete upload-ready release. It replaces the preceding package with the final manuscript and explicitly documents the three evaluated datasets throughout the abstract, study design, Table 1, workflow, results, and supplementary material. All numerical findings are unchanged from the verified analyses; this version improves manuscript/package consistency and incorporates the complete TOMPEI-CMMD external-validation expansion. INbreast full-field digital mammography was used for development, tuning, and held-out internal testing. MIAS was retained as a severe digitized-film cross-acquisition stress test with all normal mammograms included for false-positive and specificity accounting. TOMPEI-CMMD was added as a second, larger external full-field digital mammography cohort. Neither external dataset informed model fitting, checkpoint selection, threshold selection, or calibration. The release contains: - patient/case-report split audits and derived detection labels;- independent three-seed YOLOv12s and MammoShift-YOLO results;- frozen-checkpoint internal, MIAS, and TOMPEI-CMMD predictions;- lesion-level precision, sensitivity, F1, mAP, and FROC analyses;- 2,000-replicate case/pair/patient-cluster bootstrap samples and confidence intervals;- lesion subgroup, calibration, domain-shift, segmentation, and quantitative XAI outputs;- random-attribution and parameter-randomization XAI controls;- a label-free source-reference histogram-normalization experiment on TOMPEI-CMMD;- complete scripts, model configurations, checkpoint hashes, metric logs, 300-dpi figures, revised manuscript files, and a static project website. The TOMPEI-CMMD expansion evaluated 1,382 MLO mammograms from 1,360 patients containing 1,770 official polygon-derived lesions after three source-flagged exclusions. Standard preprocessing produced 277 TP, 11,021 FP, and 1,493 FN (precision 0.0245, sensitivity 0.1565, F1 0.0424, mAP@0.5 0.0223). Label-free normalization reduced false positives to 5,495 and increased precision and F1, but reduced sensitivity; paired patient-cluster intervals did not establish an mAP improvement. ## Software and libraries Primary analyses used Python 3.13.12; the TOMPEI-CMMD expansion used Python 3.13.7. Principal pinned libraries are PyTorch 2.11.0 with CUDA 12.8, torchvision 0.26.0, Ultralytics 8.4.32, OpenCV 4.13.0.92, NumPy 2.4.4, pandas 3.0.2, PyArrow 21.0.0, Matplotlib 3.10.8, SciPy 1.17.1, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scikit-image 0.26.0, Pillow 12.1.1, and python-docx 1.2.0. The experiments used an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 and FP32 detector inference. Exact versions are listed in `environment/requirements.txt`. ## Folder structure The root contains `checkpoints/` for released model weights and provenance; `code/` for acquisition, preparation, training, prediction, evaluation, bootstrap, XAI, and figure scripts; `data/` and `data_manifests/` for derived labels, split/cohort audits, and polygon-box metadata without raw mammograms; `results/` for every numerical output and complete performance ledgers; `figures/` for 300-dpi PNG and vector PDF files; `paper/` for the revised submission documents; `website/` for the static shareable project page; `environment/` for pinned dependencies; and `revision_2026-10-09/` for the self-contained external-cohort revision. `FILE_MANIFEST_SHA256.csv` records the relative path, size, and SHA-256 digest of every deposited file other than the checksum manifests themselves. ## Data availability and licensing Raw INbreast, MIAS, CMMD, and TOMPEI-CMMD mammograms are not redistributed. Users must obtain them from their original repositories and comply with the respective terms. TOMPEI-CMMD annotations and CMMD source images are distributed by The Cancer Imaging Archive under CC BY 4.0. Cite: 1. Kashiwada Y, Takaya E, Hiroya M, et al. TOMPEI-CMMD Dataset (Version 1). The Cancer Imaging Archive; 2025. doi:10.7937/WEZW-BH22.2. Cui C, Li L, Cai H, et al. The Chinese Mammography Database (CMMD). The Cancer Imaging Archive; 2021. doi:10.7937/TCIA.EQDE-4B16. ## Reuse notes The released code and derived results are for research use only. The reported model is not validated for clinical deployment or diagnosis. MIAS circular annotations were converted to approximate boxes; TOMPEI-CMMD boxes were derived from the minimum and maximum coordinates of each official polygon. TOMPEI-CMMD includes lesion-bearing MLO breasts and therefore does not support a normal-image specificity estimate. ## Keywords mammography; breast cancer; lesion detection; YOLO; transformer; domain shift; external validation; FROC; calibration; explainable AI; reproducibility

title: Reward-Quality Divergence (RQD): Code, Saved Runs and Analysis Scripts (Anonymous Review Artifact)
abstract: Anonymous review artifact for the paper Telling Judge Gaming from Judge Error in Visual Reinforcement Learning. Please do not try to identify the authors. RQD measures the gap between a judge's reward and an anchor-based quality score during reinforcement learning, subtracts the gap that exists before training (the floor), and labels the remaining gap growth as gaming, drift, collapse or none. Contents Code: the measure, the anchor checker, the judge wrapper with its prompt, the control rewards, the second grader and the re-scoring job. Results: the saved answers, rewards and anchor scores of all 236 training runs reported in the paper, plus the re-scoring and second-grader results. Analysis scripts: CPU-only scripts that rebuild every table of the paper from the saved results in a few minutes. Data: item files with the question, reference answer and anchor fact of every item (no images; the images come from the public ChartQA, GQA and DocVQA datasets). Human labels: the 100 human correctness labels used to check the anchor. Checks included: one script recomputes the anchor score of all 334,300 saved answers from the item files and the released checker and compares it with the stored score; unit tests cover the measure, the anchor and the rewards. The GRPO training loop and the cluster job scripts are not part of this review artifact; they will be released with the published paper. All training settings are listed in the paper's appendix. Code: MIT license. Result files and human labels: CC BY 4.0. The datasets keep their original licenses. See README.md for the commands.
