title: Postopek širitve Digitalne slovarske baze za slovenščino s tipično govorjenim in nestandardnim besediščem iz transkripcij govorjenega jezika
abstract: Digitalna slovarska baza za slovenščino (DSBS) je zasnovana kot osrednja po­datkovna baza s strojno berljivimi podatki o slovenščini. Njena oblikoslovna podlaga – Slovenski oblikoslovni leksikon Sloleks – trenutno vsebuje približno 380.000 leksemov ter njihovih pregibnih in naglašenih oblik skupaj z izgovori v mednarodni fonetični abecedi IPA ter njenem ekvivalentu X-SAMPA, z izjemo posameznih ročno dodanih leksemov (npr. žleht, pošlihtan, zaštekati) pa DSBS še ni bil sistematično razširjen s tipično govorjenim besediščem. V prispevku zato predstavljamo postopek širitve DSBS-ja z leksemskimi kandidati, ki smo jih strojno izluščili iz več jezikovnih virov, ki vsebujejo transkripcije govorjene slovenščine. Opišemo vire ter postopek luščenja in pregleda kandidatov: strojno označenim leksemom smo ročno popravili oblikoskladenjske oznake in leme ter jim pripisali še nekatere druge značilnosti, ki bodo uporabne pri njihovi nadaljnji leksikografski obravnavi v DSBS-ju. Za vsakega od približno 11.000 potrjenih leksemov smo nato strojno generirali še njegove pregibne oblike, naglašene oblike in izgovore s pomočjo Pregibalnika, orodja za strojno širjenje oblikoslovnega leksikona. Dokumentiramo izzive, s katerimi smo se soočali pri vključevanju tipično govorjenega besedišča v podatkovno bazo, ter rešitve, ki smo jih pri tem implementirali. Postopek bo mogoče ponoviti tudi pri luščenju besedišča iz prihodnjih različic korpusov govorjene slovenščine.

title: ConicFlow: constrained Inference-time optimal control for flow matching models
abstract: We propose ConicFlow, which frames constrained sampling from a flow matching model at inference time as an optimal control problem that balances deviation from the pretrained trajectory against reward, subject to hard terminal constraints. We discretize this problem and adapt receding-horizon control, optimizing only a short window of the trajectory at each step for computational tractability. We address the resulting sequence of receding-horizon subproblems with a receding-horizon primal-dual algorithm. Its dual multipliers capture the difficulty of satisfying each constraint and are refined throughout sampling, steering generation toward feasible final samples. We further propose a terminal-estimate variant that avoids accumulating local truncation errors by evaluating the reward and constraints at the predicted terminal point rather than at the end of the current horizon. Under standard regularity assumptions, we establish finite-horizon guarantees on suboptimality. Under convex-affine structure, we derive a sharper bound that scales linearly with omitted horizon length, and we show that the terminal-estimate variant is provably tighter when the flow dynamics change slowly. Experiments in both low- and high-dimensional settings with a recent large-scale flow matching model show that ConicFlow achieves high reward and strong constraint satisfaction while deviating less from the pretrained flow than recent baselines.

title: Simultaneous Competitive and Regret Guarantees for TCP Acknowledgment
abstract: We study simultaneous competitive and regret guarantees for TCP acknowledgment. Each acknowledgment serves all pending packets, and the objective is to minimize the total acknowledgment and waiting costs. It is well known that no deterministic online algorithm achieves a competitive ratio better than $2$. Given $k$ randomized online experts and $0<\varepsilon<1$, we construct a randomized online algorithm whose realized total cost is always at most $(2+\varepsilon)$ times the offline optimal cost $\mathrm{OPT}$ and whose expected regret against the expert with the smallest realized cost is $O(\sqrt{\mathrm{OPT}\log(k+1)}+\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The algorithm requires no advance knowledge of the number of packets or $\mathrm{OPT}$. Our algorithm controls switching costs between experts and uses the gap between the permitted competitive bound and its current cost to determine when to learn. We also prove lower bounds showing that, for $k\ge 2$, this regret bound is asymptotically optimal in $\mathrm{OPT}$, $k$, and $\varepsilon$, and that $\varepsilon>0$ is necessary for sublinear regret.

title: Circuit Design Problems in Binary Polynomial Quantum Optimization
abstract: Solving combinatorial optimization problems on near-term quantum computers mainly relies on their quadratic unconstrained binary formulation. Lately, binary polynomial formulations start to take the center stage, having a better scaling with respect to the number of used qubits. However, while quadratic forms are straightforward to implement on quantum circuits, polynomial forms of degree $d$ incur in circuit depth overheads, due to the lack of $d$-qubit gates, for $d\geq 3$, on current hardware. In this paper, we study the problem of designing the shallowest quantum circuit for a given polynomial form. We formulate it as a classical binary linear problem and we prove the \textsf{NP}-completeness of a variant of it. On the algorithmic side, we offer a scalable and performant heuristic method to tackle it, Tempura, as well as faster binary linear problem formulations, which offer computational feasibility while sacrificing optimality. Our performance evaluation shows that the algorithms yield far shorter circuits than the state-of-the-art approaches, and Tempura is mostly comparable with them in terms of runtime.

title: Double-Take: Improving Capacity, Binding, and Selectivity In Long-Context Within Bidirectional Memory
abstract: Processing a long sequence does not guarantee that distant information remains usable. As context grows, a fixed-size memory must retain many associations, connect information across positions, and preserve relevant structure without being overwhelmed by everything it observes. These are distinct requirements: a memory may store more information without representing the relationships needed for retrieval, and it may transport those relationships without preserving the ones that matter. Thus, the challenge is not simply extending context length, but constructing a memory that remains usable as context grows. We study this problem in large-chunk test-time training (TTT) and identify two basic failures: single-step writes accumulate interference, limiting capacity, while self-associative writes cannot form cross-position bindings. We introduce Double-Take (DT), which repairs these failures with multi-step unpinned updates and cross-position mixing, and adds bidirectional change-sensitive writes for selective retention. Capacity alone leaves end-to-end recall at the $0.10$ chance floor; adding binding raises it to $0.92$. Trained only on $32\,\mathrm{kb}$ genomic contexts, DT reaches $0.927$ AUROC at $131\,\mathrm{kb}$ and $0.856$ near $1\,\mathrm{Mb}$, while transferring zero-shot from human to mouse. Together, these results identify capacity, binding, and selectivity as three requirements for usable long-range memory.

title: MagCilia: A Compact Magnetociliary Tactile Sensor with 3D Force Sensing for Robotic Contact Perception and Grasping Feedback
abstract: Robotic grasping and surface exploration benefit from simultaneous measurement of normal and tangential forces and from surface information obtained through contact. Here, we present a compact magnetociliary tactile sensor (MagCilia) that combines a flexible magnetic-cilia structure with a Hall sensor for 3D force sensing. Quasi-static finite element analysis is used to investigate structural deformation and magnetic responses under multidirectional loading. To reconstruct forces from the coupled magnetic channels, we propose causal history fusion regression (CHFR), which combines current magnetic-field measurements with their recent changes. Five-fold cross-validation grouped by calibration record yields root-mean-square errors of 0.40, 0.57, and 0.69 N for Fx, Fy, and Fz, respectively, with corresponding coefficients of determination of 0.93, 0.90, and 0.92. Robotic experiments demonstrate tangential-force-guided gripper adjustment and multi-axis load monitoring under external perturbations. Frequency-domain features of the reconstructed forces distinguish six surface categories with 99.39% accuracy in three-fold cross-validation grouped by acquisition session. An online robotic demonstration additionally identifies all six tested surfaces. These results demonstrate 3D force reconstruction, grasping feedback, and surface recognition using a single compact tactile unit.

These results demonstrate 3D force reconstruction, grasping feedback, and surface recognition using a single compact tactile unit.

title: How biological synapses self-assemble gradient learning
abstract: Existing models of learning in the brain explain how given circuits learn, but not how biology could assemble those circuits in the first place. To address this gap, we formulate Self-Assembling Learning-the study of how learning systems can emerge from lower-level interactions-and introduce one example mechanism, the Self-Assembling Motif (SAM). SAM is self-assembling at two scales: The motif emerges from initially random connectivity under heterosynaptic plasticity rules, and networks of SAMs, composed hierarchically, self-organize into dynamics that provably approximate a generalized form of stochastic gradient descent-matching backpropagation-level performance. This suggests that biological learning need not be prescribed but can emerge from local rules-and to a far greater extent than previously thought.

title: Inovação e Transformação Digital Aumentada-Governada
abstract: Síntese executiva A inteligência artificial está sendo incorporada ao trabalho, não apenas para automatizar rotinas, mas também para ampliar a capacidade de pessoas e equipes em tarefas cognitivas específicas. Essa ideia possui raízes anteriores à IA generativa, Licklider (1960) descreveu a simbiose humano-computador como combinação de capacidades complementares, em seguida, Engelbart (1962), utilizou explicitamente a noção de “augmenting human intellect” para explicar como artefatos, linguagem, métodos e treinamento poderiam aumentar a capacidade humana de compreender situações complexas e resolver problemas. Trabalhos contemporâneos sobre inteligência híbrida, colaboração humano-IA, inovação aumentada e transformação organizacional retomam e atualizam essa linha. O termo “aumentada”, neste relatório, não significa que a IA torna o ser humano mais inteligente em sentido geral, significa que, em tarefas e condições delimitadas, pessoas e equipes podem ampliar alcance, velocidade, variedade de alternativas, acesso a conhecimento, capacidade de análise ou execução com o apoio da tecnologia. Essa ampliação precisa ser observada no trabalho concreto, não é garantida pela simples disponibilização de uma ferramenta e não pode ser inferida apenas pela capacidade técnica do modelo de IA e tecnologias utilizadas. A mesma literatura que descreve possibilidades de ampliação mostra que o uso da IA distribui tarefas, conhecimento e influência sobre decisões, por isso, a governança não deve surgir somente depois da implantação. Normas, frameworks e pesquisas sobre inteligência artificial responsável, auditoria algorítmica, interação humano-IA e gestão de riscos, convergem para a necessidade de propósito explícito, responsabilidade definida, avaliação de impactos, controle de dados, supervisão humana efetiva, transparência proporcional, monitoramento e possibilidade de intervenção ao longo do ciclo de vida. A recomendação deste relatório é direta ao indicar que as iniciativas de inovação e transformação digital que utilizem IA devem ser simultaneamente aumentadas e governadas. A IA deve ser escolhida para ampliar capacidades relevantes do trabalho de transformar e a governança deve ser incorporada desde a formulação do problema até a operação, a revisão dos resultados e a aprendizagem, além disso, o hífen em “Aumentada-Governada” expressa essa inseparabilidade prática. A orientação também é compatível com tradições consolidadas de estratégia, inovação, design e transformação organizacional. Cadeia de valor, capacidades dinâmicas, design centrado no ser humano, modelos operacionais digitais, inovação de modelos de negócio, cenários e roadmapping continuam preservando suas finalidades originais. Portanto, a contribuição da orientação Aumentada-Governada é acrescentar, durante sua aplicação, duas questões: (a) que capacidade a IA pode ampliar e (b) que governança precisa acompanhar essa ampliação. O resultado não é uma reivindicação de autoria terminológica nem uma teoria que promete ganhos universais, é uma síntese fundamentada e uma recomendação de gestão aplicável a organizações que desejam utilizar IA para transformar produtos, serviços, processos e modelos de negócio. Sua utilidade está em mudar a pergunta empresarial, ou seja, em vez de perguntar apenas onde implantar IA, perguntar qual capacidade precisa ser ampliada, para produzir qual valor e sob qual governança.

title: TECHNOLOGY FOR PREPARING STUDENTS TO USE ROBOTICS IN AN INNOVATIVE EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT
abstract: This article outlines the pedagogical and technical-software foundations for preparing students to use educational robotics within an innovative educational environment. It provides a scientific analysis of issues regarding the implementation of the STEM approach in the educational process, the strengthening of interdisciplinary integration, and the development of 21st-century skills (critical thinking, creativity, teamwork, and engineering thinking) among students. Additionally, a model is proposed for integrating hardware (Arduino, LEGO Education) and visual/text-based programming environments with pedagogical technologies.

title: Improved prediction of near-surface winds for solar field siting and wind load design
abstract: This talk will present results on the performance of two ML-based approaches to correct numerical weather model data based on quantile mapping of probability distributions to historical wind observation data. Our analysis highlights the potential for integrating improved near-surface wind datasets into CST and PV planning tools for better-informed site selection, improved stow strategies, and structural collector design optimization. Additional analysis and future work will be outlined on expanding the methodology to generate wind forecast models for broader application in solar resource assessment and concentrating solar thermal plant operation.

title: A large-scale pipeline for LLM-assisted corpus annotation
abstract: Abstract As natural language corpora expand at an unprecedented rate, manual annotation remains a significant methodological bottleneck in corpus linguistic work. We address this challenge by presenting a scalable pipeline for automating grammatical annotation using large language models (LLMs). We demonstrate the pipeline’s accessibility and effectiveness through a diachronic case study of variation in the English evaluative consider construction ( consider X as / to be /Ø Y). We annotate 143,933 ‘consider’ concordance lines from the Corpus of Historical American English (COHA) via the OpenAI API in under 60 hours, achieving 98%+ accuracy on two sophisticated annotation procedures. Subsequent analysis reveals previously undocumented genre-specific trajectories of change, enabling us to advance new hypotheses about the relationship between register formality and competing pressures of morphosyntactic reduction and enhancement. Our results suggest that LLMs can perform a range of data preparation tasks at scale with minimal human intervention, unlocking substantive research questions previously beyond practical reach.

title: FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems
abstract: Production recommender systems have feature-lifecycle asymmetry: adding new features must produce gains on some metric, while feature removal must not regress any metric. In practice, feature deprecation is hard to prioritize as a feature can fail to be removed if it interacts with other features, its importance changes daily, it cannot be evaluated before production models change or data drift occurs, it is in contention for A/B test space with other launches, it causes regressions in an online A/B test, or it is consumed by multiple models that need to coordinate its deprecation. We present FORTE, a model-agnostic production framework for discovering, validating, and removing features. Its efficient perturbation implementation allows daily feature evaluation. To account for interactions, it evaluates candidate feature sets constructed from all the low-rank features through grouped ablation and its offline results are sufficiently predictive of online A/B tests to allow deprecations to proceed to online testing with confidence. Lineage tracing identifies all downstream consumer models to realize the full savings of removing a feature from the training set. We validate FORTE over 2 large-scale recommender systems and find that it identifies deprecable feature sets which do not cause online regressions, while the impact on efficiency depends on model characteristics. On a search-relevance model, FORTE resulted in 3 nested candidate sets of 32, 48, and 59 features. Online guardrails rejected the largest treatment. The 48-feature set was selected for deprecation, removing 43.3% of the model's features. On a large ranking model, FORTE identified 8 candidates for removal. Retraining and A/B testing confirmed no regression. Its launch reduced the trainable parameters by 29.9%, improved serving throughput by 19.8-25.5%, and reduced annual training costs by hundreds of thousands of dollars.

title: Decoder- and Noise-Aware Optimization Framework for Clifford-Deformed Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
abstract: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computing requires qubit-efficient quantum error correction (QEC). Clifford deformations (CDs) modify the stabilizers of a QEC code to lower its logical error rate at no additional resource cost. However, the number of possible CDs grows exponentially with the number of qubits, making exhaustive search infeasible beyond small codes. In this work, we further show that under circuit level noise the optimal CD depends strongly on both the noise model and decoder. To make systematic CD optimization possible, we introduce Evolution-Based Best-arm Identification (EBBI), a shot-efficient search algorithm that treats the circuit, noise model and decoder as a black box. We benchmark EBBI's performance on the rotated surface code, under two strongly $Z$-biased circuit-level noise models with the PyMatching decoder. At distance 3, EBBI finds the optimal CD using up to $\sim 1100\times$ fewer shots than random search. At distance 5, when run at the target error rate, the median EBBI run converges to the CDs we believe to be optimal, while random search never converges. Under a $Z$-biased SI1000-like noise model, EBBI discovers a new CD, the B-XZZX code, which we generalized to larger distances. It differs from XZZX on only a fraction $\mathcal{O}(d^{-1})$ of the qubits at code distance $d$, yet its relative advantage grows from $\approx 5\%$ at $d = 3$ to $\approx 12\%$ at $d = 11$. We thus show that the B-XZZX pattern found by EBBI can be systematically scaled to larger code distances. Our work represents a first step towards scalable CD optimization for general QEC codes.

title: AV-FlowEdit: Training-Free Prompt-Driven Audio-Visual Editing with Event-Aware Spectral Trajectory Preservation
abstract: Joint audio-video diffusion models generate synchronized content, but editing existing clips requires target changes without disrupting non-target structure or cross-modal correspondence. We present AV-FlowEdit, a training-free and inversion-free framework for prompt-driven audio-video editing. Our key insight is that source--target flow differences provide both cross-modal editing directions and preservation cues. Under shared perturbations, they jointly update the video and audio branches, supporting visual-only, audio-only, and joint edits while retaining pretrained cross-modal interactions. To suppress drift accumulated during sampling, Cross-Modal Event-Aware Spectral Trajectory Preservation combines flow saliency, aligned audio activity, multiscale low-frequency displacement, and diffusion-stage scheduling. This adaptively preserves unsupported regions while allowing intended audio-visual events. AV-FlowEdit requires no model training, external masks, or optimization-based inversion. Experiments show strong prompt alignment and temporal consistency, together with competitive audio quality and cross-modal coherence.

title: Compactness and Noncompactness for the Positive Yamabe--Escobar Problem with Minimal Boundary
abstract: We study the Yamabe--Escobar equation prescribing positive constant scalar curvature and minimal boundary. The compactness conjecture asks whether being conformally equivalent to the round hemisphere is the only obstruction for its set of positive solutions to be compact. In this paper we show that this is true for dimensions 3leq nleq 14. We show that this dimensional threshold n_*=14 is sharp by constructing in ngeq 15 nonumbilic and non-locally-conformally-flat examples of metrics in the hemisphere for which a noncompact sequence of solutions exists. We do the same for the special classes of locally conformally flat metrics, n_*^{LCF}=18, and the metrics with umbilic boundary, n_*^{umb} =20. In all three settings we also prove that the Weyl--umbilicity vanishing conjecture holds for 4leq nleq n_* and construct counterexamples in n>n_* by perturbing the noncompactness examples. To the best of the author's knowledge, these are the first locally conformally flat noncompactness constructions for the positive-scalar-curvature, minimal-boundary case of the Yamabe--Escobar equation, outside the conformal class of the round hemisphere.

title: Comparing LoRA, DoRA, and OFT for Extremely Low-Resource English–Sango Machine Translation: Adaptation Performance and Out-of-Domain Retention
abstract: Extremely low-resource machine translation poses a difficult cross-lingual adaptation problem: improving target-language performance while preserving capabilities acquired through multilingual pretraining. This study compares three mathematically distinct parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods—LoRA, DoRA, and orthogonal fine-tuning (OFT)—for English–Sango translation using NLLB-200-distilled-600M, a deterministically constructed 9000-pair corpus, and three random seeds per method. Following standard domain-adaptation practice, adaptation-test performance and out-of-domain (OOD) change were evaluated separately using a native-speaker-validated adaptation test set and FLORES+ devtest, with corpus chrF as the primary metric and paired bootstrap testing with Holm correction. All nine adapted runs scored below zero-shot NLLB-200 on the complete adaptation test and FLORES+ devtest. However, the adaptation-side estimate was composition-sensitive: the descriptive direction reversed on the 38-item A-only subset, and checkpoint selection used an all-A development set whereas the final test was B-dominated. The complete adaptation-test result is therefore treated as exploratory. By contrast, the negative FLORES+ pattern was consistent across all nine adapted runs and persisted at fixed final checkpoints, making out-of-domain degradation the most stable performance finding. The methods nevertheless differed computationally: OFT used approximately one quarter of the trainable parameters required by LoRA or DoRA, whereas LoRA achieved the shortest wall-clock training time. These results provide a controlled multi-seed comparison of structurally distinct PEFT configurations for an extremely low-resource English–Sango setting and highlight the importance of considering data quality, zero-shot baselines, training variability, and computational efficiency alongside translation performance.

title: Trust-Aware Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving IoT Intrusion Detection
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has increased the need for intrusion detection mechanisms that provide accurate threat detection while preserving privacy, resisting malicious clients, and limiting communication overhead. Existing Federated Learning (FL)-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) remain challenged by heterogeneous non-IID client data, exposure of model updates, adversarial client participation, and frequent model transmission. To address these limitations, this paper proposes FLZT-IDS (Federated Learning with Zero-Trust for Intrusion Detection in IoT). The framework employs gradient-deviation monitoring to mitigate the effects of heterogeneous client updates, while Graph Neural Networks (GNN) and an Attention-based BiLSTM capture relational and temporal attack patterns, respectively. Secure Aggregation with Local Differential Privacy (SALDP) protects transmitted model updates, whereas dynamic trust-based client filtering limits the contribution of potentially malicious participants. An adaptive communication mechanism transmits local updates only when the model change exceeds a predefined threshold, thereby reducing unnecessary communication. Experiments on CICIDS2017 and Edge-IIoTset show that FLZT-IDS achieves 97.8% and 96.2% accuracy, respectively. Compared with FL-IDS, the adaptive communication and trust-filtering mechanisms reduce cumulative communication overhead by more than 30% after 100 communication rounds. Under model-poisoning experiments with 30% malicious clients, FLZT-IDS maintains accuracies of 89.3% on CICIDS2017 and 87.1% on Edge-IIoTset, demonstrating improved robustness under the evaluated adversarial setting.

title: How different judgment strategies affect accuracy in generative AI text discrimination: BERT-based clustering and hierarchical Bayesian logistic regression
abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs)-generated texts become increasingly similar to human writing. The purpose of this study was to examine (1) how individuals distinguish between human-written and LLM-generated texts, focusing on their judgment strategies; (2) the relationship between judgment strategies and detection accuracy; and (3) the interaction effects of gender, age, and frequency of large language model (LLM) use. Methods Participants were asked to judge whether the given texts (e.g., public comments) were written by LLMs or humans and to explain their reasoning using open-ended questions. The public comments were written by humans and generated using seven LLMs (ChatGPT [4o and o1], Claude3.5, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Llama3.1, and Perplexity). First, we classified participants’ explanations of reasoning related to judgments into types using BERT-based clustering (i.e., Sentence-BERT and hierarchical cluster analysis). Results BERT-based clustering suggested four interpretable clusters. Based on their characteristic patterns, we interpreted these clusters as four hypothetical judgment strategy types and tentatively proposed that they form a conceptual continuum: (1) Unsubstantiated intuition, (2) Stylistic-Cue, (3) Syntactic-Cue, and (4) Higher-Order Pattern Recognition (HOPR). A hierarchical Bayesian logistic regression analysis revealed that the detection accuracy varied across judgment types, with the HOPR type achieving relatively higher performance than the other strategy types, although its detection accuracy remained near the chance level. Additionally, we identified interaction effects between strategy type and gender; only female participants who used the HOPR strategy showed lower detection accuracy than male participants, although the qualitative interpretation of this difference warrants further empirical investigation. Conclusion These findings emphasize the role of judgment strategies and individual differences in discriminating between human and LLM-generated content.

title: Characterization of QBER contributions of phase-encoding QKD transmitters with an optical coherent receiver
abstract: The technological development of QKD (Quantum Key Distribution) is accelerating from a research topic towards commercial deployment. QKD initiatives are increasingly addressing real-world use cases. Besides lots of literature on theory and lab-demos, first high Technology-Readiness Level systems are available. Due to the security guarantees it has to provide, the performance of any QKD implementation is particularly sensitive to any imperfections that may lead to an increase of the QBER (Quantum Bit Error Rate). Achieving high performance, or a low QBER value, constitutes a challenging engineering task, as the operating systems need to be highly optimized in many aspects. In particular, accurate phase modulation is the foundation of high system performance in case of phase-encoding protocols. In most cases, the overall QBER is measured with a QKD receiver, which accumulates errors from transmitter, quantum channel and receiver. This requires an operational transmitter system and additionally prevents the investigation of the pure transmitter output signal’s characteristics. However, for support of transmitter integration and test activities as well as for validation tasks, a more suitable method remains to be developed. In this paper, we propose such a method by making use of a coherent receiver. This device provides extended signal information including the signal amplitude and its current relative phase. Therefore, it is possible to monitor phase-encoding correctness and precision, among other relevant signal properties. We analyze the reasonability of using a coherent receiver, by outlining its capabilites to measure QBER contributors occurring in a given basic reference QKD transmitter system. Our findings indicate that employing a coherent receiver is a simple method to accelerate development and validation of phase-encoding QKD transmitter systems.

title: Locality-based moral planning with linear temporal logic values
abstract: Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) is widely used to describe problem settings of various planning tasks. Our main contribution is a locality-based way to compress the search when planning with L T L f values. With it, an exact algorithm runs in time polynomial in the size of the instance, and exponential only in two narrow widths: how many propositions are active at one time, and how many temporal obligations are open at once. We measure both on every benchmark instance. We present the methodology through the PSPACE-complete CONFLICT problem from the area of logic-based ethical planning with LTL values. The proposed methodology is relevant for e.g. structured robotic domains or automated delivery tasks. We introduce locality assumptions over propositions and actions: most propositions are indexed along an ordered local axis, each action depends on and modifies only a bounded interval, the number of global propositions is bounded, and locality constrains feasible temporal action order. Under these assumptions, we derive an exact locality-based planning algorithm and show that the substate graph supports finding shortest satisfactory plans and weighted conflict resolution. We evaluate against progression and standardized compiled-automaton baselines on a benchmark test suite. With a 120-second timeout and independent validation, the locality planner is the fastest in the main comparison family, and its time complexity is illustrated by the family with variable locality widths. The externally sourced IPC Elevators domain without locality demonstrates the limits of our approach, and we derive the precise criterion on when it is favoured over the baseline.

title: Conditioning diffusions on a terminal bearing
abstract: We study sampling of a diffusion on $[0,T]$ conditioned on its terminal position lying on a prescribed ray, i.e. on an exactly observed bearing. For a linear drift we derive closed-form expressions for the Doob $h$-function and its gradient. For a broad class of tracking models admitting a Kronecker block structure, the guiding term is obtained from a single row of a matrix exponential, and the conditioned process decomposes into independent radial and angular components. For a nonlinear drift, we construct a guided process using the $h$-function of the linear model and prove absolute continuity of the law of the true conditioned process with respect to the law of the guided process, with an explicit likelihood ratio. This result is used to devise an auxiliary particle filter for bearings observed sequentially in time without noise. Numerical experiments show that the proposed filter approximates the filtering distribution and estimates the log-likelihood considerably more accurately than the shifted Rayleigh filter, at the cost of a higher computing time.

title: System-Design Optimization of a Single-Transmitter, Single-Fiber QKD-based ITS Communication Link
abstract: Deploying QKD-based secure communication at scale requires reducing duplicated optical hardware while preserving the rate of protected user data. Earlier studies established the physical feasibility of carrying CV-QKD and classical signals over shared infrastructure, motivating a quantitative comparison between optical hardware savings and the OTP-encrypted rate. We perform this comparison by defining the secure communication rate (SCR) as the rate jointly supported by secret-key generation and classical transport, and using it to optimize a shared discrete-modulation CV-QKD link. The model combines a binomial 64-QAM security bound with a trusted receiver, protocol traffic, spectral leakage - optical power leaking into the quantum receive band - and Raman scattering. At 25 km, the asymptotic model gives an optimized SCR of 12.079 Mbps, compared with 12.095 Mbps for a separated-link reference, while reducing the transmitter and fiber counts from two to one each in the modeled direction. Increasing channel separation suppresses spectral leakage, but the resulting SCR gain diminishes once receiver bandwidth limits the rate. Under the adopted receiver-noise law, increasing the bandwidth budget from 350 to 750 MHz raises the projected 25-km SCR to 24.535 Mbps despite higher trusted electronic noise. For the studied metropolitan link, sharing saves optical resources with little rate loss, while receiver-bandwidth improvements provide greater benefit than further spectral separation. Together, these results suggest an integration path: share the transmitter and fiber, limit unwanted classical power in the quantum receive band, and increase usable receiver bandwidth where the noise budget permits.

title: Evolving Creatives with Clicks: CTR-Driven Advertising image Editing via Attribute Disentanglement and Preference Alignment
abstract: The optimization objective for e-commerce advertising creatives has shifted from aesthetic quality to online business metrics like click-through rate (CTR). Recent methods generate appealing ad images from product images by constructing CTR-based reward signals and refining prompt generation via Reinforcement Learning. Such paradigms equally penalize all attributes within an underperforming image, even though some are actually beneficial to clicks. In this work, we propose Evolving Creatives with Clicks (ECC), which reformulates creative optimization as fine-grained editing rather than generation from scratch. ECC selectively refines attributes that hurt CTR while preserving those that contribute positively. Specifically, faced with a rich attribute space across massive images, ECC first identifies 28 attributes significantly correlated with CTR via ANOVA and Random Forest regression. Based on attribute contrasts between images with disparate CTRs, we instruction-tune a prompt model to generate editing suggestions, then refine it with real click preferences since reference-derived suggestions are not uniformly beneficial. Furthermore, we introduce Consistent Preference Optimization (CPO) as ECC's preference optimization strategy, which enforces consistency across semantically equivalent shuffled suggestions to mitigate DPO overfitting and improve preference generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ECC significantly improves the CTR of ad images, outperforming state-of-the-art models by a substantial margin. The complete data pipeline, including attribute extraction and analysis, the resulting dataset, and source code will be released upon acceptance.

title: Enhanced Uncertainty Quantification Variational Autoencoders for the Solution of Bayesian Inverse Problems
abstract: Among other uses, neural networks are used to solve deterministic and Bayesian inverse problems, where variational autoencoders enable the Bayesian estimation of model parameters and their distribution from observational data allowing real-time inverse uncertainty quantification. In this work, we build upon existing research by proposing a novel loss function to train variational autoencoders. For affine forward maps, we theoretically prove that an affine transformation of the latent states of the trained variational autoencoder represents the mean and covariance of the posterior distribution of the model parameters. We validate this result through numerical tests and we show the superior accuracy and generalization performance of the proposed variational autoencoder compared with the original formulation. We test the proposed variational autoencoder on a Laplace equation, comparing it to the original formulation and to Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. The proposed variational autoencoder outperforms the original formulation in terms of accuracy and yields slightly lower errors than Markov chain Monte Carlo in estimating the posterior variance over 100 in silico generated samples, although it exhibits slightly higher errors in the posterior mean estimate. Moreover, the variational autoencoder enables the solution of Bayesian inverse problems nearly 800 times faster than Markov chain Monte Carlo.

title: TAMDIBULOQ OLTIN KONI RUDALARIDA Au–As ASSOTSIATSIYASINING AHAMIYATI
abstract: Tamdibuloq koni rudalarining geokimyoviy tahlili oltin va mishyak o‘rtasida barqaror ijobiy bog‘liqlik mavjudligini ko‘rsatdi. Asosiy rudali minerallar pirit va arsenopirit bo‘lib, oltin ko‘pincha ular bilan genetik bog‘langan. Au–As assotsiatsiyasi oltin mavjudligini va rudalanishning gidrotermal tabiatini tasdiqlaydi. Oltin asosan kvarc va kvarc-karbonat tomirlarida, shuningdek mayda kvarslashgan zonalarda uchraydi. Mishyakning yuqori anomaliyalari yashirin oltinli zonalarni prognoz qilishda muhim indikator bo‘lishi mumkin. Mazkur assotsiatsiya Tamdibuloq konida geokimyoviy qidiruv mezoni sifatida tavsiya etiladi.

title: E7 Subgroup Symmetry in Phosphorus Qubit Encoding for Biological Quantum Error Correction — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240 E8 root vectors decompose into an E7 Lie algebra (133 roots) plus a 56-dimensional E7 representation plus 56 additional roots, creating a natural hierarchical structure for quantum information. title: OQIMLI SHIFRLASH ALGORITMLARINING KRIPTOBARDOSHLIGINI KOMPLEKS BAHOLASH METODOLOGIYASI
abstract: So'nggi yillarda Internet of Things (IoT), simsiz sensor tarmoqlari, 5G/6G aloqa tizimlari va boshqa resurslari cheklangan axborot-kommunikatsiya muhitlarining jadal rivojlanishi oqimli shifrlash algoritmlariga bo'lgan ehtiyojni sezilarli darajada oshirdi. Mazkur algoritmlar yuqori tezkorlik, kam hisoblash murakkabligi va apparat resurslaridan samarali foydalanishi bilan ajralib tursa-da, ularning kriptobardoshligini kompleks baholash mavjud tadqiqotlarning dolzarb muammolaridan biri bo'lib qolmoqda. Mazkur maqolada oqimli shifrlash algoritmlarining xavfsizlik darajasini baholash uchun Boolean Dependency Graph (BDG) va Influence Matrix yondashuvlarini integratsiyalashga asoslangan yangi metodologiya taklif etiladi. Taklif etilgan metodologiya algoritmning ichki holatini grafik va matritsaviy modellar orqali tavsiflash, bitlararo funksional bog'liqliklarni aniqlash, ta'sirlarning tarqalish intensivligi va diffuziya dinamikasini miqdoriy ko'rsatkichlar asosida baholash imkonini beradi.

title: Fuzzy Ontology Reasoning over Sustainable Development Data
abstract: Sustainable-development indicators are inherently graded: a territory is not simply poor or resilient, but exhibits these characteristics to varying degrees. Consequently, policy questions are naturally expressed through vague concepts such as high unemployment, stressed neighbourhood, or green-transition readiness. This work shows how such questions can be answered through reasoning over a fuzzy Web Ontology Language (OWL 2) ontology, rather than by ad hoc data-processing scripts. Our case study is the ontology of the Sustainability Decision Framework (SDF) Project, a five-module fuzzy ontology integrating Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) statistics for the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) region with geopolitical knowledge and a fuzzy semantic layer comprising 35 linguistic datatypes and 21 composite concepts defined through weighted sums and ordered weighted averaging (OWA). The ontology contains almost 400,000 statistical observations, and its complete export into a fuzzyDL Knowledge Base comprises 2.96 million axioms; for this reason, reasoning is performed on the slices of the ontology that are relevant to each query. Reasoning is performed using fuzzy-dl-owl2, our Python re-engineering of the fuzzyDL reasoner and the Fuzzy OWL 2 framework. title: When Feature Alignment Helps, Hurts, or Washes out: Carrier-Dependent Domain Adaptation for Cherenkov Telescope Event Classification
abstract: Feature alignment domain adaptation (DA) methods such as CORAL and MMD are widely used to mitigate distribution shift between training (source) and deployment (target) domains. They are typically evaluated on a single downstream classifier, which implicitly assumes that the alignment benefit transfers across model families. We test this assumption on a controlled class-symmetric shift of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope features, with five carrier classifiers, three alignment methods, and fifteen seeds per cell. Establishing this requires first correcting an evaluation protocol that we believe to be common in benchmarks built by perturbing a single sample: when the target consist of a perturbed copy of data that the carrier was partly trained on, the measured benefit of adaptation is inflated by a factor that tracks the carrier’s capacity to memorise (from 1.0 for logistic regression to 5.7 for an unbounded-depth random forest), so that such a benchmark reports a carrier gradient whether or not one actually exists. When scored only on events that no carrier has seen, the carrier still matters (indeed, twice over): the same shift costs a hyperplane carrier 0.004 of AUC and a tree ensemble 0.006–0.008, and CORAL then recovers 58% of that loss on logistic regression, against 84–98% on the tree ensembles, a difference that RBF-kernel MMD does not show on any carrier for which the ratio is determined. A measurement of marginal sensitivity taken without any adaptation reproduces the ordering. Two effects that would be reported by a full-target protocol are absent on held-out events: a benefit growing with tree depth, and an advantage of covariance alignment over mean matching on deep trees. We propose a two-axis framework (shift symmetry × carrier marginal sensitivity), then test its class-symmetric row and give practical recommendations for evaluating and deploying domain adaptation under shift.

title: Diagnosing Generalization Boundaries in AI-Based Vulnerability Detection via Calibrated Embedding Distances
abstract: High benchmark scores in learning-based vulnerability detection mask severe degradation under distribution shifts. This paper demonstrates that calibrated embedding geometry exposes these hidden generalization boundaries on syntactically similar vulnerable and patched code pairs. An evaluation of CodeBERT and Qwen2.5-Coder across pattern, project, and temporal shifts on a strictly paired dataset reveals three main findings. First, whitened intermediate-layer embeddings with local nearest-neighbour scoring separate unfamiliar samples with a mean out-of-distribution AUROC of 0.739 (RQ1). Second, distance scores reveal a shift-specific reliability gradient where accuracy drops by over 35 percentage points and cross-project shifts cause the sharpest degradation, even though temporal shifts drift geometrically farthest (RQ2). Third, false positives on patched code systematically correlate with geometric proximity to vulnerable training neighbourhoods, increasing from 9.4% in the lowest-risk decile to 58.8% in the highest (RQ3). These calibrated distances establish a diagnostic signal that maps representation geometry directly to model degradation without requiring auxiliary models.

title: Not All Correct Fixes Run Alike: An Empirical Study of Patch Performance in Repository-Level Issue Resolution
abstract: Repository-level issue-resolution benchmarks such as SWE-bench evaluate submitted patches primarily based on whether they pass the correctness tests, leaving the runtime performance of different test-passing patches largely unexplored. Evaluating patch performance is essential but challenging since designing performance workloads for each benchmark instance is costly. However, these benchmarks already provide a natural candidate: the built-in \emph{FAIL\_TO\_PASS} (F2P) tests, which exercise the behavior affected by the issue fix. We therefore investigate whether the provided F2P tests can be repurposed to evaluate patch performance. Overall, we choose four frontier models, Claude Opus~5, GPT~5.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Qwen~3.8 Max, paired with SWE-agent to resolve the pre-filtered measurable corpus from verified splits of SWE-bench and SWE-bench-Live, yielding 262 cases with at least two different correct solutions, including the developer ground-truth patch. We then measure each solution's runtime performance in instruction count and wall-clock time on the native F2P test, and use Welch ANOVA instead of the RSD proposed in prior work as a more robust statistical discrimination criterion. We find that this methodology exhibits notable discrimination capability in runtime performance and identifies performance differences among patches in almost half of the instances. Our empirical study shows that the runtime performance of generated patches is independent of the issue resolution rate of LLMs, with nearly reversed model rankings. The case study also shows that the performance analysis reveals architectural regression in some patches that the correctness evaluation overlooked. These findings suggest that resolution rate does not adequately characterize LLMs' capability for repository-level issue resolution, motivating future evaluations to consider patch performance alongside it.

title: CB-Orchestrator: Adaptive Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents via Contextual Bandits
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in tackling complex tasks through agentic workflows. However, manually designing these workflows is labor-intensive and lacks flexibility to adapt to diverse queries. While automated workflow optimization is a promising direction, existing methods often incur expensive API costs during training-phase feedback collection. Furthermore, they fail to adaptively reuse high-quality workflows, which creates a bottleneck for both performance and cost-effectiveness. To address these limitations, we propose CB-Orchestrator, an adaptive framework that decouples workflow generation from selection. In the first stage, we construct a diverse pool of candidate workflows via evolutionary search. In the second stage, we formulate workflow selection as a Contextual Bandit problem, which enables sample-efficient learning by balancing exploration and exploitation, thereby significantly reducing the feedback required for training. During inference, the model adaptively selects the optimal workflow tailored to each query. Evaluations across five diverse benchmarks demonstrate that CB-Orchestrator consistently outperforms all baselines. Notably, on the MATH dataset, CB-Orchestrator achieves better performance than strong recent baselines while reducing training-phase API token overhead by no less than 40.55% and total end-to-end training (including workflow pool generation) token overhead by no less than 29.73%.

title: TAME-Nav: Temporal Asymmetric Mixture-of-Experts Distillation for Agile and Versatile Robot Navigation
abstract: Agile and reliable navigation is a core capability for embodied robots navigating complex spatial constraints and dynamic interactions. However, a single policy often struggles to accommodate the distinct decision-making demands of diverse scenarios. We present TAME-Nav, an asymmetric Teacher-Student navigation framework built around a temporal soft mixture of experts (Soft-MoE). The Teacher combines clean observations with causally maintained dynamic-obstacle tracks to construct privileged representations, while the Student learns complementary navigation features from corrupted observation histories through temporal encoding, soft expert routing, and latent distillation. Procedural scenario generation and parallel task-level simulation broaden training coverage, while deployment-informed asymmetric domain randomization supports sim-to-real transfer. Across in-distribution and unseen compositional scenarios, TAME-Nav achieves higher success rates, lower collision rates, and higher navigation scores than representative baselines. On a real quadruped robot, it completes all twenty trials across local-trap escape and narrow-passage navigation with sudden dynamic obstacles, with only one minor contact.

title: NumLang: A research programming language with a higher-order supercompiler, polyhedral recurrence solver, and Lean 4 mechanized correctness proofs.
abstract: NumLang is an experimental compiled research language and program optimizer implemented in Rust. It integrates multiple program transformation paradigms into a unified SSA Mid-Level Intermediate Representation (MIR) pipeline: Hamilton-style Global Distillation: Inter-procedural process tree distillation that folds across distinct call sites to eliminate intermediate algebraic structures (e.g. multi-stage stream and tree traversals). Multi-Result Supercompilation (MRSC): Bounded configuration hypergraph search paired with Pareto-optimal candidate selection under register and instruction cost models. Polyhedral Recurrence Detection: Algebraic difference engine detecting constant forward differences and companion matrices, collapsing arithmetic progressions and linear recurrences. Reynolds Defunctionalization: Type-directed whole-program closure conversion mapping higher-order lambdas into first-order tagged variants with static dispatches. Lazy Thunk / Codata Supercompilation: Demand-driven symbolic forcing over SSA MIR converting lazy producer-consumer stream pipelines into scalar register loops. Self-Applicable Specialization: A subset specializer (src/stdlib/minspec.nl) structured for Futamura projections (specializing interpreters into compiled residuals). Lean 4 Mechanized Operational Models: Formal machine-checked small-step operational semantics and semantic preservation proofs with zero sorry and zero unproven axioms.

title: Model-Dependent Reliability of Self-Reported Confidence under a Shared Black-Box MT Protocol
abstract: This paper studies a trustworthy-AI reliability question for black-box language-model services: can one shared confidence threshold be reused across models under a common protocol? I evaluate English→German translation with eight models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google on 500 WMT17 sentences(4,000translation confidence pairs) at temperature 0. Quality is scored with sentence-level chrF, and low quality is operationally defined as the within-model bottom 20% tail. Relative to that target, expected calibration error (ECE) and mismatch@0.9 differ widely despite similar mean chrF (54.0–60.1): ECE ranges from 0.076 to 0.180, and mismatch@0.9 ranges from 0.2% to 18.2%. The released snapshot also shows uneven parse-warning burden (443/4000 rows; 11.1%), an implementation-level con found for cross-model reliability comparisons. The central claim is therefore practical and scoped: under this shared protocol and operational target, self-reported confidence is model-dependent and non-portable as a common probability scale, so a fixed threshold does not induce comparable routing/abstention operating points. Supplementary analyses indicate that model specific isotonic remapping can reduce ECE but does not restore portability. Limitations are explicit: operational (not semantic) target, no bundled COMET/xCOMET checkpoints, no completed semantic-audit labels, and no bundled non-baseline prompt-variant outputs.

title: Investigation on Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Model Using Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is challenged by high-dimensional input features that cause redundancy and overfitting. To address this, we propose a short-term PV forecasting model integrating a CNN-LSTM architecture with active subspace-based global sensitivity analysis, which quantitatively evaluates feature influence via gradient information. Using operational data from a PV plant, we compare three feature selection schemes across CNN-LSTM, CNN, and LSTM models. For CNN-LSTM, the baseline yields an average R2 of 0.8769 (RMSE: 134.2 kW), while Pearson-based selection slightly reduces performance (R2 = 0.8646, RMSE: 140.7 kW). In contrast, the active subspace method achieves an average R2 of 0.9341 (RMSE: 83.6 kW), representing improvements of 6.52% and 8.04% over the no-selection and Pearson schemes, respectively. Overfitting is mitigated and convergence accelerates. The method also shows consistent improvements on CNN and LSTM models, confirming its model-agnostic effectiveness. These results demonstrate that the active subspace method is an efficient and interpretable feature engineering tool for PV forecasting.

title: ANALISIS TOLERANSI BERAGAMA DI KOTA SALATIGA MENGGUNAKAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHIE NAIVE BAYES DAN RANDOM FOREST
abstract: Perkembangan media sosial memberikan ruang bagi masyarakat untuk menyampaikan opini terkait berbagai isu sosial, termasuk toleransi beragama. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis persepsi masyarakat terhadap toleransi beragama di Kota Salatiga menggunakan pendekatan analisis sentimen berbasis machine learning. Data penelitian diperoleh dari platform Twitter melalui proses crawling dengan jumlah sekitar 670 komentar. Dataset kemudian diproses melalui tahapan text pre-processing yang meliputi cleaning, case folding, normalisasi, tokenisasi, dan stemming sebelum dilakukan ekstraksi fitur menggunakan metode TF-IDF. Proses klasifikasi sentimen dilakukan dengan membandingkan tiga algoritma, yaitu Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes, dan Random Forest. Evaluasi performa model menggunakan metrik akurasi, precision, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa opini masyarakat didominasi oleh sentimen positif yang merepresentasikan citra Kota Salatiga sebagai wilayah dengan tingkat toleransi beragama yang tinggi. Naive Bayes memperoleh nilai akurasi tertinggi sebesar 92%, namun Random Forest menunjukkan kemampuan klasifikasi yang lebih stabil dalam menangani ketidakseimbangan data. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa penerapan teknik text mining mampu menghasilkan informasi berbasis data digital yang relevan untuk mendukung pemahaman kondisi sosial masyarakat secara objektif Kata kunci: Analisis Sentimen, Toleransi Beragama, Machine Learning, Twitter.

title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions
abstract: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. However, samples generated from different random seeds may remain visually similar, limiting creative exploration. Existing approaches can increase variation, but often require additional optimization or sampling overhead, while stronger perturbations may introduce distortions that degrade image quality or prompt alignment. We propose a training-free method that leverages the local pullback geometry induced by the mapping from the conditioning-embedding space to the image space to identify directions of maximal output sensitivity. By steering different sampling trajectories along these directions, we encourage distinct generations while maintaining consistency with the conditioning signal. Experiments on MS-COCO and BrushNet show the efficacy of the method in improving diversity on prompt-conditioned image generation and inpainting.

title: What We Talk About When We Talk About Emotion Editing
abstract: Emotional image editing aims to change the emotion a scene conveys while preserving its essential content. Because the same scene can support different emotional interpretations, achieving an emotional goal requires visual changes grounded in the source context. Motivated by the Component Process Model, which links emotional responses to event appraisal, we investigate neural representations as a reference for these editing decisions. Using TRIBE v2, an fMRI encoding model, we analyze 400 source-target pairs across eight emotion categories. Hidden states from EmoEdit, EmoEditor, and AffectDelta correspond more strongly to predicted target-image responses in visual regions than in affect-related regions. This imbalance motivates ROI-ReFT, which combines source visual responses as a content reference with a predicted affective response change as an editing direction. Two interacting branches use both conditions to guide a frozen editor throughout generation. Predicted responses of the generated image supervise affective change and constrain visual drift. On a post hoc selected subset of 400 editing requests, ROI-ReFT achieves 91.75% target-emotion accuracy and 83.25% joint success, with the same output both matching the target emotion and reaching source-output DINO-I of at least 0.80. Our code and dataset will be publicly released.

Hidden states from EmoEdit, EmoEditor, and AffectDelta correspond more strongly to predicted target-image responses in visual regions than in affect-related regions. This imbalance motivates ROI-ReFT, which combines source visual responses as a content reference with a predicted affective response change as an editing direction. Two interacting branches use both conditions to guide a frozen editor throughout generation. Predicted responses of the generated image supervise affective change and constrain visual drift. On a post hoc selected subset of 400 editing requests, ROI-ReFT achieves 91.75% target-emotion accuracy and 83.25% joint success, with the same output both matching the target emotion and reaching source-output DINO-I of at least 0.80. Our code and dataset will be publicly released.

title: Absence of Continuous Spin Particles in Superstring Theory
abstract: The study of continuous spin particles, as general low-energy implications of relativity and quantum mechanics, has intensified in recent years with potential experimental signatures. In this note we show that these particles are absent in perturbative super-string theories, generalising a result in arXiv:1302.4771 to the supersymmetric case. This stands out as a general low-energy prediction of all perturbative superstring constructions.

title: Quantum Sampling and Moment Estimation for Transformed Gaussian Random Fields
abstract: Abstract. We present a quantum algorithm for efficiently sampling transformed Gaussian random fields in [Formula: see text]-dimensional domains, based on an enhanced version of the classical moving average method. Pointwise transformations enforcing boundedness are essential for using Gaussian random fields in quantum computation and arise naturally, for example, in modeling coefficient fields representing microstructures in partial differential equations. Generating this microstructure from its few statistical parameters directly on the quantum device bypasses the input bottleneck. Our method enables an efficient quantum representation of the resulting random field and prepares a quantum state that approximates it to accuracy [Formula: see text] in time [Formula: see text]. Combined with amplitude estimation and a quantum pseudorandom number generator, this leads to algorithms for estimating linear and nonlinear observables, including mixed and higher-order moments, with total complexity [Formula: see text]. We illustrate the theoretical findings through numerical experiments on simulated quantum hardware.

title: Legendre pairs of lengths 169, 195 and 205
abstract: We construct cyclic Legendre pairs of lengths 169, 195 and 205, and hence Hadamard matrices of orders 340, 392 and 412. In each pair the negative supports of the two sequences are unions of orbits of a group of multipliers, so a short table of difference counts proves the Legendre equations. At lengths 169 and 205 the second sequence is the first decimated by a square root of −1. At length 195 the sequences are chosen independently, and in no equivalent pair is one a decimation of the other. Exactly 32 normalized ordered pairs of length 195 have both sequences fixed by the multiplier group of order 12 used in the construction, and they are all equivalent. At length 205 we classify the pairs equivalent to a pair with a16i = ai and bi = aui, where u2 ≡ −1 (mod 205): there are exactly six equivalence classes. The six resulting Hadamard matrices are pairwise inequivalent, even up to transposition. Each has an automorphism group of order 4100, and the six remain pairwise inequivalent after any number of Sylvester doublings. The census, the classification and the matrix results rest on four exhaustive computations, each carried out by two separately written programs. The proofs are verified in Lean, with these four computations as the only hypotheses. The source archive contains the pairs and the six order-412 matrices, the outputs of both programs for each of the four computations, the programs that check them, the Lean development and the LaTeX source. Its README gives a command for each check; verification/check_witnesses.py checks every pair in the article and its Hadamard matrix in about a second with Python alone. The article and data are licensed under CC BY 4.0; the programs and the Lean development are licensed under MIT, as LICENSES.md in the archive states. Use of generative AI. OpenAI's ChatGPT and Codex, together with Anthropic's Claude, were used in developing the mathematics, writing and checking the programs and the Lean proofs, and preparing the text. The author is responsible for the mathematical statements, computations and references. Version 1.0.1. Corrects an out-of-date sentence on order 668 in the introduction, gives the kernel step of Theorem 7.5 the argument checked in Lean, and describes the archive contents exactly. The results are unchanged.

title: Rotate the Router: A Control for Expert-Specialisation Claims in Mixture-of-Experts Models, Demonstrated on Five, and What Its Readings Do Not License
abstract: Claims that a Mixture-of-Experts model routes by domain are made in two literatures that never check the same thing. Analyses of expert specialisation report separation without asking what an uninformative router would produce on the same hidden states; systems that compose domain experts into an MoE report task scores without reporting whether the router they trained routes by domain at all. The control. Take the model's own gate and rotate it by a Haar-random orthogonal matrix. This preserves every singular value and every row norm and changes only the gate's orientation to the representation, giving a router that is linear, identically conditioned, and has learned nothing. It costs eight forward sweeps of a corpus, needs no training and no second model, and applies to any MoE whose gate can be read. The rotated gate is a reference distribution, not an intervention: it is applied to hidden states captured from the unmodified model. On five models the rotated gate separates topics 17.4-26.0x above its own null, so a large share of what is normally reported as specialisation is available to an arbitrary projection. What the trained gate adds beyond it spans thirteenfold: 4.34x and 3.82x for two OLMoE checkpoints, 1.14x for Granite-3.1-3b-a800m, while Mixtral-8x7B falls below its own rotations at 0.33x and BAR-5x7B, a model assembled expressly from separately trained domain experts, at 0.45x. Read without the control, all five look specialised. Routing weight is not importance. BAR's composed router places 62.8% of its weight on a frozen anchor and 0.14% on its maths and code experts together. That small share is not smallness of contribution: disabling the maths expert costs 30 points of GSM8K accuracy where disabling the anchor costs 11.7. Every size-of-effect claim here rests on an intervention rather than on a routing statistic. What the statistic does not predict. Installing a rotated gate and running the model destroys it: 0/60 on GSM8K for BAR, for Granite and for OLMoE-Instruct alike. Those three span the full thirteenfold range of the statistic, in both of its directions, and two orders of magnitude of its absolute value, so neither the sign nor the size of the routing statistic predicts the behavioural outcome. The two base checkpoints cannot be scored zero-shot, since their generations run on into questions of their own, so they are prompted with eight worked examples and stopped at the answer they state. Both collapse: OLMoE 9/60 to 0/60, Mixtral 28/60 to 1/60. Mixtral's answer loss moves only 1.54 nats where the other four lose 7.62 to 8.74, so a loss that barely moves is not evidence that a router intervention was harmless. Reassigning which expert each gate row points at, at exactly matched parameter mass with nothing removed, is eventually fatal on every model tested, but where the threshold sits is model-specific: averaged over three draws each, Granite loses half its accuracy when two experts of forty are displaced, while OLMoE keeps 61% of its own at four times that displacement. A rule derived from an exhaustive sweep of BAR's 44 derangements separated them perfectly and is falsified when tested on Granite; the paper reports it as falsified. What a large reading does not license. No domain in three models tolerates losing a single expert across eighteen domain-model pairs, so a gap is not a route to a smaller domain model. Refitting only the routers, 0.03% of parameters, gives a gain reliable under an exact 720-assignment null but worth only 0.18-0.67% of baseline loss. One methodological result: the same refit places a model at rank 683/720 and at rank 1/720 depending only on whether the learning rate equalises nominal step size or realised router movement. What the routing distribution actually is. BAR's gate has no bias term, so each row's logit splits cleanly into a part identical for every token and a part content can move. The constant part ALONE reproduces the measured weight split, correlating with the observed shares at r = 0.9997 in logs, and its spread across experts is 7.52 logits where the largest content term, measured per token, reaches 2.27 at three standard deviations. Content cannot carry an expert across the 5.60-logit gap between the three favoured experts and maths and code, but it can swap neighbours: safety and tool-use sit 0.54 logits apart. The anchor is the most rigidly fixed of the five, at 26 times its per-token content term (155 at document granularity); maths and code are the most content-sensitive rows in the gate, doing the routing work from a floor seven logits down. A minimal composition matches the whole model. No domain expert stands alone: routing every problem to the maths expert scores 0/60 on GSM8K, as does routing to the code expert. Only the frozen anchor functions by itself, at 20.0%. But anchor plus maths reaches 42/60 against the full five-expert mixture's 40/60, a two-problem difference we report as not-worse rather than better. Two of five experts do the work of five, and the three holding 37% of the routing weight between them are the droppable ones. This is the paper's one positive modularity result, and it is the mirror of the retention arm: a router can compose modularity that was built in, and cannot manufacture modularity that is not there. A safety expert that barely responds to content is examined across eight stimulus classes. Jailbreak framing moves it 1.01x and harmful content 1.11x. The paper states what that does not establish: the test uses jailbreak-shaped prompts rather than verified-successful attacks. All experiments ran on Apple Silicon with 32 GB unified memory.

title: Efficient Exact Gaussian Process Inference via Incremental Block-Matrix Identity Updates
abstract: Exact gaussian process (GP) inference scales cubically in data size, posing a severe bottleneck for applications that require repeated GP kernel inversions, such as time series models like gaussian process factor analysis (GPFA), where data size can vary across trials. To address this, we introduce an algorithmic variant of GPFA that shares computations across trials of different lengths. It does so by leveraging block-matrix identities to incrementally reuse inverses and determinants from smaller GP kernel matrices to accelerate computations on larger ones without sacrificing numerical precision. By casting successive trial-length extensions as Schur-complement updates, our method reduces the cost of each new inversion to depend only on the size difference among matrices. We demonstrate that this approach yields more than two times speed-ups over direct and persymmetric inversion baselines on both synthetic data sets and data from neural recordings. In an additional comparison to sparse inducing-point GPFA, sparse inference reduced inference time for small inducing sets at the expense of worse model fits, while optimizing inducing locations was slower than our exact GPFA variant when the optimization cost was included. We also provide a scikit-learn-compatible Python GPFA package, BlockInverseGPFA, and introduce a variance-explained metric for model evaluation.

title: Probabilistic Ship Trajectory Forecasting using Transformer Models on AIS Data
abstract: Anticipation of vessel trajectories is an essential task when navigating at sea. This applies to both human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. Trajectory forecasting enables sub-routines such as collision avoidance to assess the situation and react accordingly in time. This paper investigates Transformer and Performer models for trajectory prediction of surface vessels in confined waters. Using widely available position data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), candidate models are trained and evaluated. Historical information on how other vessels have moved in the local area surrounding each agent is conveyed using positional heat maps. The heat maps are generated using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and encoded with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) before entering the Transformer models. The models are trained with quantile loss to efficiently obtain a model-aware prediction interval, as this is crucial for timely collision avoidance. The proposed model architectures are shown to greatly outperform previous work while the inclusion of local heat maps enables the prediction of vessel movement that is not otherwise indicated from the previous positions.

title: Decoding Register Tokens Preserves Global Scene Details
abstract: Pretrained vision transformers learn structured image representations spanning spatial patch tokens and non-spatial tokens. Recent analyses suggest that non-spatial register tokens encode global scene properties such as illumination, blur, and style. Yet patch-based image decoders discard these outputs, leaving the decoder to recover image appearance from patches alone. We investigate whether retaining register features improves decoding when the complete spatial patch representation is already available. We study this question using representation autoencoders (RAEs) with frozen register-equipped encoders. Our decoder processes four register tokens together with all patch tokens through joint self-attention. Appearance probes, paired reconstruction-error analysis, and fixed-decoder register substitutions examine which global image properties are accessible from registers and how their values affect reconstructed pixels. For generation, we train a multi-head attention pooling (MHAP) predictor to recover register features from sampled patches, keeping the pretrained diffusion model and its samples unchanged. On ImageNet-1K, our ViT-B decoders achieve mean reconstruction FIDs of 0.472 with DINOv2 and 0.442 with DINOv3, reductions of 9.5% and 5.2% relative to their respective patch-only baselines. The corresponding PSNRs are 19.73 and 20.54 dB. For generation, our DINOv2 models achieve a mean FID of 1.641, 9.8% below the patch-only baseline on identical sampled patches.

title: Block encoding of semiseparable matrices via their generators
abstract: We present an explicit quantum circuit that constructs a block encoding of a generator-representable semiseparable (one-pair) matrix directly from its two generators. For an $N\times N$ semiseparable matrix with $N=2^{n}$, the circuit uses $2n+2$ ancilla qubits and has $O({\rm polylog} N)$ depth, and it realizes a $(2\sqrt{N},\,2n+2,\,2 \sqrt{2}\ \varepsilon)$-block encoding, where $\varepsilon$ is controlled by the accuracy of the state-preparation routines that load the generators. The building blocks of the circuit are cyclic shifts, swaps, and Hadamard gates, each admitting an efficient implementation through the binary decomposition of the relevant indices.

title: CliQ-RRG: Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation
abstract: Radiology reports are essential for diagnostic reasoning and patient care, yet their manual preparation is time-consuming and cognitively demanding. Automatic radiology report generation (RRG) offers a scalable alternative, but existing models often produce lengthy, unstructured narratives that overlook diagnostic cues and multi-view information. We present Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation (CliQ-RRG), a unified two-stage framework for interpretable and clinically grounded reporting. In Stage 1, CliQ-RRG employs a Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment module that aligns image and text representations using predicted disease embeddings, reinforced by a Prior-Guided Attention Module (PrAM) to capture multi-view dependencies across current and prior scans. In Stage 2, GraphRAG-guided retrieval augments intermediate textual representations with graph-grounded clinical evidence, and a large language model restructures them into concise, interpretable question-answer (QA) pairs with diagnostic summaries. Experiments on two public chest X-ray benchmarks demonstrate that CliQ-RRG consistently outperforms prior methods across both lexical and clinical metrics, generating accurate and clinically coherent QA-style radiology reports. Code is available at: https://github.com/chandravardhan-singh-raghaw/CliQ-RRG.

title: GLRMask: Constrained Decoding with Boolean Array Weighted Automata
abstract: Grammar-constrained decoding (GCD) forces LLM outputs to conform to a specified grammar. During sampling, GCD applies a mask to the model’s next-token distribution, ruling out tokens that would leave no grammar-valid continuation. For context-free grammars, token admissibility under this mask depends on the parser state. Existing CFG-capable systems commonly resolve this dependence by exploring parser behavior online during mask generation. For delimiter-rich JSON-schema workloads this online work is often small enough that optimized systems are already practical; it becomes a sharper issue for tail predictability and for grammars whose lexer/parser interactions are less JSON-like. This paper presents GLRMask, a GCD system that compiles the parser-state-dependent part of token admissibility ahead of time. Given a grammar and a vocabulary, GLRMask constructs a deterministic weighted automaton, the Parser DWA, whose input symbols are parser-stack symbols and whose weights are Boolean masks over lexer-state/token pairs. At runtime, mask generation traverses the graph-structured parser stack through this automaton one symbol at a time, with each transition’s Boolean weight narrowing a running set of allowed tokens as it is taken. The traversal treats the parser stack as read-only. State-mutating parser actions are confined to commit, which advances the parser with the sampled token. evidence.title: GLRMask: Constrained Decoding with Boolean Array Weighted Automata
evidence.abstract: Grammar-constrained decoding (GCD) forces LLM outputs to conform to a specified grammar. During sampling, GCD applies a mask to the model’s next-token distribution, ruling out tokens that would leave no grammar-valid continuation. For context-free grammars, token admissibility under this mask depends on the parser state. Existing CFG-capable systems commonly resolve this dependence by exploring parser behavior online during mask generation. This paper presents GLRMask, a GCD system that compiles the parser-state-dependent part of token admissibility ahead of time. Given a grammar and a vocabulary, GLRMask constructs a deterministic weighted automaton, the Parser DWA, whose input symbols are parser-stack symbols and whose weights are Boolean masks over lexer-state/token pairs. At runtime, mask generation traverses the graph-structured parser stack through this automaton one symbol at a time, with each transition’s Boolean weight narrowing a running set of allowed tokens as it is taken. The traversal treats the parser stack as read-only. State-mutating parser actions are confined to commit, which advances the parser with the sampled token. On 2,925,983 aligned token positions from JSONSchemaBench, Static GLRMask has a median Time Between Masks of 2.54 µs, a p99 of 9.54 µs and a maximum of 59.3 µs, compared with 8.71 µs, 379.6 µs and 7.84 ms for llguidance.

title: IBORALARNI MATNDAN ANIQLASH VA IKKI TILLI EKVIVALENTLIGINI BAHOLASHDA ONTOLOGIYAGA ASOSLANGAN MATEMATIK MODEL
abstract: Maqolada oʻzbek va turk iboralarini matndan avtomatik aniqlash hamda ularning oʻzaro ekvivalentlik darajasini baholash uchun ontologiyaga asoslangan matematik model taklif etiladi. Model ikki tilli bilimlar bazasiga tayanadi. Unda oʻzbek tilining 2 098 ta va turk tilining 2 496 ta iborasi rasmiylashtirilgan, ular oʻrtasida 3 193 ta tekshirilgan ekvivalentlik munosabati oʻrnatilgan va toʻrt darajali shkala qoʻllanilgan. Ontologik bilim mashinaviy oʻrganish usullariga ikki yoʻl bilan kiritilgan, ya'ni belgilar toʻplamini kengaytirish va aprior taqsimotni shakllantirish orqali. Haqiqiy korpusda oʻtkazilgan tajribalar ontologik bilim kiritilganda aniqlash sifati barqaror oʻsishini va bashorat noaniqligi kamayishini koʻrsatdi.
