title: Fault-tolerant execution of error-corrected quantum algorithms
abstract: Scaling up quantum algorithms to tackle high-impact problems in science and industry requires quantum error correction and fault tolerance. While progress has been made in experimentally realizing error-corrected primitives, the end-to-end execution of logical quantum algorithms using only fault-tolerant (FT) components has remained out of reach. We demonstrate the FT and error-corrected execution of two quantum algorithms, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm applied to the Poisson equation, on Quantinuum H2 and Helios trapped-ion quantum processors using the $[[7,1,3]]$ Steane code. For QAOA circuits on 5 and 6 logical qubits, we show performance improvements from increasing the number of QAOA layers and the number of $T$ gates used to approximate logical rotations, despite increased physical circuit complexity. We further show that QAOA circuits with up to 8 logical qubits and 9 logical $T$ gates perform similarly to unencoded circuits. For the largest QAOA circuits we run, with 12 logical (97 physical) qubits and 2132 physical two-qubit gates, we still observe better-than-random performance. Finally, we show that adding active QEC cycles and increasing the repeat-until-success limit of state preparation subroutines can improve the performance of a quantum algorithm, thereby demonstrating critical capabilities of scalable FT quantum computation. Our results are enabled by an FT logical $T$ gate implementation with an infidelity of $\sim 2.6(4)\times10^{-3}$ and dynamic circuits with measurement-dependent feedback. Our work demonstrates near-break-even performance of complex, error-corrected algorithmic quantum circuits using only FT components.

title: AI-Powered Personalised Mobile Learning Using Large Language Models: Design, Implementation, and a Simulation-Based Feasibility Evaluation
abstract: The significance of mobile learning (m-learning) has been greatly highlighted by the advent of technology due to its flexibility, accessibility and capability of being used to learn at any time and place. The development of Large Language Models (LLMs) offers great potential for creating adaptive, conversational and content-aware learning experiences via mobile apps. Most existing mobile-learning systems, however, still provide largely static content and shallow personalisation, which limits sustained learner engagement and adaptive support. This paper presents the design and implementation of an Android-based, LLM-powered personalised m-learning platform that integrates four components: a conversational tutoring agent, an Item-Response-Theory (IRT)-based adaptive quiz engine, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) content-recommendation module, and an analytics-driven feedback loop. We describe the system architecture, the prompt-orchestration and knowledge-tracing pipelines, and a rigorous quasi-experimental evaluation protocol (pre-/post-test, System Usability Scale (SUS), and engagement analytics) designed for a controlled classroom deployment. To validate the core algorithmic contributions prior to human-subject trials, we conduct two simulation-based feasibility studies: (i) a synthetic-learner simulation comparing the adaptive difficulty engine against a static item sequence and (ii) a retrieval-precision benchmark comparing RAG-based content recommendation against keyword-matching on a synthetic tagged corpus. The adaptive engine delivered quiz items within the optimal challenge zone (0.4 < P(correct) < 0.8) for 77.8% of interactions, compared with 40.8% for the static baseline, while the RAG recommender achieved substantially higher retrieval precision at every cut-off (P@10 = 0.845 versus 0.483 for keyword matching). These results provide algorithmic evidence that the proposed adaptive and retrieval components behave as intended and motivate the full-scale classroom evaluation described in the protocol. The paper concludes with a discussion of design implications, limitations, and a concrete plan for the human-subject study and future extensions of the platform.

title: Responsible AI- Enabled Innovation: A Conversation Starter for Victoria’s Innovation Ecosystem
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming a general-purpose capability for innovation. Victoria should ensure that founders and innovators across all sectors, not only AI-native startups, can use it to discover opportunities, develop and test ventures, improve productivity, and grow responsibly. This conversation starter proposes a practical agenda for inquiry and action. It invites innovators, investors, researchers, industry partners, universities, accelerators and government to work together to identify valuable applications, capability gaps, appropriate safeguards and effective support mechanisms for responsible AI-enabled innovation. AI can lower the time, cost and expertise required to research opportunities, generate concepts, develop prototypes and operate new ventures. However, faster experimentation does not necessarily produce stronger innovation. The opportunity is therefore not simply to increase AI adoption but to help innovators combine AI’s speed and reach with human judgement, domain expertise, engagement with users and affected communities, proportionate safeguards and clear accountability. AI use is expanding across Australian businesses and is particularly associated with innovation-active firms. At the same time, access to expertise, secure infrastructure, legal and intellectual-property advice, validation opportunities, mentors and investment networks remains uneven. Without coordinated action, well-resourced ventures may be better positioned to capture AI’s benefits, while smaller and under-supported innovators face greater risks of superficial adoption and preventable mistakes. Victoria already has significant research, sector, startup, commercialisation and investment capabilities. The immediate opportunity is to connect these existing strengths and build a responsible AI-enabled innovation layer across the ecosystem, not to create another standalone organisation or duplicate established programs. The immediate request is to convene interested partners to refine the agenda, identify priority sectors and use cases, determine suitable pilot opportunities, and agree on roles, resources and measures of success. The intended outcome is a practical foundation for helping Victorian innovators use AI to develop ventures that are differentiated, evidence-based, commercially credible, socially valuable and worthy of trust.

The intended outcome is a practical foundation for helping Victorian innovators use AI to develop ventures that are differentiated, evidence-based, commercially credible, socially valuable and worthy of trust.

title: Spec2VEC : Interpretable Spectral Representations of Planetary Signals in Vector Spaces
abstract: Summary The application of machine learning to planetary geophysics is frequently bottlenecked by a scarcity of labeled data and the complexity of non-stationary seismo-acoustic signals. While deep learning offers powerful feature extraction, it requires massive datasets that are rarely available for phenomena like Martian quakes or deep-ocean volcanism. Consequently, researchers often rely on unsupervised machine learning or hand-engineered features that are typically impoverished or hard to interpret. To resolve this, we introduce Spec2VEC, a framework that transforms parameter-dependent TFRs into a robust, interpretable, and high-dimensional vector space. Spec2VEC treats spectrograms not merely as energy distributions but as structured, textured images, and extracts physics-informed, dataset-agnostic features without requiring massive training loops. The framework systematically extracts a feature vector using two novel pathways: (1) a Textural path that utilizes Hilbert space-filling curves to map 2D spectral patterns into 1D sequences for advanced information-theoretic analysis (e.g., permutation entropy, fractal dimension); and (2) a Spatial path driven by PDFSI (Probabilistic Distribution Fitting for Signal Identification), a novel probabilistic pre-conditioning engine that quantifies spatial connectivity by dynamically separating coherent signal modes from stochastic noise. We validate this feature space on a comprehensive benchmark of complex synthetic wavefields and two real-world examples: an Exotic Seismic Events Catalog (ESEC) and a Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) dataset. Spec2VEC provides objective features for information discrimination and enables highly accurate classification of the diverse geophysical signal classes present in the ESEC catalog. Furthermore, application on the high data volume DAS dataset confirms its computational efficiency and domain-agnostic capability to isolate anomalous seismic arrivals from background noise. Ultimately, Spec2VEC bridges the interpretability of classical signal processing with the discriminative power of modern representation learning, providing a reliable, interpretable foundation for automated discovery across the geosciences.

title: AI and Corporate Strategy: HealthCheckAI
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) transforms operational excellence from a slow-moving quality-improvement initiative to a continuous adaptive source of competitive advantage. HealthCheckAI functions more like the human body's own intelligence: constantly sensing, adapting, and evolving without conscious effort. HealthCheckAI transforms organizational operations through three fundamental capabilities to create “evolutionary intelligence”. They are omnidirectional sensing, adaptive simulation, and continuous reconfiguration. Organizations that successfully implement HealthCheckAI transform operational excellence from a static achievement to a dynamic capability, called as operational evolvability. If HealthCheckAI is the organization's operating system for adaptive excellence, Adaptive Risk Intelligence Architecture (ARIA) is its financial immune system. What makes ARIA distinct is its operating environment. Internal risks include compliance failures, communication breakdowns, and data integrity issues. Chief financial officers and Chief risk officers must also manage external risks, from market volatility to shifting regulatory landscapes.

title: Detection of extremely rare dead cells in fluorescence microscopy images
abstract: Dead cell detection in fluorescence microscopy is essential for phenotypic screening and drug efficacy assessment. However, automated identification remains challenging due to signal variability, optical artifacts, and colocalization ambiguities across multiple channels. Markers that define nuclear boundaries do not neatly coincide spatially or temporally with apoptotic markers. Furthermore, marker accumulation kinetics vary across individual cells and apoptosis stages, making universal thresholds unreliable. We present a systematic comparison of several computational approaches for detecting apoptotic cells in nucleus-stained specimens: (1) heuristic methods using intensity thresholds, distributions, correlations, and domain guidance; (2) classification using numerical features (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM) and image features (ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0); and (3) anomaly detection, also using numerical features (Isolation Forest, one-class SVM and PCA reconstruction) and image features (convolutional autoencoders and Deep SVDD). Using a dataset of 258 images containing 65,527 cells/nuclei across multiple scenes with 243 manually annotated ground truth dead cells, we evaluate each method on metrics such as PR-AUC, Precision, Recall, F1-score, and macro-F1. Our results indicate that classification using image features (deep learning) and numerical features (traditional) achieved the best performance, with ResNet-18 and XGBoost significantly outperforming manually designed heuristics and anomaly detection methods. Our findings demonstrate that such biomedical problems remain highly challenging to solve even with the state-of-the-art computational and learning techniques. We aim to provide an effective decision-support tool to researchers while tackling such problems either fully-automatically or in a human-in-the-loop setting as an aide to domain scientists.

title: MHR-Router: Multimodal Heterogeneous Retrieval-Enhanced Adaptive Routing for VLM Inference
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit complementary capabilities, yet selecting the most suitable expert for a given image-question query remains challenging due to heterogeneous multimodal inputs and varying expert strengths. Existing routing approaches rely on text-based cues or static model profiles, failing to capture fine-grained visual evidence and expert-specific failure patterns. To address this, we propose MHR-Router, a multimodal heterogeneous retrieval-enhanced adaptive routing framework for VLM inference. It accurately dispatches each multimodal query to the most suitable VLM expert via local retrieval evidence. MHR-Router consists of two stages: (1) Multimodal Routing Representation, which fuses frozen multimodal features into a comprehensive query representation; and (2) Heterogeneous Retrieval-Enhanced Adaptive Routing, which retrieves expert-specific success and failure memories as local evidence and employs a shared scorer to adaptively select the optimal expert. Experiments show that MHR-Router effectively achieves heterogeneous modality routing and consistently improves accuracy over traditional baselines.

title: Redirecting Teacher Supervision: Temporal-Response-Guided Latent Distillation for Video-Language Models
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers capabilities through teacher predictions on student-generated sequences, as studied by GKD and MiniLLM for language models and Video-OPD for video tasks. We ask how internal supervision can further support temporal learning. Direct hidden-state alignment does not explicitly use the student's temporal responses to choose a supervision direction. We propose Temporal-Response Guidance (TRG), which measures representation responses to local temporal perturbations, adds the teacher correction's projection onto their span back to the original correction, and restores its original norm. The projection is not normalized separately, and correction components outside the response space are retained. With an orthogonal tangent projector and a detached target, TRG changes the supervision direction while preserving the cosine-loss value and aligned-representation gradient norm at target construction. On TempCompass, Video-MME, MVBench, and Video-MMMU, TRG improves the 4B student's macro accuracy by 2.86 percentage points over the reported output-only OPD baseline.

title: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems
abstract: Multi-agent systems are increasingly used to solve coding tasks by coordinating agents that share code and plans. These agents are often optimized with reinforcement learning (RL) using automated evaluators, but bypassing evaluation can earn reward without producing a genuine solution. Prior work has largely treated reward hacking as a single-agent failure. In this work, we show that a reward-hacking strategy elicited in one agent can propagate to others and affect system coordination. Across four open-weight backbones, coding RL elicits and amplifies reward hacking in two settings: explicit mechanism descriptions in the system prompt and mid-training that models upstream exposure to facts about the coding environment. Using post-RL agents from the mid-training setting as sources, we observe propagation through code and shared memory, and across roles through natural-language plans. Even agents based on small open-weight models induce reward hacking in stronger closed-weight targets. On hard tasks, propagation can intensify along a transmission chain after the original source leaves as the code acquires more persuasive justifications. We also theoretically analyze conditions under which reward hacking amplifies, persists, or decays across agent interactions. Beyond propagation, reward hacking can bias task routing toward reward-hacking agents and survive candidate aggregation. As potential mitigations, we evaluate code review by the coder or a separate verifier, both of which reduce delivered hacks. Together, these results establish reward hacking as a transmissible strategy whose effects extend beyond the agent in which it first emerges.

title: Calibration-Aware Patient-Level Prediction of Source-Defined MSIMUT Status in Colorectal Cancer from Whole-Slide Histopathology Images Using Foundation-Model Embeddings
abstract: Background/Objectives: Microsatellite instability (MSI) is clinically important in colorectal cancer, but definitive assessment requires molecular or immunohistochemical testing. This study developed a leakage-safe, calibration-aware patient-level framework for predicting a source-defined MSIMUT category from hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide-derived patches using fixed Phikon foundation-model embeddings. Methods: The TCGA-derived colorectal cohort comprised 360 patients, including 65 source-defined positive and 295 MSS cases, represented by 192,312 pre-extracted patches. Patch embeddings were aggregated using mean, max, and mean-plus-max pooling, and downstream classifiers were evaluated under patient-level cross-validation with calibration, threshold, decision-curve, clinicopathological, source-provenance, and patch-count sensitivity analyses. Results: In the primary random patient-level evaluation, logistic regression with mean-plus-max pooling achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.915 and PR-AUC of 0.809. Fully nested Platt calibration yielded pooled out-of-sample ROC-AUC 0.913, PR-AUC 0.796, Brier score 0.073, calibration slope 1.037, and calibration-in-the-large 0.023. Within the internally cross-validated mean-plus-max framework, an exploratory sensitivity ≥ 0.95 operating point yielded sensitivity 0.969, specificity 0.393, and negative predictive value 0.983. Provenance reconstruction identified source-partition-dependent patch-count structure. In a source-TRAIN to source-TEST holdout, mean-plus-max ROC-AUC decreased to 0.788, while patch count alone was near chance in source-TEST (ROC-AUC 0.517) and explicit patch-count addition did not improve discrimination. Conclusions: These findings support the methodological feasibility of fixed foundation-model embeddings for internal MSI-related pre-screening research, while showing that apparent performance is sensitive to source structure. Independent multicenter validation with clinically adjudicated MSI-H/dMMR endpoints remains necessary before clinical application.

title: MЕТОД АВТОМАТИЧЕСКОГО РАЗРЕШЕНИЯ ОМОГРАФИИ НА ОСНОВЕ ЕВКЛИДОВОЙ МЕТРИКИ WEN
abstract: В статье проведен обзор классических методов разрешения лексической многозначности, использующих векторное представление слов и евклидово расстояние. Представлен новый метод WSD – метод автоматического разрешения омографии на основе евклидовой метрики. Приведено описание работы метода WEN на примере распознавания омографа «замок» в предложении, показан процесс «оцифровки» слов и предложений из баз, вычисление расстояний от тестового предложения до баз предложений с различными значениями омографа. Представлены данные об экспериментальном исследовании метода WEN на базах предложений с омографами для малоресурсного чеченского языка. Проведено сравнение полученных метрик точности с аналогичными методами для различных языков.

title: BLAD: Test Dataset for Bilingual Acronym Disambiguation for Dutch and English Domain-Specific Text
abstract: We have curated a dataset of multi-sense acronym usage within the documentation of an established power company, given a list of acronyms known to be actively in use. Dataset contains 176 unique sentences for 126 multi-sense acronyms. Some acronym senses could not be found in the documents, for these we do not have an example sentence. The senses vary between two and five per acronym. As such, the internal disambiguation is a multi-class problem with a median of two classes (expansions) per acronym. Of the examples, 26 are in English, while the rest are in Dutch. Every expansion is annotated with a language tag (en/nl). Each expansion term is also annotated according to its domain specificity as "global" (has a dedicated Wikipedia page), "domain-specific" (acronym and expansion occur together at least more than once in Web search results) and "company" (used only within the company) \textit{(see Table 1 for distribution)}. The "domain-specific" category does not refer to a specific domain here - the examples vary across domains such as energy/electricity and information technology/business intelligence.

title: AI in the Next Five Years: Navigating Strategic Uncertainty
abstract: AI fundamentally transforms decision-making, organizational structures, competitive dynamics, and leadership imperatives. AI has become an essential force reshaping business and society, bringing unprecedented opportunities and significant risks. Strategic clarity in the age of AI will not emerge from eliminating uncertainty but rather from becoming adept at navigating it. The C-suite must embrace strategic agility, preparedness, and continual learning as corner stones of leadership that will win the future. The generative AI boom triggered by ChatGPT's launch in late 2022 has produced genuine capability and inflated expectations in equal measure. For executives seeking competitive advantage, neither the technoutopian nor the defensive doomer position serves. Most AI forecasts focus on what will be destroyed: jobs eliminated, industries disrupted, companies made obsolete.

title: Thinking with Images without Coordinates
abstract: Recent advances in multi-modal large language models have shifted toward the "thinking with images" paradigm to improve reasoning faithfulness, yet existing methods rely heavily on explicit coordinate- based grounding. We identify two fundamental limitations in this approach, i.e., a semantic gap where sparse regressions miss high-dimensional latent structures, and a resolution gap due to the granularity mismatch between patch-level tokens and pixel-level coordinates. To address these, we propose TiCO (Thinking with images without COordinates). It reformulates visual reasoning as a semantic evidence discovery process within the latent space, and evidence is injected as token-level regions without pixel coordinates. Specifically, TiCO utilizes a dedicated probe token to estimate similarity distributions and performs importance sampling over spatially connected components to generate diverse, semantically dominant evidence rollouts. Extensive experiments across multiple high-resolution and general visual reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that our TiCO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art coordinate-based methods with significantly improved inference efficiency.

title: Knowing Whether, Not Just Where: Anchor-Probing Distillation for Open-Set Remote Sensing Visual Grounding
abstract: Open-set visual grounding in remote sensing requires models to determine not only where a queried object is located, but also whether the image provides sufficient evidence for the query at all. Existing closed-set grounding models, however, tend to return plausible boxes even for absent objects, blurring localization confidence with genuine Visual Support. We introduce AnchorProbe-Distill (APD), a teacher-student framework that recasts open-set grounding as Visual Support learning. APD builds on the insight that supported queries should induce coherent spatial anchors, whereas unsupported or mismatched queries tend to produce unstable or misleading localization patterns. APD-T therefore uses the Original Query as a Reference Anchor to interpret query perturbations: Semantic-Preserving Queries retain the annotated target, Near-Category Ambiguous Queries are resolved according to whether they form a reliable alternative anchor or collapse onto the Reference Anchor, and Far-Category Counterfactual Queries provide rejection supervision. This reference-aware reasoning is distilled into APD-S, enabling unified localization and rejection from a single image--query pair. Experiments show that APD enables the resulting model to reject absent targets while also improving its localization of present targets.

APD builds on the insight that supported queries should induce coherent spatial anchors, whereas unsupported or mismatched queries tend to produce unstable or misleading localization patterns. APD-T therefore uses the Original Query as a Reference Anchor to interpret query perturbations: Semantic-Preserving Queries retain the annotated target, Near-Category Ambiguous Queries are resolved according to whether they form a reliable alternative anchor or collapse onto the Reference Anchor, and Far-Category Counterfactual Queries provide rejection supervision. This reference-aware reasoning is distilled into APD-S, enabling unified localization and rejection from a single image--query pair. Experiments show that APD enables the resulting model to reject absent targets while also improving its localization of present targets.

title: Modelling Josephson Junctions with Boundary Conditions: Towards High-Fidelity Models for Superconducting Qubits
abstract: Josephson junctions are the central nonlinear element of superconducting qubits, yet their standard description is reached through a chain of approximations. We propose a purely quantum-mechanical model of the junction, formulated directly in Hilbert space: a charged particle moves on a one-dimensional loop, and the junction is a point at which the wave function obeys self-adjoint boundary conditions, labelled by a coupling strength $λ$, which controls the transparency of the junction, and a phase jump $δ$, which plays the role of the superconducting phase difference. For a loop with a single junction we solve the spectral problem and show that the ground-state momentum expectation, identified with the supercurrent, factorises exactly as $\langle\hat{p}_0\rangle = I_c(δ,λ)\sinδ$. For opaque junctions $I_c$ becomes independent of $δ$ and the first Josephson relation $I=I_c\sinδ$ is recovered; for strongly attractive coupling, where the ground state is bound to the junction, the $\sinδ$ law is also recovered, but with an exponentially suppressed amplitude. For more transparent junctions, however, the model \emph{predicts} deviations from the pure $\sinδ$ law: $I_c$ acquires a dependence on $δ$ already at order $λ^{-2}$, compatible with the higher Josephson harmonics recently found necessary to describe superconducting qubit spectra, and a fully transparent contact yields a current linear in $δ$. When the phase varies in time, a gauge transformation shows that the voltage drop across the junction is proportional to $\dotδ$, so that the second Josephson relation emerges without being imposed. The boundary-condition approach thus reproduces both Josephson relations from first principles and predicts corrections to them, offering a route towards higher-fidelity models of superconducting qubits.

title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy
abstract: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.

title: Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence
abstract: Memory-augmented assistants retrieve evidence from stored conversations and documents to answer queries. Most embedding-based retrievers compare single-vector representations of queries and memories, even when relevance depends on a small part of the content. Such local evidence can be matched to queries using the contextual token representations already computed by the same embedding models. Our method uses sparse token matching to improve retrieval without additional training. Each query token retrieves a small set of matching tokens across candidate memories. The matching scores are aggregated for each memory and combined with whole-memory similarity to rank memories. An optional low-rank query adapter can be trained with supervision while keeping the encoder and stored memory representations fixed. Our method improves retrieval across eight benchmarks and multiple model families without additional training. Query adaptation further increases the gains to 13.3 and 14.3 percentage points in average Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on Qwen3-Embedding-4B. These retrieval gains translate into higher question-answering accuracy on long-term memory benchmarks.

title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
abstract: Recurrent-depth language models improve inference-time reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared network to refine internal representations, but the additional recurrent computation also increases inference cost. This overhead is particularly pronounced during long-context prefill, where the full input sequence is repeatedly processed across recurrent depth. Weight-and-activation quantization offers a natural way to accelerate this computation through lower-precision arithmetic, yet repeatedly applying quantized computation introduces numerical perturbations that accumulate along the recurrent trajectory. We systematically analyze how such errors propagate across recurrent depth and show that quantization errors introduced earlier are attenuated by more subsequent recurrent steps and therefore have a smaller effect on the final representation. Matched-budget experiments strongly support this prediction, showing that placing quantized computation earlier in recurrent depth consistently yields the best fidelity. Based on this insight, we introduce RAMP (Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision), which performs early recurrent refinement using low-precision weight-and-activation computation and restores high precision for terminal refinement. Across context lengths up to 4K, RAMP preserves near-full-precision prefill quality while achieving up to 1.16x end-to-end first-prefill speedup on an NVIDIA H100, corresponding to a 13.9% latency reduction.

title: Inverse Synthesis of Shock Time Series from Shock Response Spectra Using Ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders
abstract: The shock response spectrum (SRS) characterizes the peak responses of single-degree-of-freedom systems to transient acceleration. Because the mapping from an acceleration time series (waveform) to its SRS is many-to-one, inverse synthesis seeks candidate waveforms consistent with a prescribed spectrum. We extend an earlier conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) framework with a recurrent decoder that predicts multiscale wavelet coefficients and reconstructs waveforms through an inverse discrete wavelet transform. Individual models exhibit limited variability under latent sampling, motivating an ensemble of independently trained models spanning different mother wavelets and decomposition levels. Each member produces a separate candidate waveform for the same target SRS. Evaluation on four held-out benchmark datasets shows lower mean and median spectral errors for the illustrated wavelet model than for the earlier direct time-domain CVAE and a sum-of-decayed-sinusoids (SDS) baseline. A conditioning study examines frequency-grid and encoding choices. Comparisons with published inverse-SRS methods demonstrate superior performance across four holdout benchmark datasets (two operational shock datasets, one earthquake dataset, and one synthetic shock dataset) and competitive performance on synthetic targets reported by Brake. Single-model inference requires approximately 0.1-0.6 ms per waveform during batched inference compared with 5-8 s for SDS, excluding offline training. This low inference cost enables rapid generation of distinct SRS-compatible candidate waveforms across the ensemble, although their physical suitability requires assessment beyond spectral agreement.

title: Continuous-time evolution via probabilistic angle interpolation and its applications
abstract: We explore the applicability of a stochastic time-evolution algorithm based on probabilistic angle interpolation. To simplify the pre-processing of the algorithm, we take the continuous-time limit, thereby explicitly eliminating Trotter errors and streamlining the resource analysis. We also introduce a noise-mitigation method tailored to it. As demonstrations, we apply the algorithm to two representative problems: estimating the ground-state energy of the $H_3^+$ molecular Hamiltonian and computing out-of-time-ordered correlators in the sparse Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model. We evaluate the protocol's performance through numerical simulations and experiments on a trapped-ion quantum computer, Quantinuum Reimei.

title: Mapping the Intersection of Neuromarketing and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into neuromarketing has significantly transformed how consumer behavior is analyzed, interpreted, and influenced. By combining neuroscientific methods with advanced computational techniques, neuromarketing allows for the exploration of subconscious cognitive and emotional processes that traditional market research methods often fail to capture. Despite this growing body of research, the literature remains fragmented and conceptually dispersed, limiting a structured understanding of its intellectual foundations, thematic evolution, and future research directions. The results reveal a strong growth trajectory in neuromarketing research with AI, reflecting the increasing academic and managerial interest in data-driven and neuro-informed decision-making. It provides a conceptual basis for future research and assists researchers and practitioners in understanding the opportunities and challenges associated with the responsible and effective use of artificial intelligence in neuromarketing contexts

title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing From Predictive Analytics to Generative Creativity
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the foundations of modern marketing, shifting from data-driven decision-making toward an era of intelligent creativity that fuses predictive analytics with generative innovation. This chapter conceptually examines how the integration of predictive and generative AI—through the Integrated Predictive–Generative Framework (IPGF)—redefines marketing intelligence by merging analytical precision with creative synthesis. Through theoretical analysis and case-based interpretation, the chapter explores predictive AI in forecasting consumer behavior and generative AI in producing personalized, emotionally resonant content. It also identifies ethical, psychological, and social implications associated with AI-driven creativity, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and human oversight as essential principles for sustainable, human-centered marketing ecosystems.

title: Impacto de datos sintéticos generados mediante CTGAN en modelos de aprendizaje automático para la predicción
abstract: The objective of this study was to evaluate comparatively the predictive performance and explainability of Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost trained on real data versus real data augmented with CTGAN. This research is computational/experimental in nature, focusing on predictive models, with a quantitative approach, a comparative purpose, and an applied orientation. The results revealed findings contrary to what is reported in most of the literature reviewed: adding synthetic data to the training did not improve the predictive performance of any of the three models but rather reduced it in a statistically significant manner, even when that same synthetic data passed statistical fidelity validation compared to the real data. In conclusion, at the theoretical level, the study provides a concrete example of the relationship between statistical fidelity and the predictive utility of synthetic data an aspect that remains largely unexplored in the reviewed literature.

title: MaLeFiz - Maschinelles Lernen zur effizienten Identifikation auffälliger Finanztransaktionen; Teilvorhaben "Technikentwicklung"
abstract: Im Rahmen des Projekts MaLeFiz wurden im Teilvorhaben "Technikentwicklung" Methoden des maschinellen Lernens zur Identifikation auffälliger Finanztransaktionen (Geldwäscheerkennung) entwickelt und evaluiert. Nach anfänglicher Literaturrecherche und Grundlagenschaffung musste aufgrund des Ausbleibens einer Datenspende durch eine Bank auf synthetische Daten zurückgegriffen werden. Hierzu wurde ein Transaktionsgenerator kalibriert und fertiggestellt, der realitätsnahe Finanztransaktionsdaten erzeugt. Es wurden fünf Kategorien von Realisierungskonzepten entwickelt, darunter Basisalgorithmen, graphbasierte Verfahren, Ensemble-Methoden und Outlier Detection, und hinsichtlich Performanz sowie Nachvollziehbarkeit (u.a. mittels Shapley Values und LLMs) evaluiert. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass klassische Methoden oft vergleichbare oder bessere Resultate liefern als komplexere Deep-Learning-Ansätze und zugleich besser interpretierbar sind. Ein zentrales Projektergebnis ist ein interaktiver Online-Demonstrator, der die technischen, juristischen und sozialwissenschaftlichen Ergebnisse des Gesamtprojekts zusammenführt. Das Projekt zeigt, dass es kein universell bestes Modell gibt, sondern ein Set anpassbarer, nachvollziehbarer KI-Werkzeuge für unterschiedliche Anwendungsfälle im Transaktionsmonitoring.

title: АВТОМАТИЗАЦИЯ ВЫЯВЛЕНИЯ ДУБЛИКАТОВ РАЦИОНАЛИЗАТОРСКИХ ПРЕДЛОЖЕНИЙ ЗА СЧЕТ АНАЛИЗА ТЕКСТОВОЙ СХОЖЕСТИ
abstract: Рассматривается задача поиска семантически схожих и дублирующих рационализаторских предложений в исполняемом бизнес-процессе «Управление рационализаторской деятель-ностью». Для оценки смысловой близости исследовались модели преобразования текста в числовые представления (embedding-модели). Эффективность моделей оценивалась на основе степени сходства текстов и результатов экспертной оценки. Для повышения точности поиска дубликатов выполнена оптимизация весов объектов предложений с помощью эволюционного алгоритма. На основе метрик бенчмарка ruMTEB и экспертной оценки выявлена наиболее эффективная модель.

title: Incoherent-light nonlinear optical computing via data reverberation in a liquid-crystal cavity
abstract: Artificial neural networks are powerful but increasingly constrained by energy use and hardware cost. Optical computing offers speed and efficiency, yet achieving practical optical nonlinearity typically requires high-power lasers or specialized materials. Here we demonstrate a low-power optical extreme learner driven by incoherent light that generates nonlinear input-output behavior through data reverberation in a liquid-crystal cavity. With a simple trained readout, the system performs accurately on image classification and XOR, matching fully nonlinear digital models while remaining compact and energy efficient.
